entries.title: 1641 Depositions (Trinity College Dublin)
entries.institution: Trinity College Dublin, with the Universities of Aberdeen and Cambridge (funded by the Irish Research Council and the AHRC)
entries.notes: Transcripts, with page images, of the witness statements (depositions and examinations) collected after the Irish rising of October 1641, bound in 32 volumes (TCD MSS 809-840) and kept in Trinity College Library. Every transcript is readable online without login. The project page says the transcribing and online publication ran from 2007 to September 2010 and that the site presents about 8,000 depositions, examinations and associated materials. All the depositions are dated 1641-1653, within 1450-1700. The site's content pages were last changed on 2020-10-16 (WordPress page records), so it is marked archived. Only a TEI-compliant encoding is mentioned on the project pages; no download of the files was found. The counts rest on the site's own listing of 6,932 deposition records, and the texts themselves could not be read: the site answers automated requests with a reCAPTCHA challenge.
entries.license_note: FAQ (archived copy; live site is behind a CAPTCHA): "The copyright for the transcriptions belongs to the 1641 Depositions Project/the Library of TCD and the transcriptions may not be published without permission"; image copyright belongs to the Board of the Library of TCD and images cannot be downloaded.

entries.title: ABaC:us — Austrian Baroque Corpus
entries.institution: Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW), Austrian Centre for Digital Humanities and Cultural Heritage (ACDH-CH)
entries.notes: Digital corpus of German baroque literary texts (c. 1650-1750), focused on devotional literature around death preparation (Ars moriendi, Totentanz, Memento mori) connected with Abraham a Sancta Clara (1644-1709), e.g. Mercks Wienn (1680), Grosse Todten Bruderschaft (1681). First-edition principle, XML-TEI P5 with linguistic annotation (tokenisation, PoS tagging, lemmatisation) and person/place indices. Project directed by Claudia Resch and Ulrike Czeitschner; online since 2015, new infrastructure launched 2025. Project archive page: https://www.oeaw.ac.at/acdh/research/literary-studies/research/project-archive/abacus. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: Includes CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Licences or rights differ by text, corpus or editorial layer; consult the source terms for the selected material.

entries.title: ABU — Bibliothèque Universelle
entries.institution: Association des Bibliophiles Universels (ABU); hosted by the CEDRIC team (Multimédia et Interaction Homme-Machine) at the Conservatoire national des arts et métiers
entries.notes: Free-access collection of French-language public-domain texts, in the catalogue's early-modern part including works such as the Lettres de la religieuse portugaise, Argens's Lettres juives and Corneille's plays. It is produced and distributed by volunteer members of the Association des Bibliophiles Universels (ABU, a 1901-law association founded in April 1993) and hosted by the CEDRIC multimedia and human-computer interaction team at the Conservatoire national des arts et metiers, Paris. The texts are plain HTML pages for reading online; the catalogue lists 288 texts by 101 authors (January 2002), and the site has had no visible additions since then. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: The ABU licence (v1.1, August 1999) covers the compilation: copying for private use, teaching or research is allowed; redistribution must carry the licence, the file header and producer credits and flag modifications.

entries.title: ADL Danish
entries.notes: Texts of the Archive for Danish Literature (ADL), a collaboration between the Det Danske Sprog- og Litteraturselskab (DSL) and the Royal Danish Library (KB), published in the public GitHub repository kb-dk/public-adl-text-sources. The corpus comprises 498 volumes (165,512 pages) of Danish literature, all encoded in TEI; the repository contains the roughly two-thirds of pages that have been OCR'd and encoded, one TEI-XML file per volume under texts/. The repository also documents the encoding practices, offers XSLT scripts to extract single works, and accepts contributions by pull request; it was last pushed to in August 2026. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Alciato's Book of Emblems: The Memorial Web Edition in Latin and English
entries.author: Andrea Alciato
entries.institution: Memorial University of Newfoundland (William Barker, Mark Feltham, Jean Guthrie)
entries.region: Italy and Germany (first printed in Augsburg, 1531)
entries.notes: Web edition of the 212 emblems of Alciato's Emblematum liber, with the Latin text taken from the 1621 variorum edition and checked against the 1531, 1534 and 1546 editions, an English translation, commentary files and images. The original address (www.mun.ca/alciato) now returns 404, so the URL is the Internet Archive copy of 3 October 2022; the site was last updated in April 2005. The site also carries images of Whitney's Choice of Emblemes (1586) and a 17th-century jest book. The counts cover the Latin text file only, not the English text, the commentaries or those two other works. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: No licence or copyright statement on the archived home page (capture of 2022-10-03), the project description page or the footer; no data repository. Checked 2026-10-13 via the Wayback Machine (live site not re-tested).

entries.title: ALDICAM-CM — Atlas lingüístico diacrónico e interactivo de la Comunidad de Madrid
entries.institution: GITHE, Universidad de Alcalá (project S2015/HUM-3443, Comunidad de Madrid / FSE)
entries.notes: Transcribed archival documents from the 13th to the 19th century from archives of the Comunidad de Madrid (Archivo Regional, Archivo de la Villa, municipal, ecclesiastical and private archives), with paleographic and critical presentation and facsimiles, searchable and mappable without login. Same search engine as CODEA+ 2022; about a third of the regestos coincide with CODEA+ 2022 documents. No bulk download found. About a third of its document summaries coincide with CODEA+ 2022. Twelve documents without a date and three without paleographic text are not in the counts. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: No licence or terms on the ALDICAM-CM query page, its help/info tabs or the project blog. The sister corpus CODEA+ 2022 on corpuscodea.es has "Condiciones de uso" allowing free consultation and use for teaching and research but forbidding commercial use; this is not stated for ALDICAM itself (checked 2026-10-13).

entries.title: Amadis in Translation (Digital Amadis)
entries.institution: University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg (Stacey Triplette, Elisa Beshero-Bondar) and Universidade de Santiago de Compostela (Helena Bermúdez Sabel)
entries.notes: Digital study of the transformation of Montalvo's Amadís de Gaula across editions and translations (Spanish, French, English, from the 1500s to the early 1800s). The corpus files are the 35 TEI XML chapters of the 1547 Sevilla printing of Montalvo's Amadís (facsimile source: Biblioteca Virtual de Andalucía), used to align Garci Rodríguez de Montalvo's text with Robert Southey's 1803 translation and study translation shifts. Project team: Stacey Triplette, Elisa Beshero-Bondar, Helena Bermúdez Sabel; maintained by Beshero-Bondar since 2015. Code and TEI data are on GitHub (AGPL-3.0), with an archived release on Zenodo. Project documentation and a 1533 frontispiece facsimile on the project site. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Acta Pacis Westphalicae digital (APW digital)
entries.institution: Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn and Bayerische Staatsbibliothek (Bavarian State Library), Munich
entries.notes: Digital edition of the Acta Pacis Westphalicae, the documents of the Westphalian peace congress (instructions, correspondence, minutes, negotiation papers and diaries; the congress ran 1643-1649, with a few earlier or later items). All volumes of the three series are readable online with a document-by-document view, scans of the printed pages, PDF download of the printed volumes and the TEI XML full text of each document (served as TEI fragments, without a teiHeader). No login is needed. The edition text is a digitised critical edition of the archival originals (about 157 archives). The counts cover 3,210 of the 14,545 listed documents (22%), from 19 of the 41 volumes; the server was unstable during the harvest. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: Page "APW digital" (live version reached only through search because the site sits behind an Anubis bot wall): "Die xml-Dateien auf APW digital stehen unter der Lizenz CC BY-SA 4.0"; credit the Zentrum fuer Historische Friedensforschung, Bonn. The edition is published with permission of the Aschendorff publishing house; the licence is stated for the XML files.

entries.title: Briefe und Akten zur Kirchenpolitik Friedrichs des Weisen und Johanns des Beständigen 1513 bis 1532
entries.author: Frederick the Wise and John the Steadfast, Electors of Saxony, and correspondents
entries.institution: Sächsische Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Leipzig (Manfred Rudersdorf, Armin Kohnle and team)
entries.notes: Academy edition of the church-policy correspondence and records of the two electors. The online database lists 3,385 documents; for 1,760 of them (dated 1493 to December 1522) editing is marked complete. Of these, those with an edited source text show it beside the German summary; the others currently show a summary and metadata only, and the rest of the database is metadata. The printed volumes (three so far, the latest in December 2025) are not online here. Twelve further documents appear with full transcriptions and images under 'Kabinettstücke'. News on the site is dated October 2026. The counts cover the 302 documents with an edited source text found on the document pages, and will grow as texts are added. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Balassi Bálint összes verse: hálózati kritikai kiadás (network critical edition of the complete poems)
entries.author: Bálint Balassi
entries.institution: Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest (edited by Iván Horváth and Tünde Tóth; published by Gépeskönyv)
entries.notes: Critical edition of Balassi's poems, first published online in 1998 (version 1.0), revised as 1.1 (1999) and 2.0 (2002), with facsimiles, apparatus, notes and a repertory. The site is a set of HTML frames. Newest file seen was modified in 2006. The poems carry no individual dates, so their place within 1450-1700 rests on the author's life span (he died in 1594). entries.title: Balkan Slavic Digital Editions (Pop Punčov Sbornik, Life of St. Petka, Tale of Alexander, Excerpts)
entries.institution: University of Zurich, Institute of Slavic Studies (SNSF project 176378, Barbara Sonnenhauser) and Czech Academy of Sciences; hosted at LMU Munich (Ivan Šimko, Anastasia Escher)
entries.notes: Corpus of Balkan Slavic texts from the 10th to the 19th century collected for the study of linguistic change: Pop Punčo's Sbornik (1796), the Life of St. Petka in many copies, the Tale of Alexander the Elder, and an Excerpts sub-corpus. Texts come with English translations, morphological and syntactic annotation, search and facsimiles. Sources within 1450-1700 include Vuković's Zbornik za putnike (printed 1536), the Joseph-Volokolamsk manuscript of 1537, the Tikhonravov damaskin and other 17th-century damaskini, Šimun Kozičić (1530s), and Letters of Wallachian princes. Texts are read in the web interface. The search engine loads its corpus from public token-level JSON files with diplomatic form, lemma, MULTEXT-East tags and Universal Dependencies relations (lt_data.json for the Excerpts texts, petka_data.json for the Life of St. Petka, sva_data.json for the Tale of Alexander, data_1.json and data_2.json for Pop Punčo's Sbornik of 1796). These files are not advertised as downloads. Search results can be exported as CSV or CoNLL-U. The 23 Damaskini texts are also deposited at CLARIN.SI (11356/1441). Status active: the home page was modified in July 2026 and the Excerpts page in February 2026. The counts cover the 13 texts dated within 1450-1700, leaving out the Sbornik (1796), and several dates are approximate (century midpoints or decades). Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Annotated Corpus of Pre-Standardized Balkan Slavic Literature 1.1
entries.notes: The 23-text Damaskini subcorpus (16th-19th c. Balkan Slavic, Bulgarian/Macedonian/Torlak, ~53k tokens) is exactly the resource published at CLARIN.SI handle 11356/1441 (v1.1, 2021) by the SNSF-funded ZuCoSlaV project of Ivan Simko (University of Zurich, Slavic Seminary). Formats are TSV/CoNLL-U/plain text (not TEI). License: CC BY-SA 4.0. entries.title: Klasikoen Gordailua (Euskal Klasikoen Corpusa, UPV/EHU)
entries.notes: Klasikoen Gordailua (Repository of Classics), run by armiarma.eus since 2005, which aims to gather nearly all classic Basque texts up to the twentieth century; its search tool, the Corpus Arakatzailea, dates from 2007. The Basque Classics Corpus (Euskal Klasikoen Corpusa) of the UPV/EHU Institute of the Basque Language republishes this material (published there on 2013-12-05; author Joseba Ezeiza): 496 books from the 16th century to 1975, searchable by author, period, dialect and genre. The whole corpus can be downloaded as a single file in TEI or RTF. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.author: Pierre Bayle
entries.institution: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne, IHRIM (directed by Antony McKenna and Fabienne Vial-Bonacci)
entries.notes: Critical edition of the letters sent and received by Pierre Bayle (1647-1706), with transcriptions, annotations, indexes and translations of Latin letters. The site publishes letters 1-1405 (volumes I-XI of the printed edition, 1662-1698); volumes XII-XIV (letters up to 1791 and 1706) are not online. The site mentions TEI/XML output but no files are public. The site was updated in 2025. entries.notes: Digitised edition of Ludovico Bertonio's Vocabulario de la Lengua Aymara (Juli, 1612), distributed as a StarDict dictionary in the native-dics repository of Amos Batto. entries.title: Bess of Hardwick's Letters: The Complete Correspondence, c. 1550-1608
entries.author: Elizabeth Talbot, Countess of Shrewsbury (Bess of Hardwick), and correspondents
entries.institution: University of Glasgow (Alison Wiggins, ed.), with technical development by the Digital Humanities Institute, Sheffield
entries.notes: Complete correspondence of Bess of Hardwick (c. 1521/7-1608): 234 letters to and from her, each with diplomatic and normalised transcripts, colour images of 185 of them, and commentary. All letters fall within 1550-1608 (1550s: 7; 1560s: 31; 1570s: 74; 1580s: 52; 1590s: 18; 1600s: 52). The letters are served as XML (a project-specific format, not TEI), and the whole set, with a metadata database, can be downloaded from the Digital Humanities Institute data service. Version 1.0 was released in September 2013 and the data was deposited on 13 July 2021; no later change is visible, so the status is archived. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: BetaMasaheft Geez
entries.notes: TEI-XML records of Ethiopian and Eritrean literary works (Ge'ez and other languages of the Christian written tradition) kept in the BetaMasaheft/Works GitHub repository, the data layer of the Beta masahaft project 'Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea'. The records are served through the project's eXist-db application at betamasaheft.eu, which links works to manuscripts, persons and places and is built on a Clavis Aethiopica numbering of works. The project is a long-term programme of the Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg (2016-2040), directed by Alessandro Bausi and hosted by the Hiob Ludolf Centre for Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies, University of Hamburg; it follows an ERC project led by Denis Nosnitsin (2009-2015). The repository is under active development (last push October 2026). Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: Beta masahaft project, Hiob Ludolf Centre for Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies, Universitaet Hamburg / Akademie der Wissenschaften in Hamburg (director Alessandro Bausi)
entries.license_note: The project site says all its data are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, but the TEI headers of the Works files state CC BY-SA 4.0 ("This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0"); the repository has no LICENSE file. Discrepancy to be noted; the site value is kept.

entries.title: Biblioteca Italiana
entries.notes: Digital library of texts of Italian literary and cultural tradition from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, promoted since 1996 by the Centro Interuniversitario Biblioteca Italiana Telematica (CIBIT) and run from the Department of Italianistica e Spettacolo at Sapienza University of Rome; the BIBIT section was started under Amedeo Quondam in 2003. BIBIT holds more than 1,600 works in full-text editions based on scholarly reference editions, encoded in XML/TEI (the TEI header records each text's history), which can be read, searched with concordances and downloaded; the site also holds scanned incunabula and the Scrittori d'Italia series as images. The portal's content pages were last edited in 2019. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Controversia Confessio
entries.notes: Source edition on the formation of confessions and confessionalisation (1548-1580), documenting the theological disputes after the Augsburg Interim of 1548 and the Leipzig Interim, in nine planned thematic volumes. The project's database records more than 2000 printed controversial writings of 1548-1577/80 (full titles, authorship, printers, dates, present library locations, title-page scans and often summaries) and about 240 short biographies of the theologians and politicians involved; digital versions of the printed edition volumes are being produced in cooperation with the Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbuettel and the University and State Library Darmstadt. The project has run since 2007 as a long-term project of the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz, with the Leibniz-Institut fuer Europaeische Geschichte and Johannes Gutenberg-Universitaet Mainz, and ended with the conference volume C&C 12 published in 2025. The search interface is open without login and full documents are available as per-document PDF files (with a metadata sheet on page 1); the search interface shows concordances and example passages as HTML; there is no bulk download and no TEI. Documents are transcriptions with expanded abbreviations. The countries listed are a selection of the 20+ countries covered. The counts cover the 7,334 documents with a year between 1494 and 1700, and documents dated only by century are not included. entries.title: Corpus Corporum
entries.institution: Universität Zürich
entries.notes: Repository of Latin texts (with some Greek) from antiquity to the early modern period, run by the Institute for Greek and Latin Philology of the University of Zurich, directed by Philipp Roelli. It holds the Patrologia Latina, the Vulgate and many other corpora, stored as standardised TEI-XML and searchable by full text, Boolean, proximity and lemma (Latin), with period limits (about 83 percent of texts carry a date tag), dictionaries, a synoptic Bible view and metrical analysis; texts can be downloaded for non-commercial use. The present interface was rebuilt around 2019 and the site is still maintained. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

Tunberg. The texts are TEI-XML, openly downloadable from a GitHub repository (with Zenodo DOI) and searchable through PhiloLogic4 and a BaseX database; the online edition is dated 2024 and the repository was last updated in April 2026. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: A Social Edition of the Devonshire MS (BL Add. MS 17492)
entries.institution: University of Victoria (editorial team led by Ray Siemens); print edition by Iter & ACMRS Press
entries.notes:
A digital edition of a mid-sixteenth-century miscellany of verse and prose, compiled in the court circle of Margaret Douglas and later the Rutland household, with contributions by Thomas Wyatt, Mary Shelton and others. Diplomatic transcription, modernised text and scholarly apparatus, encoded in TEI P5. The original dedicated site (devonshire.unb.ca) is offline; the social edition now lives on Wikibooks, and the ~200 TEI XML transcriptions and witnesses (CC BY-SA 4.0) are archived at Oxford LLDS: https://llds.phon.ox.ac.uk/llds/xmlui/handle/20.500.14106/2587

The counts cover the 186 poem and item files of the manuscript, not the 288 witness files. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

Each ballad is offered as a sheet facsimile, a facsimile transcription (preserving the original layout), a plain text transcription and, where available, a recording of the tune, with detailed catalogue headings. A TEI-XML file with the transcription and metadata can be downloaded from the transcription view of each ballad. The project began in 2003 under director Patricia Fumerton at the University of California, Santa Barbara (associate director Carl Stahmer), and has received repeated National Endowment for the Humanities grants (NEH 1 to NEH 8, the latest for 2020-22). entries.title: Bibliothèques Virtuelles Humanistes — Épistémon
entries.institution: Centre d'études supérieures de la Renaissance (CESR), Université de Tours / CNRS (Bibliothèques Virtuelles Humanistes)
entries.notes: Epistemon is the text database of the Bibliothèques Virtuelles Humanistes (BVH) programme at the Centre d'Études Supérieures de la Renaissance, Université de Tours (head: Rémi Jimenes). It offers Renaissance texts (literature and author corpora, literary manuscripts and 16th-century archival documents) transcribed in a 'patrimonial' manner that respects layout, spelling and punctuation, encoded in XML-TEI following the project's TEI-Renaissance guidelines. The first texts went online in 1998 at the University of Poitiers and moved to Tours in 2001; TEI encoding has been used since 2007. Texts are read and searched through XTF, PhiloLogic and TXM, with facsimiles shown alongside where available. Fidelity levels of older transcriptions are heterogeneous, and the base is still being extended and revised. It includes the Montaigne author corpus of the ANR MONLOE project (montaigne.univ-tours.fr): the genetic edition of the Exemplaire de Bordeaux of the 1588 Essais (also deposited on HAL, halshs-01239978), the 1580 edition of the Essais (books I and II), Montaigne's 1581 translation of Sebond's Théologie naturelle, La Boétie's Servitude volontaire (Bordeaux Ms 2199), letters and family archives; MONLOE's editions of Montaigne's marginalia and inscriptions are PDFs on the BVH server and are not counted. The counts combine two harvests that share no text: 70 texts from the BVH site and 46 printed texts from a legacy TEI copy in Lou Burnard's tei-fr repository on GitHub (last updated 2015). Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: The Epistemon editorial principles and the BVH legal notice (mentions.asp) place the texts under 'Creative Commons Attribution - NonCommercial - ShareAlike 4.0 International'. Library-owned originals and images remain under the holding institutions' rights; the site footer still links an older CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 FR badge.

entries.title: Ganjoor (گنجور) — Persian poetry library
entries.notes: Ganjoor is a Persian poetry website and database of classical Persian poets and their poems; the Renascor record covers the part of the content dated 1466-1700. It was started by an individual hobbyist and moved to ganjoor.net in 2007/8; it is not tied to any institution or commercial body. Poems are typed by volunteers mostly from free sources, with sources listed on the Sources page. The data is exported periodically as a database and, as of 2026-10-13, as a public git-tracked JSON repository (about 240 poets and 135,000 poems) on GitHub. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: The Nottingham Corpus of Early Modern German Midwifery and Women's Medicine, ca. 1500–1700 (GeMi, OTA 2562)

entries.title: GerManC - Historical Corpus of German 1650-1800 (OTA 2544)
entries.notes: GerManC is a manually annotated, genre-balanced corpus of Early Modern German (1650-1800), built at the University of Manchester and distributed through the Oxford Text Archive (record ota:2544) under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The former project site no longer responds, and the Oxford Text Archive pages sit behind an anti-bot check, so they may need a browser. entries.title: Glasgow University Emblem Website (Alciato and French Emblems projects)

It is run by the University of Glasgow (Special Collections and the Stirling Maxwell Centre; contacts Laurence Grove, Luis Gomes, Alison Adams) with partners including Emblematica Online, the Universidade da Coruna and the Herzog August Bibliothek. The site is still online as HTML pages. entries.title: The Hartlib Papers (Samuel Hartlib, c. 1600-1662)
entries.author: Samuel Hartlib and correspondents
entries.institution: University of Sheffield, Digital Humanities Institute (Mark Greengrass, Michael Leslie and others)
entries.region: England, with letters from across Europe
entries.notes: Correspondence, diaries and papers of the 'intelligencer' Samuel Hartlib (Sheffield University Library MS 61), with full-text transcriptions and facsimiles of over 25,000 folios; the open online edition dates from 2013. The site opens with a short automatic browser check. The transcriptions are downloadable as hartlib-txt.zip (5,740 .txt files: 5,234 main documents, 442 additional items, 64 pamphlets); the files are plain text carrying SGML/HTML-like layout and editorial tags (<DOC>, <HEADER>, <BLOCK>, <I>, <EDITOR>, <ADD>, <DEL>), not well-formed XML. Dated documents run from the 1630s to the 1660s (a handful earlier or later); about 1,600 files carry no date but belong to the same papers. The data service also offers a cleaned and lemmatised version (TXT and XML) made by the Alan Turing Institute, and the page images (1.8 GB). Undated files are not counted in the period. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: HistCorp — Historical Corpora and Tools (fornsvenska / Fornsvenska textbanken)
entries.notes: HistCorp is an open platform for historical corpora and tools, distributed via the Swedish CLARIN node. Its Swedish section draws on Fornsvenska textbanken (machine-readable Old and Early Modern Swedish texts 1350-1758), which HistCorp supplies as plain text (txt and one-token-per-line tok files); the original Fornsvenska textbanken material is published as annotated XML by Språkbanken Text (https://doi.org/10.23695/pyqj-0s75). The source site (project2.sol.lu.se/fornsvenska) no longer resolves; the texts are available through the HistCorp Swedish download (Zenodo). The 5.6 M words exceed Fornsvenska's 44 texts and 1.4 M tokens, so the entry includes other HistCorp Swedish corpora; the texts counted here come from this download bundle. Freely available; the licence is CC BY. Related searchable corpora are offered by Språkbanken Text's Korp ('all_hist' mode). Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: IMPACTes OriginalImprint
entries.notes: IMPACT-es is a diachronic corpus of historical Spanish with over one hundred books (about 8 million words) from the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes and ground-truth pages from the Spanish national libraries, with a complementary lexicon of more than 10,000 lemmas linked to variant forms; about 7% of the words carry lemma, part of speech and modern equivalent. It was produced by the Universidad de Alicante and the Fundacion Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes within the IMPACT project, described by Sanchez-Martinez, Martinez-Sempere, Ivars-Ribes and Carrasco in Language Resources and Evaluation. The ground-truth files (works by Cervantes, Lope, Calderon, Garcilaso, Quevedo and others, in 16 folders) are on GitHub (impactcentre/groundtruth-spa) and the corpus is offered as zipped XML with DTDs; no later changes were found. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: Universidad de Alicante and Fundación Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes (IMPACT project)

entries.title: Inscriptiones Alborum Amicorum (IAA)
entries.institution: University of Szeged, University Library (Miklós Latzkovits, Lajos Adamik, László Bujtás and others)
entries.notes: Database of entries (inscriptions, mottoes, dedications, signatures, owners' notes) in 16th-18th century alba amicorum with a Hungarian connection: entries by Hungarians or owners from Hungary, entries made in Hungary, and entries mentioning Hungary. Each record separates the date, place, motto, dedication, signature and quoted or composed inscription text, with scans where permitted. Record numbers run to about 17,090, and the database covers the 16th to the 18th century. Status active: copyright line 2003-2026 and the database is described as continuously growing. The counts cover the entries dated 1450-1700 that have transcribed text, and 327 entries with only metadata or notes are left out. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: The site shows '© Latzkovits, Miklós 2003-2026' and no open licence. The about page says any further use of the entry photographs is allowed only with permission of the album's current owner or holding collection.

entries.notes: Izbornyk (litopys.org.ua), 'History of Ukraine, 9th-18th centuries: primary sources and interpretations', an electronic library of early Ukrainian writing. The project was started and is run by a single editor who signs as Maksym (Kyiv), with the main site opened on 1 October 2003 and a mirror at izbornyk.org.ua opened in 2008. The site is still online and carries visit statistics for 2016. entries.title: Kirishitan Japanese
entries.notes: Transcriptions of Jesuit mission press books printed in Japanese in romanised or Japanese script, from the 'Text Data Sets for Research on the History of Japanese' of the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics (NINJAL). They include the Amakusa edition of Feiqe no monogatari (1592) and Esopo no fabulas (1593) after the British Library copy (Or.59.aa.1), the 1596 Contemptus Mundi after the Herzog August Bibliothek copy, and the 1603 Nippojisho dictionary as entry-word data. Each text is offered as downloadable plain text (txt), in original romanisation and, for some, a Japanese-script transliteration; the transcriptions were published from 2019 (Contemptus Mundi 2023, revised 2025; Nippojisho entry words 2025-10). The Contemptus Mundi transcription was made with Transkribus by Sven Osterkamp, Sophie Neutzler and So Miyagawa; the site is maintained and still updated (news of July 2026). Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Lazarraga Eskuizkribua: edizioa eta azterketa / The Lazarraga Manuscript: edition and study
entries.author: Joan Perez Lazarraga
entries.institution: Monumenta Linguae Vasconum research group, UPV/EHU (Gidor Bilbao, Joseba A. Lakarra and others)
entries.notes: Edition of a Basque-Spanish manuscript of poems and prose by Joan Perez Lazarraga (c. 1547-1605), found in 2004. Transcriptions (diplomatic Basque or Spanish text), modernised spelling and Spanish translations are given for each piece, with commentary, grammar and glossary. Text A (the 'Artzain-liburua' pastoral and 29 poems) is shown as web pages; text B (34 pieces) and text C are offered as PDF transcriptions. The first palaeographic study dates the hand to 1564-1567, and a poem refers to events of 1564; the manuscript is generally dated before 1602. Pages were last modified on 19 May 2017 (version 1.2 of the edition). The counts cover 64 of the 65 pieces, since the PDF of text C is no longer available on the site. entries.title: Lexicons of Early Modern English (LEME)
entries.institution: University of Toronto
entries.notes: Lexicons of Early Modern English (LEME), a historical database of monolingual, bilingual and polyglot dictionaries, lexical encyclopedias, hard-word glossaries, spelling lists and other lexically valuable treatises in print or manuscript from about 1475 to 1755 (the catalogue covers 1477-1699). Edited by Ian Lancashire at the University of Toronto, it was first co-published by University of Toronto Press and University of Toronto Libraries (2018 edition) and is now maintained by Lancashire with Isabelle Zhu and a team of programmers. The texts are read on the site as entry-structured pages and are also deposited as TEI-based XML in the University of Toronto's TSpace repository; the site was last revised in 2024 and the collection is still being added to. entries.title: Lettres de Calvin: digital critical edition of the French correspondence of John Calvin
entries.institution: Yanet Hernández Pedraza (doctoral candidate, Université de Montréal)
entries.license_note: The site's legal notice releases the data under CC BY-SA 4.0 and the source code on GitHub under the MIT licence. The header of each TEI file still names CC BY-SA 3.0.
entries.notes: Bilingual critical edition of the letters John Calvin wrote in French between 1538 and 1554, still growing: the site currently publishes 27 of the 120 letters of the planned corpus. Each letter has facsimiles of the manuscript or printed sources, the text of Jules Bonnet's 1854 edition in sixteenth-century French, a modernised and annotated French version, and a Spanish translation; a selection of autograph manuscripts also has diplomatic transcriptions. The TEI XML files of the French letters are in the GitHub repository (the Spanish versions are in a separate folder). The project is the work of one researcher. The counts cover the 27 letters published so far, from the Bonnet base text. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: The Newton Project
entries.institution: University of Oxford
entries.notes: Online edition of the writings of Isaac Newton (1642-1727), printed and unprinted, covering his alchemical, mathematical, Mint, optical, religious and scientific papers, notebooks and correspondence. Most documents are transcribed from manuscript sources in a diplomatic rendition that records Newton's amendments, alongside a normalised, more readable version, with TEI-P5 and MathML XML viewable for each text, plus catalogue records and, for some items, translations from Latin and links to images of the originals. The project was formed in 1998 under the general editorship of Rob Iliffe and Scott Mandelbrote; it is based at the Faculty of History, University of Oxford (hosted there since autumn 2016), and was funded 2008-2014 by two AHRC grants and two JISC awards plus private donors. It is a non-profit and the site is still maintained (copyright line 2026). entries.notes: Database of Renaissance archival acts at the CESR, Tours: 95% notarial minutes (Tours, Amboise, Touraine, Paris, Bourges, Chartres, Châteaudun), with municipal accounts and deliberations and urban correspondence, 1450-1650. Of the 20,800 documents published on 1 April 2025, about 85% are given as analyses (summaries) and about 15% as transcriptions; the search engine indexes the two separately. Only the transcriptions are texts for this catalogue, and their number is not published, so texts and words are omitted. The data are encoded in XML-TEI with TELMA (IRHT) and shown as HTML through XTF (MSH Val de Loire); no TEI download was found on the site, Nakala, Zenodo or HAL, and the 2023 BVH report lists a FAIR release as work in progress. The base continues 'De minute en minute', created by the CESR in 2007 on the BVH site and moved in full to this platform in 2018; Pierre Aquilon contributed the Tours and Paris notarial records. The site returned server errors (HTTP 502 and 500) on 2026-10-27; a progress report of November 2025 (HAL halshs-05404234) shows continuing work. Sources: D. Rivaud, presentation at the École des chartes, 9 April 2025 (https://www.chartes.psl.eu/sites/default/files/public/media/document/2025-05/rivaud.pdf); S. Breuil, HAL halshs-03597555 (2018); rfgenealogie.com, 25 October 2022.

entries.title: Saggi musicali italiani (SMI)
entries.notes: Saggi musicali italiani (SMI) is an archive of Italian-language texts on music theory and aesthetics, modelled on the Thesaurus Musicarum Latinarum, with transcriptions and page graphics for treatises from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century. The sixteenth- and early seventeenth-century part includes Pietro Aaron, Zarlino, Bocchi, Bottrigari (printed and manuscript), Artusi, Bonini, Doni and Cerreto. Texts are transcribed in plain ASCII, following the source's spelling except for expanded abbreviations, spaced apostrophes and normalised accents. The project was started in 1998 at Indiana University by Andreas Giger (director until 2018) at the Center for the History of Music Theory and Literature (CHMTL), Jacobs School of Music; Giuliano Di Bacco has directed it since 2019, when redevelopment into a wider archive of vernacular music-theory texts began. The search utility was shut down after a cyberattack in 2015 and restored in 2017; in 2026 the original address redirects to a CHMTL page saying the digital thesauri are unavailable after a university-wide outage and are being moved to a new server. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Ticha Zapotec

entries.title: VAKK Estonian
entries.notes: Corpus of Old Written Estonian (VAKK) of the University of Tartu, with texts from the 15th to the 19th century. It holds all known surviving Estonian texts of the 15th and 16th centuries (manuscripts and prints, name lists excepted), most surviving 17th-century prints and known manuscript sermons, and a selection of 18th- and 19th-century prints; it also hosts 19th-century parish court protocols. Older texts are lemmatised and morphologically tagged, partly by hand and partly with Külli Prillop's Vakker software, and the corpus is searched and filtered online, with CSV or Excel export of results. The work began in 1995 in the Old Written Language research group of the Chair of Estonian (led by Valve-Liivi Kingisepp) and is funded by Estonian national programmes; the corpus has a DOI and is listed in META-SHARE. Checked 2026-10-13; the sister edition of Zrínyi in the same series does carry a copyright line, so this edition may be covered by the publisher's rights, but nothing says so.

entries.title: Die autobiographischen Aufzeichnungen Hermann Weinsbergs – Digitale Gesamtausgabe
entries.author: Hermann Weinsberg
entries.institution: Abteilung für Geschichte der Frühen Neuzeit und Rheinische Landesgeschichte, Universität Bonn, with the Historisches Archiv der Stadt Köln
entries.notes: Transcription of the three books of the Cologne citizen Hermann Weinsberg (1518-1597): Liber Iuventutis, Liber Senectutis and Liber Decrepitudinis, in Cologne German with Latin passages, each served as a series of long HTML pages (8, 11 and 10 files) with marginal notes. Everything dates from 1518-1597, so all of it is in period. The pages use an old frameset layout; the site says some functions (editorial notes) no longer work and that a relaunch is being prepared. The home page shows 'Letzte Änderung: 09.04.2024'. A DFG project since 2002. The counts cover the three books without the author's marginal notes. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: The only rights notice is the home-page footer '(c) 2003, Institut für geschichtliche Landeskunde der Rheinlande (heute: Abteilung für Geschichte der Frühen Neuzeit und Rheinische Landesgeschichte)'; the project, research and manuscript pages give only a recommended citation form. No open licence or terms of use found (checked 2026-10-13).

entries.title: Historical Corpus of the Welsh Language, 1500-1850 (HCWL; Corpws Hanesyddol yr Iaith Gymraeg)
entries.notes: Historical Corpus of the Welsh Language 1500-1850: about 420,000 words of Welsh in TEI XML (30 texts, including the 1588 Welsh Bible), built at the University of Cambridge (Department of Linguistics, David Willis) from c. 2004. celticstudies.net is the corpus's official site (published from the GitHub repository dwew2/hcwl); a parsed derivative (PARSHCWL) is included in the repository. A LINDAT/CLARIAH-CZ record (LRT-883) exists but is metadata-only and points to the old Cambridge address. Site copyright 2004, University of Cambridge. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: University of Cambridge, Linguistics Dept. (David Willis)
entries.license_note: Source-specific reuse conditions; no standard open licence established.

entries.title: Wikisource
entries.notes: Texts harvested from the language subdomains of Wikisource (de, es, it, ca, cs, el, sv, pl, hr, hu, pt, among others), the multilingual library of openly licensed digitised source texts; the entry points to the portal wikisource.org, whose per-language subdomains host each text. Several Renascor Corpus collections scope Renaissance-era texts and early Bibles specifically (e.g. Luther NT 1522, Gustav Vasa Bible 1541, Diodati 1607). Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: WiN — Wiedererzählen im Norden. Digitale Analyse weltlicher Erzählungen in niederdeutschen Inkunabeln (WiN-Korpus v1.0)
entries.notes: The WiN project (Goettingen GCDH, funded by Niedersächsisches Vorab) built a parallel corpus of Early New High German short narratives and their Middle Low German versions from late 15th c. incunabula (Dracole, Griseldis, Juden, Graf, Kaufleute...), published as WiN-Korpus v1.0 (2022) in the LAUDATIO repository (HU Berlin), TEI-annotated, with the transcription handbook on DARIAH-DE; the project page is uni-goettingen.de/de/wiedererzählen+im+norden./607371.html. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: Georg-August-Universität Göttingen (Heike Sahm, Marco Coniglio, Chiara De Bastiani, Anabel Recker, Jan Christian Schaffert; PRO*Niedersachsen)
entries.license_note: The LAUDATIO repository metadata for the corpus (id XnU19IIBa2XDdNuCXFx-, version 1.0, published 2022 by the University of Göttingen) gives corpus_publication_license https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. This is the corpus-level licence; the underlying incunabula are public domain, and the browse page itself is rendered by script, so the URL is the API record that states it.

entries.title: Winthrop Papers Digital Edition (Papers of the Winthrop Family)
entries.author: John Winthrop, Adam Winthrop and the Winthrop family
entries.institution: Massachusetts Historical Society
entries.notes: Digitised volumes of the Winthrop Papers documentary edition (letters, diaries, memoranda, legal documents and John Winthrop's journal), with the editors' markup of uncertain readings, deletions and gaps. The documents are dated 1544-1644 (plus 1682), and the browse list also holds a few items dated outside the period (1265, 1274, 1927). Only volumes 1-4 are online. No licence is stated beyond the MHS copyright line (2026). Status active: the site carries a 2026 copyright notice. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: Postil Time Machine (PosTiMe) — digital edition of the Old Lithuanian Postilles incl. the Wolfenbuettel Postille of 1573
entries.notes: PosTiMe (DFG, Frankfurt/Cologne, 2021+) produces the language-historically annotated TEI edition and reference corpus of the Old Lithuanian Lutheran postilles; its core object is the Wolfenbüttel Postille of 1573 (Cod. Guelf. 11.2 Aug. 2, Herzog August Bibliothek), the first Lithuanian collection of sermons. The Renascor Corpus text ('Wolfenbüttel Postil (1573), Old Lithuanian', source 'WP1573-TEI (postime, TITUS-derived)') is the WP1573-TEI layer derived from the earlier TITUS transcription associated with the Gelumbeckaite/HAB 1573 Postille edition project; the HAB project page describes the underlying critical edition. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: Goethe-Universitaet Frankfurt (Jolanta Gelumbeckaite) and Universitaet zu Koeln (Oyvind Eide); DFG 443985248; Wolfenbuettel ms. Cod. Guelf. 11.2 Aug. 2 at the HAB
entries.license_note: Copyright restrictions apply; no standard open reuse licence established.

entries.title: Wolne Lektury
entries.notes: Wolne Lektury is a Polish online library of free e-books and audiobooks run by the Fundacja Wolne Lektury, aimed especially at schoolchildren and offering many set school readings. Works that are in the public domain or released under free licences are annotated (footnotes, literary motifs, links to Wikimedia) and offered in HTML, TXT, PDF, EPUB, MOBI and FB2; a public API and an OAI-PMH interface are provided. The library describes holdings of several thousand works (7332 on its about page) and over a thousand audiobooks, among them older Polish texts relevant to the 1450-1700 range. The site is active and publishes news in October 2026. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: Includes CC-BY-SA-3.0-PL. Licences or rights differ by text, corpus or editorial layer; consult the source terms for the selected material.

entries.title: Künstlike Werltspröke und Eyn schön rimbökelin (WSRB): digital edition of 16th-century Middle Low German proverb collections
entries.institution: Universität Rostock (Franz-Josef Holznagel, Annika Bostelmann, Doreen Brandt, Hellmut Braun, Anne Gessing; DFG project 287283426)
entries.notes: Transcriptions and facsimiles of the eight known editions of the 'Künstlike Werltspröke' (seven editions) and the 'Schön rimbökelin', printed in Lübeck and later Hamburg between about 1540 and 1601, and a critical edition of 849 sayings with search and filters. The DOI belongs to the data publication in the RosDok repository (all TEI files plus the software); the TEI of each transcription is also served at /wsrb/xml_raw/. A book edition appeared at the same time. The counts cover the eight transcriptions, not the critical edition of the sayings. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

entries.title: ZlatyFond Slovak
entries.notes: Zlatý fond denníka SME is a digitised collection of classics of Slovak literature, run by the publisher Petit Press (daily SME) in cooperation with the Institute of Slovak Literature of the Slovak Academy of Sciences. Founded by Tomáš Ulej and launched around December 2006, it relies on volunteer digitisers and gives priority to recent, linguistically modern editions; the oldest editions are digitised only rarely. The project is led by Viera Studeničová. The live site refused automated requests (firewall), so these facts come from an archived copy of January 2025. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.institution: Petit Press (daily SME) with the Institute of Slovak Literature, Slovak Academy of Sciences
entries.license_note: The copyright page says works may be freely shared under 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 2.5 License' (no changes without the digitiser's consent, source and editor named, no commercial use); extraction or reuse of a substantial part of the database needs Petit Press's consent, except for private use, teaching and non-commercial research.

entries.title: Zrínyi Miklós: Adriai tengernek syrénája (parallel source edition of the Syrena codex and the 1651 print)
entries.institution: ELTE BTK Régi Magyar Irodalomtörténeti Tanszék (Gépeskönyv series); edited by Orlovszky Géza, Budapest 1998
entries.author: Zrínyi Miklós
entries.region: Kingdom of Hungary; printed in Vienna
entries.notes: Parallel edition (published 1998 in the Gépeskönyv series of the Old Hungarian Literature Department, ELTE) of Miklós Zrínyi's epic cycle 'Adriai tengernek syrénája': the text of the so-called Syrena manuscript beside the 1651 Vienna print (printed by Kosmerovi Máte), with the idylls, the 15 parts of the Obsidio Szigetiana, and the shorter poems. Both witnesses are old-spelling transcriptions in plain HTML pages. The site's files date from 2006 and show no later change, so it is listed as archived. The text opens in a frameset; the page at this address links to it. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
entries.license_note: The title page of the edition reads '(c) Orlovszky Géza, (c) Gépeskönyv' (Budapest 1998, ELTE BTK Department of Old Hungarian Literature, supported by the OMFB); no open licence or terms of use are given. The series index also marks this edition 'Jelszavas' (password-protected).

entries.title: Huldrych Zwingli Briefe: Digitale Texte
entries.author: Huldrych Zwingli and his correspondents
entries.institution: Institut für Schweizerische Reformationsgeschichte, Universität Zürich
entries.region: Zurich and Switzerland, with letters to and from Basel, Vienna, Cologne and elsewhere
entries.license_note: The imprint states: original data © Huldreich Zwinglis sämtliche Werke, Theologischer Verlag Zürich; digital presentation © Institut für Schweizerische Reformationsgeschichte, Universität Zürich. Free to read online.
entries.notes: Each letter is its own page (n=Brief.1 to Brief.790, 804 pages) with the running text of the critical edition Huldreich Zwinglis sämtliche Werke vol. 7-9 (Corpus Reformatorum 94-96, 1911-1925), without the apparatus; letters from 1510 to 1528. Letters 790-1292 (vols. 10-11, 1528-1531) are not online. Searchable by full text, sender, recipient and place. The wiki's change log shows the letters last edited in 2011 and the last change of any page on 1 July 2021, and the site still runs on old PHP, so it is listed as archived. The counts cover all 804 letter pages, fetched once in a browser because the site refuses automated clients. Corpus statistics (text and word counts) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.10 (texts harvested from this resource in October 2026, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).

derived.sort_title: 1641 depositions (trinity college dublin)
derived.notes_display: Transcripts, with page images, of the witness statements (depositions and examinations) collected after the Irish rising of October 1641, bound in 32 volumes (TCD MSS 809-840) and kept in Trinity College Library. Every transcript is readable online without login. The project page says the transcribing and online publication ran from 2007 to September 2010 and that the site presents about 8,000 depositions, examinations and associated materials. All the depositions are dated 1641-1653, within 1450-1700. The site's content pages were last changed on 2020-10-16 (WordPress page records), so it is marked archived. Only a TEI-compliant encoding is mentioned on the project pages; no download of the files was found. The counts rest on the site's own listing of 6,932 deposition records, and the texts themselves could not be read: the site answers automated requests with a reCAPTCHA challenge.

derived.sort_title: abac:us — austrian baroque corpus
derived.notes_display: Digital corpus of German baroque literary texts (c. 1650-1750), focused on devotional literature around death preparation (Ars moriendi, Totentanz, Memento mori) connected with Abraham a Sancta Clara (1644-1709), e.g. Mercks Wienn (1680), Grosse Todten Bruderschaft (1681). First-edition principle, XML-TEI P5 with linguistic annotation (tokenisation, PoS tagging, lemmatisation) and person/place indices. Project directed by Claudia Resch and Ulrike Czeitschner; online since 2015, new infrastructure launched 2025. Project archive page: https://www.oeaw.ac.at/acdh/research/literary-studies/research/project-archive/abacus.

derived.sort_title: abu — bibliotheque universelle
derived.notes_display: Free-access collection of French-language public-domain texts, in the catalogue's early-modern part including works such as the Lettres de la religieuse portugaise, Argens's Lettres juives and Corneille's plays. It is produced and distributed by volunteer members of the Association des Bibliophiles Universels (ABU, a 1901-law association founded in April 1993) and hosted by the CEDRIC multimedia and human-computer interaction team at the Conservatoire national des arts et metiers, Paris. The texts are plain HTML pages for reading online; the catalogue lists 288 texts by 101 authors (January 2002), and the site has had no visible additions since then.

derived.sort_title: adl danish
derived.notes_display: Texts of the Archive for Danish Literature (ADL), a collaboration between the Det Danske Sprog- og Litteraturselskab (DSL) and the Royal Danish Library (KB), published in the public GitHub repository kb-dk/public-adl-text-sources. The corpus comprises 498 volumes (165,512 pages) of Danish literature, all encoded in TEI; the repository contains the roughly two-thirds of pages that have been OCR'd and encoded, one TEI-XML file per volume under texts/. The repository also documents the encoding practices, offers XSLT scripts to extract single works, and accepts contributions by pull request; it was last pushed to in August 2026.

derived.sort_title: alciato's book of emblems: the memorial web edition in latin and english
derived.notes_display: Web edition of the 212 emblems of Alciato's Emblematum liber, with the Latin text taken from the 1621 variorum edition and checked against the 1531, 1534 and 1546 editions, an English translation, commentary files and images. The original address (www.mun.ca/alciato) now returns 404, so the URL is the Internet Archive copy of 3 October 2022; the site was last updated in April 2005. The site also carries images of Whitney's Choice of Emblemes (1586) and a 17th-century jest book. The counts cover the Latin text file only, not the English text, the commentaries or those two other works.

derived.sort_title: aldicam-cm — atlas linguistico diacronico e interactivo de la comunidad de madrid
derived.notes_display: Transcribed archival documents from the 13th to the 19th century from archives of the Comunidad de Madrid (Archivo Regional, Archivo de la Villa, municipal, ecclesiastical and private archives), with paleographic and critical presentation and facsimiles, searchable and mappable without login. Same search engine as CODEA+ 2022; about a third of the regestos coincide with CODEA+ 2022 documents. No bulk download found. About a third of its document summaries coincide with CODEA+ 2022. Twelve documents without a date and three without paleographic text are not in the counts.

derived.sort_title: amadis in translation (digital amadis)
derived.notes_display: Digital study of the transformation of Montalvo's Amadís de Gaula across editions and translations (Spanish, French, English, from the 1500s to the early 1800s). The corpus files are the 35 TEI XML chapters of the 1547 Sevilla printing of Montalvo's Amadís (facsimile source: Biblioteca Virtual de Andalucía), used to align Garci Rodríguez de Montalvo's text with Robert Southey's 1803 translation and study translation shifts. Project team: Stacey Triplette, Elisa Beshero-Bondar, Helena Bermúdez Sabel; maintained by Beshero-Bondar since 2015. Code and TEI data are on GitHub (AGPL-3.0), with an archived release on Zenodo. Project documentation and a 1533 frontispiece facsimile on the project site.

derived.sort_title: acta pacis westphalicae digital (apw digital)
derived.notes_display: Digital edition of the Acta Pacis Westphalicae, the documents of the Westphalian peace congress (instructions, correspondence, minutes, negotiation papers and diaries; the congress ran 1643-1649, with a few earlier or later items). All volumes of the three series are readable online with a document-by-document view, scans of the printed pages, PDF download of the printed volumes and the TEI XML full text of each document (served as TEI fragments, without a teiHeader). No login is needed. The edition text is a digitised critical edition of the archival originals (about 157 archives). The counts cover 3,210 of the 14,545 listed documents (22%), from 19 of the 41 volumes; the server was unstable during the harvest.

derived.sort_title: briefe und akten zur kirchenpolitik friedrichs des weisen und johanns des bestandigen 1513 bis 1532
derived.notes_display: Academy edition of the church-policy correspondence and records of the two electors. The online database lists 3,385 documents; for 1,760 of them (dated 1493 to December 1522) editing is marked complete. Of these, those with an edited source text show it beside the German summary; the others currently show a summary and metadata only, and the rest of the database is metadata. The printed volumes (three so far, the latest in December 2025) are not online here. Twelve further documents appear with full transcriptions and images under 'Kabinettstücke'. News on the site is dated October 2026. The counts cover the 302 documents with an edited source text found on the document pages, and will grow as texts are added.

derived.sort_title: balassi balint osszes verse: halozati kritikai kiadas (network critical edition of the complete poems)
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of Balassi's poems, first published online in 1998 (version 1.0), revised as 1.1 (1999) and 2.0 (2002), with facsimiles, apparatus, notes and a repertory. The site is a set of HTML frames. Newest file seen was modified in 2006. The poems carry no individual dates, so their place within 1450-1700 rests on the author's life span (he died in 1594).

derived.sort_title: balkan slavic digital editions (pop puncov sbornik, life of st. petka, tale of alexander, excerpts)
derived.notes_display: Corpus of Balkan Slavic texts from the 10th to the 19th century collected for the study of linguistic change: Pop Punčo's Sbornik (1796), the Life of St. Petka in many copies, the Tale of Alexander the Elder, and an Excerpts sub-corpus. Texts come with English translations, morphological and syntactic annotation, search and facsimiles. Sources within 1450-1700 include Vuković's Zbornik za putnike (printed 1536), the Joseph-Volokolamsk manuscript of 1537, the Tikhonravov damaskin and other 17th-century damaskini, Šimun Kozičić (1530s), and Letters of Wallachian princes. Texts are read in the web interface. The search engine loads its corpus from public token-level JSON files with diplomatic form, lemma, MULTEXT-East tags and Universal Dependencies relations (lt_data.json for the Excerpts texts, petka_data.json for the Life of St. Petka, sva_data.json for the Tale of Alexander, data_1.json and data_2.json for Pop Punčo's Sbornik of 1796). These files are not advertised as downloads. Search results can be exported as CSV or CoNLL-U. The 23 Damaskini texts are also deposited at CLARIN.SI (11356/1441). Status active: the home page was modified in July 2026 and the Excerpts page in February 2026. The counts cover the 13 texts dated within 1450-1700, leaving out the Sbornik (1796), and several dates are approximate (century midpoints or decades).

derived.sort_title: annotated corpus of pre-standardized balkan slavic literature 1.1
derived.notes_display: The 23-text Damaskini subcorpus (16th-19th c. Balkan Slavic, Bulgarian/Macedonian/Torlak, ~53k tokens) is exactly the resource published at CLARIN.SI handle 11356/1441 (v1.1, 2021) by the SNSF-funded ZuCoSlaV project of Ivan Simko (University of Zurich, Slavic Seminary). The UZH GitLab project (https://gitlab.uzh.ch/uzh-slavic-corpora/pre-standardized-balkan-slavic-literature) only holds a README, so the CLARIN.SI record is the only place with the data. Formats are TSV/CoNLL-U/plain text (not TEI). License: CC BY-SA 4.0.

derived.sort_title: bartoli correspondence
klasikoen gordailua (euskal klasikoen corpusa, upv/ehu)
derived.notes_display: Klasikoen Gordailua (Repository of Classics), run by armiarma.eus since 2005, which aims to gather nearly all classic Basque texts up to the twentieth century; its search tool, the Corpus Arakatzailea, dates from 2007. The Basque Classics Corpus (Euskal Klasikoen Corpusa) of the UPV/EHU Institute of the Basque Language republishes this material (published there on 2013-12-05; author Joseba Ezeiza): 496 books from the 16th century to 1975, searchable by author, period, dialect and genre. The whole corpus can be downloaded as a single file in TEI or RTF.

derived.sort_title: correspondance de pierre bayle (edition electronique)
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of the letters sent and received by Pierre Bayle (1647-1706), with transcriptions, annotations, indexes and translations of Latin letters. The site publishes letters 1-1405 (volumes I-XI of the printed edition, 1662-1698); volumes XII-XIV (letters up to 1791 and 1706) are not online. The site mentions TEI/XML output but no files are public. The site was updated in 2025.

derived.sort_title: biblioteca digital del pensamiento novohispano (bdpn)
derived.notes_display: BDPN is the UNAM 'Biblioteca Digital del Pensamiento Novohispano' of 16th-17th century Mexican texts (astrological and astronomical discourse, letters, almanacs). The official site (bdpn.unam.mx) is online and states that the TEI files are distributed in the GitHub repository ficino2021/bdpn; the site licence is CC BY-NC 4.0 while the repository carries CC0.

derived.sort_title: belarusian skaryna
derived.notes_display: Four texts from Francysk Skaryna's Bible printings. Only the preface to the whole Bible comes from knihi.com (Belaruskaya Palichka, original orthography, source edition not stated); the other three texts (Judith, Psalter and Proverbs prefaces) come from the Belarusian Wikisource transcription of Harecki's 1922 chrestomathy, because knihi.com gives those in modern Belarusian.

derived.sort_title: bertonio aymara
derived.notes_display: Digitised edition of Ludovico Bertonio's Vocabulario de la Lengua Aymara (Juli, 1612), distributed as a StarDict dictionary in the native-dics repository of Amos Batto. The text is not a diplomatic transcription: the orthography was modernised by Radio San Gabriel, and the dictionary was digitised by ILLA-A.

derived.sort_title: bess of hardwick's letters: the complete correspondence, c. 1550-1608
derived.notes_display: Complete correspondence of Bess of Hardwick (c. 1521/7-1608): 234 letters to and from her, each with diplomatic and normalised transcripts, colour images of 185 of them, and commentary. All letters fall within 1550-1608 (1550s: 7; 1560s: 31; 1570s: 74; 1580s: 52; 1590s: 18; 1600s: 52). The letters are served as XML (a project-specific format, not TEI), and the whole set, with a metadata database, can be downloaded from the Digital Humanities Institute data service. Version 1.0 was released in September 2013 and the data was deposited on 13 July 2021; no later change is visible, so the status is archived.

derived.sort_title: betamasaheft geez
derived.notes_display: TEI-XML records of Ethiopian and Eritrean literary works (Ge'ez and other languages of the Christian written tradition) kept in the BetaMasaheft/Works GitHub repository, the data layer of the Beta masahaft project 'Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea'. The records are served through the project's eXist-db application at betamasaheft.eu, which links works to manuscripts, persons and places and is built on a Clavis Aethiopica numbering of works. The project is a long-term programme of the Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Hamburg (2016-2040), directed by Alessandro Bausi and hosted by the Hiob Ludolf Centre for Ethiopian and Eritrean Studies, University of Hamburg; it follows an ERC project led by Denis Nosnitsin (2009-2015). The repository is under active development (last push October 2026).

derived.sort_title: bibliotheca augustana
derived.notes_display: Bibliotheca Augustana, a collection of electronic texts in Latin and in Greek, German, English, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Russian, Portuguese, Czech and Yiddish, with a chronological and an alphabetical index for each language section. It is the personal project of Ulrich Harsch (professor emeritus, Augsburg University of Applied Sciences), online since 1 March 1996 and still hosted on the university's web space. Texts are plain HTML pages for reading online; the imprint states that images from other sources are either below the threshold of protection or released by their authors.

derived.sort_title: biblioteca virtual miguel de cervantes (bvmc)
derived.notes_display: The 331 Spanish texts (comedias like 'El gran teatro del mundo', 'El vellocino de oro', etc.) were harvested from the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes, the major Spanish digital library run with the Universidad de Alicante. Open access but individual texts are copyrighted by BVMC (no blanket open licence).

derived.sort_title: biblioteca italiana
derived.notes_display: Digital library of texts of Italian literary and cultural tradition from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, promoted since 1996 by the Centro Interuniversitario Biblioteca Italiana Telematica (CIBIT) and run from the Department of Italianistica e Spettacolo at Sapienza University of Rome; the BIBIT section was started under Amedeo Quondam in 2003. BIBIT holds more than 1,600 works in full-text editions based on scholarly reference editions, encoded in XML/TEI (the TEI header records each text's history), which can be read, searched with concordances and downloaded; the site also holds scanned incunabula and the Scrittori d'Italia series as images. The portal's content pages were last edited in 2019.

derived.sort_title: blotius digital: digitale edition des inventars der wiener hofbibliothek (1576)
derived.notes_display: Edition of the first surviving catalogue of the imperial court library (ÖNB Cod. 13525, 'pars posterior', M-Z, compiled 1575/76), shown beside the facsimile with registers of places, persons and works. Only part is transcribed: the page states that letters N to U are not transcribed at the moment. Published 2019 (TEI header 'lastChanged 2019-04-29'); no later update found, so it is listed as archived. The inventory (656 entries) is counted as one text, and only the transcribed part is included.

derived.sort_title: bodleian first folio: digital edition of shakespeare's comedies, histories and tragedies (1623)
derived.notes_display: Diplomatic transcriptions of the 36 plays in the Bodleian Library's copy of the Shakespeare First Folio (1623, shelfmark Arch. G c.7), shown beside the page images and encoded in TEI P5, with published transcription guidelines. Each play can be downloaded as an XML file, as a formatted PDF and with its page images. The site has not changed since 2019 and its blog since April 2020, but it is still online.

derived.sort_title: diplomatic correspondence of thomas bodley, 1585-1597
derived.notes_display: Letters to and from Thomas Bodley during his diplomatic career, with customisable transcripts (abbreviations expanded or shown, as the reader chooses). Texts: 990 XML letter files in the project's GitHub repository (1585-1597). The XML uses the project's own markup, not TEI; the repository was last pushed in 2013 but the site pages show 2025 modification dates, so it is treated as still online and maintained. The counts cover the 982 files with transcribed letter text; six files without letter text were left out.

derived.sort_title: bokselskap
derived.notes_display: Bokselskap (Det norske språk- og litteraturselskap, with the National Library of Norway) publishes Norwegian texts online. A CC0 TEI P5 dump of about 380 texts, dated 19 January 2023, is available from Språkbanken (National Library of Norway); the site now lists more books and offers no XML download itself.

derived.sort_title: book of margery kempe: facsimile and edition (including the wynkyn de worde pamphlet)
derived.notes_display: Only the Wynkyn de Worde pamphlet (Here begynneth a shorte treatyse of contemplacyon..., printed in Fleet Street around 1501) falls in the period: the site gives a diplomatic transcription of it, beside facsimile images, in the Showcase viewer, plus a comparison with the Book. The main text, the manuscript BL MS Add. 61823 (copied around 1440, with later annotating hands), has diplomatic and reader's editions on the site. Active: a project page was edited on 2025-04-03. The counts cover the pamphlet only, since the manuscript lies outside 1450-1700.

derived.sort_title: boschdoc: source documents on hieronymus bosch
derived.notes_display: Database of 939 entries (the home page says almost 1) about Bosch, his family, patrons and works: mostly handwritten court records, accounts and inventories of 's-Hertogenbosch, plus some early printed works and Spanish manuscripts, each with facsimile, transcription, remarks and translation. The site was published for the 2016 Bosch anniversary and its data files date from 2021, with no later change seen. The counts cover the entries that have a transcription, and the 56 entries without one are left out.

derived.sort_title: workdiaries of robert boyle
derived.notes_display: Editorial and diplomatic transcripts, with images, of Robert Boyle's workdiaries (records of experiments, recipes, reading notes) from the Royal Society and the British Library, with indexes of people, places and books. The site dates from about 2007; its pages show 2025 modification dates (static re-hosting), so it is listed as active, though no new content is evident. Copyright: the site states materials are copyrighted and for personal use.

derived.sort_title: briefe adeliger frauen (16.-18. jh.): beziehungen und bezugssysteme
derived.notes_display: Letters of Austrian noblewomen from family archives (Schallenberg, Starhemberg and others), with transcriptions and short summaries, plus lists of the wider holdings (about 2,900 letters, 16th-18th century). The letters transcribed on the site are dated 1494 to 1678, none after 1700. The site dates from 1999-2004 (last modified November 2004). The counts cover the letters with period text, and entries with only a modern summary are not included.

derived.sort_title: briefwisseling van constantijn huygens 1607-1687
derived.notes_display: Database of 9,237 letters to and from Constantijn Huygens (1596-1687), each with metadata and a facsimile of the original, linked to the text of J.A. Worp's edition (6 volumes, 1911-1917) in the Huygens 'retroboeken' viewer, which serves the text of each page as searchable OCR; new letters unpublished by Worp, and transcriptions and translations of selected letters (musical letters, letters of Anna Maria van Schurman and Lucia van Aerssen-Walta) are added. A metadata export (brieven.xls) is offered. Status active: the project blog has posts up to September 2026. Its texts could not be counted: the site refuses automated requests, and the text is OCR of Worp's printed edition with his introductions, notes and indexes mixed in.

derived.sort_title: brievenalsbuit
das bucherinventar der elisabeth von calenberg (1539): edition und anmerkungen
derived.notes_display: Edition of the list of books in the private rooms of Duchess Elisabeth of Braunschweig-Calenberg, from the inventory handed to her chambermaid at Münden in June 1539, with transcription facsimile links, footnotes and bibliographies (published 2011 as Editiones Electronicae Guelferbytanae 7). The TEI file holds one inventory extract with 69 numbered book entries. The TEI file was last modified in 2011.

derived.sort_title: bullinger digital
derived.notes_display: Correspondence of the Zurich reformer Heinrich Bullinger (1504-1575), about 12,000 letters to and from him dated 1523-1575, held mostly in the Staatsarchiv des Kantons Zuerich and the Zentralbibliothek Zuerich. Metadata, summaries and footnotes come from the printed HBBW edition; the letter texts come from the HBBW, other printed editions, the HBBW team's preparatory work and automatic handwriting recognition, and are published with facsimiles, normalised search forms, machine translation into English and linked named entities. The project ran 2020-2025 at the Institute of Computational Linguistics, University of Zurich (leaders Patricia Scheurer, Phillip B. Stroebel, Martin Volk; funded by the UZH Foundation); at its end in May 2025 the TEI-XML corpus was handed to the Staatsarchiv Zuerich, which now maintains the online search system.

derived.sort_title: camena
derived.notes_display: Texts are taken from a republication of the project's XML files on GitHub (Neven Jovanović, University of Zagreb, snapshot 2016), licensed CC-BY-SA; the CAMENA site at the Universität Mannheim serves the same material work by work. The project has had no news since 2017.

derived.sort_title: archivio tommaso campanella (atc)
derived.notes_display: Archivio Tommaso Campanella (ATC), part of the ILIESI 'Archivio dei filosofi del Rinascimento' (with the Bruno and Vanini archives). It gathers the writings of Tommaso Campanella (1568-1639) in text-with-facsimile form, mostly following modern critical editions (for example by Luigi Firpo and Germana Ernst), together with a detailed chronology, a census of early Campanella prints in Italian and foreign libraries, documents, bibliographic notes, studies, images and an ethical-political lexicon. The texts are also available as TEI XML files. Run by ILIESI-CNR (Rome) under the scientific direction of Eugenio Canone; the site is dedicated to Germana Ernst and its pages carry copyright dates 2009-2020.

derived.sort_title: casebooks project
derived.notes_display: Digital edition of the medical casebooks of the astrologers Simon Forman and Richard Napier (1596-1634), whose consultation records are held by the Bodleian Library, Oxford. Each case is transcribed in XML and published with page images, name, place and treatment directories, critical introductions and selected cases in full. It was produced by the Casebooks Project, a team at the University of Cambridge led by Professor Lauren Kassell, with Wellcome Trust funding from 2008 (pilot, programme and strategic awards, 2008-2019); since 2019 the project is in an archiving and preservation phase.
