The raw XML transcriptions and authority lists are published in the CasebooksProject/casebooks-data GitHub repository, and the images are at the Cambridge Digital Library. The site's pages returned errors when checked on 2026-10-13, so the details come from archived copies.

derived.sort_title: digital edition of filippo cavriana's correspondence
derived.notes_display: The repository Pantagrueliste/CavrianaCorr is a digital TEI edition of Filippo Cavriana's late-16th-century correspondence, described as 'Digital Edition of Filippo Cavriana's Correspondence'; licence CC BY 4.0. Matches the collected 2-text collection exactly.

derived.sort_title: celt corpus of electronic texts
derived.notes_display: Online textbase of Irish history, literature and politics from University College Cork, comprising texts in Irish, Latin, Anglo-Norman French and English, with English translations where possible; a large part dates from before 1700. Texts are taken from the best printed editions, scanned, proofread and encoded in TEI-conformant SGML or XML, with HTML versions and introductions and bibliographies, and can be read, searched and downloaded. CELT was founded in 1992 by Professor Donnchadh O Corrain, who directed it until his retirement; it was funded by the American Ireland Funds, the Irish Higher Education Authority and the Irish Research Council for the Humanities and Social Sciences, among others. The site is still online but its copyright line reads 1997-2010 and the FAQ counts 1638 texts as of 24 February 2021.

derived.sort_title: la entretenida by miguel de cervantes: a digital, annotated edition and an english translation
derived.notes_display: Edition of Cervantes's play from the 1615 first edition (Ocho comedias y ocho entremeses), in several versions: facsimile, modern-spelling transcription, edited text and unpunctuated text, with an English translation, indices, a map and performance information. Site marked 2018; its newest file is from May 2023, so nothing changed in the last three years. The counts cover the first-edition text only, not the other versions or the English translation.

derived.sort_title: teatro de autores portugueses do sec. xvi
derived.notes_display: Textual database of critical editions of 16th-century Portuguese theatre by the Centro de Estudos de Teatro (ULisboa). The live obras page (ver http://cet-e-quinhentos.com/obras) lists the exact collected autos, including 'Auto de Santiago' by Afonso Álvares and 'Auto das Padeiras' (Anónimo). HTML site with critical apparatus/glossary/facsimiles (not TEI). Licence not stated.

derived.sort_title: charta — corpus hispanico y americano en la red: textos antiguos
derived.notes_display: Selection of archival documents drawn from the corpora of the member research groups of the CHARTA network (CODCAR, CODEMA, CORHEN, CODEA, CDHM, COREECOM, CODDEC, DGSXIX, DOLEO, CorColombia, CORAPRINA, COHSANRE, COTAGAL, DCEP, CORDEREGRA, CORDINA, COHIECOS), so the texts also exist in those corpora. Each document has facsimile (where available), paleographic and critical presentations; free reading and search without login on the TEITOK platform; per-document TEI XML is served at corpora.uah.es/charta/xmlfiles/<id>.xml the XML files are listed at index.php?action=files and downloaded one by one; there is no bulk archive.

derived.sort_title: chm mapudungun
derived.notes_display: Digital, linguistically tagged collection of early writings in Mapudungun (Mapuche), covering materials from 1606 to 1930, mostly by missionaries but also explorers, military men and ethnographers. Texts are shown as web versions that often follow the source's layout with a parallel Spanish or Latin translation, and are parsed by hand and semi-automatically for lemma, part of speech and morpheme, searchable in original spelling, in the Alfabeto Mapuche Unificado or by English gloss. Version 1.0 was compiled by Benjamin Molineaux (Angus McIntosh Centre for Historical Linguistics, University of Edinburgh) under a Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship (April 2018 to March 2021); the search interface was built by Vasilis Karaiskos. The texts are also available as TEI-XML files.

derived.sort_title: chymistry of isaac newton
derived.notes_display: Online edition of Newton's alchemical manuscripts from Cambridge and other libraries, each shown in a normalised and a diplomatic transcription (encoded in TEI/XML, but the XML is not offered for download), with English translations of non-English passages, glossary and analysis tools. Newton wrote and copied about one million words on alchemy; the site's browse list holds 73 manuscripts, which is the count given, some of them Newton's copies of older texts. The Oxford Newton Project is a separate resource. Pages show an update stamp of 2025-07-03. The count of 73 manuscripts comes from the browse list, and the texts themselves could not be read to count words: the site does not allow automated access to the transcriptions, and the TEI files are not published.

derived.sort_title: dantiscus' correspondence
derived.notes_display: CIDTC is the digital critical edition of the correspondence of Johannes Dantiscus (1485-1548), royal Polish diplomat, published online at the University of Warsaw's editions.al.uw.edu.pl on an eXist-db/TEI-Publisher stack. The root URL shows a bare eXist-db landing page; the edition app itself lives at /exist/apps/dantiscus/, serving TEI P5 XML files with IDs of the form IDLxxxxx.xml exactly as the origin indicates.

derived.sort_title: epistolarium (ckcc)
derived.notes_display: Web application and corpus of about 20,000 letters written by and to scholars of the 17th-century Dutch Republic (among them Grotius, Constantijn and Christiaan Huygens, Descartes, Leeuwenhoek and Swammerdam), with faceted search and geographic, time-based, social-network and co-citation visualisations. The project Circulation of Knowledge and Learned Practices in the 17th-century Dutch Republic was run by Huygens ING with DANS, the University of Amsterdam, the Descartes Centre and the Koninklijke Bibliotheek, funded by NWO and CLARIN-NL; the letters were converted to TEI XML. Version 1.0 appeared in June 2013 and the ePistolarium was launched on 14 June 2013; an archived version of the project data (dated 23 July 2013) is deposited at DANS. The data are a snapshot of 2013 and no later additions were found.

derived.sort_title: codea+ 2022 — corpus de documentos espanoles anteriores a 1900
derived.notes_display: Archival documents from the origins of Spanish to 1899 (Archivo Histórico Nacional, Simancas, Indias, Corona de Aragón and many local archives), each with facsimile, paleographic and critical transcription; lemmatised and POS-tagged (>90% of the lexicon). Texts are read and searched in the web interface only; no bulk download found (the corpus conditions of use forbid derivative corpora). The DOI 10.37536/CODEA.2015 is the one given in the project's citation instructions. CODEA+ 2015 remains available separately. The documents themselves were not downloaded because the licence (CC BY-NC-ND) does not allow reuse of the documents in a corpus.

derived.sort_title: codiaje — the annotated diachronic corpus of judeo-spanish
derived.notes_display: Multi-alphabetic annotated diachronic corpus of Judeo-Spanish (16th–21st c.) built in TEITOK (TEI-XML over CQP); hosted with a live TEITOK interface at LINDAT/CLARIN. Directed by Aldina Quintana (Hebrew University of Jerusalem); described in Scriptum Digital 9 (2020). The project's description page is on Aldina Quintana's HUJI site.

derived.sort_title: colonia — corpus of classical (colonial) portuguese
derived.notes_display: Colonia is the diachronic corpus of classical Portuguese (16th-20th c.) of the AC/DC annotation project at Linguateca (Diana Santos). The live Linguateca author/works list for Colonia enumerates exactly the collected works — Anchieta, Pero Vaz de Caminha, Gandavo, Vieira sermons/letters, Camões, Guerr(a?)e(d)eiro, Melo. The corpus's own site (corporavm.uni-koeln.de/colonia) is dead; Linguateca's page remains the live official listing.

derived.sort_title: controversia confessio
derived.notes_display: Source edition on the formation of confessions and confessionalisation (1548-1580), documenting the theological disputes after the Augsburg Interim of 1548 and the Leipzig Interim, in nine planned thematic volumes. The project's database records more than 2000 printed controversial writings of 1548-1577/80 (full titles, authorship, printers, dates, present library locations, title-page scans and often summaries) and about 240 short biographies of the theologians and politicians involved; digital versions of the printed edition volumes are being produced in cooperation with the Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbuettel and the University and State Library Darmstadt. The project has run since 2007 as a long-term project of the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz, with the Leibniz-Institut fuer Europaeische Geschichte and Johannes Gutenberg-Universitaet Mainz, and ended with the conference volume C&C 12 published in 2025.

derived.sort_title: git-coqalane — corpus tei-xml des coq-a-l'ane
derived.notes_display: TEI-XML corpus of the Renaissance coq-a-l'âne epistle genre (poems 1530-1650) by Cyril Cano-Arnedo, one TEI file per poem, reuse under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, published on GitHub (ongoing encoding) with an earlier partial copy on Huma-Num GitLab. The 57 texts counted here match the GitLab copy.

derived.sort_title: cordiam — corpus diacronico y diatopico del espanol de america
derived.notes_display: Three subcorpora: Documentos (6,851 texts, archival documents from 'corpus de corpus'), Literatura (6,367; 16th-19th c.) and Prensa (16,271; 18th-19th c. only). The search interface is open without login and full documents are available as per-document PDF files (with a metadata sheet on page 1); the search interface shows concordances and example passages as HTML; there is no bulk download and no TEI. Documents are transcriptions with expanded abbreviations. The countries listed are a selection of the 20+ countries covered. The counts cover the 7,334 documents with a year between 1494 and 1700, and documents dated only by century are not included.

derived.sort_title: coreecom — corpus electronico del espanol colonial mexicano
derived.notes_display: The 'Corpus documental' list (checked 2026-10-12) contains 119 documents, all with Periodo between 1500 and 1599 (1500-1524: 11; 1525-1549: 31; 1550-1574: 43; 1575-1599: 34), from AGI, AGN México, AHN, Simancas etc. Intro text announces 16th-18th century coverage but only the 16th century is online. Each document page shows a facsimile reference, the paleographic edition and the critical edition side by side. There is no data download. The site footer gives a last update of 30 August 2019. A member of the CHARTA network.

derived.sort_title: taklow kernewek ('cornish things') — cornish language text resources
derived.notes_display: Taklow Kernewek, a personal site by David Trethewey, hosts digitised Cornish texts including 'Gwreans an Bys' (The Creation of the World, Cornish mystery play, MS 1611) in plain text. The text used is the Kernewek Kemmyn respelling (Keith Syed and Ray Edwards, KDL edition 2000) of Whitley Stokes's edition (1864); the manuscript-spelling text is kernewek_corpus/cwkdlms.txt in the GitHub repository. Licence not stated on the site.

derived.sort_title: homelyes xiii in cornysche (tregear homilies, bl add ms 46397)
derived.notes_display: Computer text of the Tregear Homilies (Homelyes XIII in Cornysche, a Cornish translation of thirteen homilies, British Library Add MS 46397, dated 1556), transcribed on Wikisource as plain wikitext. It reproduces the 1994 KDL (Cornish Language Board) reprint of Christopher Bice's 1969 edition, prepared by Keith Syed, who followed Bice in every detail even where he knew the transcription differed from the manuscript. The page was created in 2009 and last edited on 7 February 2020; it carries a contents list of the thirteen homilies and bracketed compiler's notes.

derived.sort_title: corpus corporum
derived.notes_display: Repository of Latin texts (with some Greek) from antiquity to the early modern period, run by the Institute for Greek and Latin Philology of the University of Zurich, directed by Philipp Roelli. It holds the Patrologia Latina, the Vulgate and many other corpora, stored as standardised TEI-XML and searchable by full text, Boolean, proximity and lemma (Latin), with period limits (about 83 percent of texts carry a date tag), dictionaries, a synoptic Bible view and metrical analysis; texts can be downloaded for non-commercial use. The present interface was rebuilt around 2019 and the site is still maintained.

derived.sort_title: corpus mallorca — documentos castellanos de los archivos mallorquines
derived.notes_display: Unpublished Castilian documents from archives in Mallorca, Menorca and Ibiza (Arxiu del Regne de Mallorca, municipal archives, Epistolario Santacilia, etc.), edited with CHARTA norms (paleographic transcription and critical presentation, facsimiles), searchable by archive, province, type, date; used for the study of Catalan-Spanish contact. Some passages in Latin or Catalan are tagged. Funded by FFI2014-59135-R and FFI2017-83899-P. No download; page last modified 2024-09-22 (index.html). The corpus has 1,251 documents dated 1640-1909. Most documents are from the Balearic Islands.

derived.sort_title: corpus17 — 17th c. french texts corpus
derived.notes_display: CORPUS17 is Simon Gabay's open GitHub corpus of 17th-century French texts encoded in diplomatic TEI (e-ditiones/CORPUS17, description '17th c. French texts corpus'). The 120 collected texts (dates 1624-1687 etc.) mirror its TEI files. No explicit licence in repo metadata listed by the GitHub API.

derived.sort_title: cosuiza — corpus de documentos hispanicos de suiza
derived.notes_display: 123 TEITOK documents (stats page 'action=stats', checked 2026-10-12): non-literary manuscripts edited following the CHARTA criteria (palaeographic and critical presentation, TEI XML with lemma/POS). Raw TEI XML is served per document. Part of the CHARTA network. The counts cover the 27 documents dated within 1450-1700, but 70 of the 123 documents have no date in their TEI header, so the period share is understated, and the corpus is under construction.

derived.sort_title: anthologies of the spoudastirion neou ellinismou (snhell.gr) — cretan greek lyric poetry
derived.notes_display: Three Cretan poems (dedications to Chortatsis' Erofili and Panoria and Foskolos' Fortounatos) from the online anthology of the Spoudastirion Neou Ellinismou (snhell.gr; text from Kritiki Lyriki Poiisi, Ermis 1999), harvested through the Wayback Machine. The host snhell.gr no longer resolves; the entry points to an archived snapshot of Chortatsis' page (2025), and the Foskolos text is at https://web.archive.org/web/20250809221230/http://www.snhell.gr/anthology/content.asp?id=46&author_id=54.

derived.sort_title: croala (croatiae auctores latini)
derived.notes_display: Peer-reviewed, freely available digital collection of Latin texts by Croatian authors and others connected with Croatia, from the epitaph of Queen Jelena (976) to Ivan Golub's Latin poems (first published 1984), of which the part before 1700 is relevant here. Published by the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences of the University of Zagreb from the research project 'Digitalizacija hrvatskih latinista', with an editorial board led by Neven Jovanovic (Zagreb) with Yasmin Haskell, Nella Lonza, Bratislav Lucin, Elia Marinova, Darko Novakovic and Terence O. Tunberg. The texts are TEI-XML, openly downloadable from a GitHub repository (with Zenodo DOI) and searchable through PhiloLogic4 and a BaseX database; the online edition is dated 2024 and the repository was last updated in April 2026.

derived.sort_title: bible-corpus, czech collection — czech bible text (kralice translation) from the multilingual parallel bible corpus
derived.notes_display: The 66 books of the Czech Bible in the Multilingual Parallel Bible Corpus (Christos Christodoulopoulos), now hosted in the TextGrid Repository (TEI P5) and formerly on GitHub (CES XML, CC0-1.0). The text is the Kralice Bible wording in modernised spelling taken from the Bible Database, so 1613 is the date of the translation, not of a diplomatic transcription.

derived.sort_title: early modern danish postils v0.2.0
derived.notes_display: Verified via the Zenodo API: record 7479443 (v0.2.0) is 'Early Modern Danish Postils' by Jonas Kjøller-Rasmussen (University of Copenhagen), concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7113232 — the canonical project URL; the record used here is version 0.2.0. 13 texts, plain text distribution. License MIT.

derived.sort_title: dasypodius' dictionarium latinogermanicum (1535)
derived.notes_display: Transcription of the first edition of Dasypodius' dictionary (Strasbourg: Rihel, 1535, Strasbourg copy) with variant readings of the 1536 edition, in five TEI files (contents and preface, A-B, C-H, I-O, P-Z) and a TEI introduction, revised 30 November 2012. Last file modified 2012. The dictionary (about 6,600 entries) is counted as one text, without the 1536 variant readings.

derived.sort_title: digitale bibliotheek voor de nederlandse letteren (dbnl)
derived.notes_display: Digital library of Dutch-language literature, linguistics and cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present, covering the whole Dutch-speaking area; the 1550-1700 period has its own section, and there are regional collections (Limburg, Friesland, Suriname, South Africa), a children's literature selection, reference works, e-books and a public-domain collection. It is run in cooperation between the Taalunie, BibliothecairErfgoed.be and the KB (National Library of the Netherlands), which owns the database rights. Works can be read online and downloaded for private use; the site was still updated in October 2026.

derived.sort_title: deux visages de l'astree (first critical edition of honore d'urfe's l'astree)
derived.notes_display: Web edition, begun in 2007, of the four parts of L'Astrée in two versions: a faithful critical text (reference editions of 1621 for parts I-III and of 1624 for part IV) and a 'functional' version in more modern French, with variants, notes, indexes and illustrations; the preliminary editions of 1607, 1610 and 1619 are also online. The author died in 2021; the site moved to the University of Rouen in March 2025 and its news page records a change in June 2026. A downloadable Word version of the functional edition is offered. The counts cover the four parts of the reference edition, without the preliminary editions of 1607, 1610 and 1619.

derived.sort_title: social edition of the devonshire ms (bl add. ms 17492)
derived.notes_display:
A digital edition of a mid-sixteenth-century miscellany of verse and prose, compiled in the court circle of Margaret Douglas and later the Rutland household, with contributions by Thomas Wyatt, Mary Shelton and others. Diplomatic transcription, modernised text and scholarly apparatus, encoded in TEI P5. The original dedicated site (devonshire.unb.ca) is offline; the social edition now lives on Wikibooks, and the ~200 TEI XML transcriptions and witnesses (CC BY-SA 4.0) are archived at Oxford LLDS: https://llds.phon.ox.ac.uk/llds/xmlui/handle/20.500.14106/2587

The counts cover the 186 poem and item files of the manuscript, not the 288 witness files.

derived.sort_title: old romanian manuscripts on wikisource (codex sturdzanus, manuscrisul de la ieud)
derived.notes_display: Four pages of Old Romanian religious texts transcribed on Romanian Wikisource: 'Povestea Sfintei Dumineci' from the Codex Sturdzanus (copied by priest Grigore of Măhaci, 1580-1619) and three texts from the Manuscrisul de la Ieud (c. 1630). Not related to the journal Diacronia.

derived.sort_title: diacu — a dataset for the diachronic analysis of church slavonic
derived.notes_display: DIACU v1.0 (GitHub repo, description 'A dataset for the DIAchronic analysis of Church Slavonic, version 1.0') aggregates documents from Old Church Slavonic to Ruthenian, including 15th-century Bulgarian manuscripts distributed by Sofia University's historical dictionary / Cyrillomethodiana collections, matching the Late-15th-c. Bulgarian homilies of the collection (Homilia Domini nostri Iesu Christi de quid et quo..., Vita Hilarionis Moglen...). 3 texts retained. The data are distributed as a single JSON file (data/DIACU_1.0.json, about 22.8 MB, 652 documents), whose Content fields hold plain text. No explicit licence in repo metadata.

derived.sort_title: diakorp v6: diachronic corpus of czech
derived.notes_display: Diakorp v6 (~3.45M words, 116 documents, 14th-20th c., normalized transcriptions with original spellings) is officially deposited on LINDAT/CLARIAH-CZ with a persistent identifier, distributed in a CQP-vertical format (not TEI). The 7 collected texts (Kabátník's Cesta z Čech..., Komenský's Labyrint...) are among its 116 source documents. Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

derived.sort_title: dibilit-korpus (digitale bibliothek, literatur)
derived.notes_display: DiBiLit is the BBAW/DTA homogenized corpus of 2,000+ texts derived from the 'Digitale Bibliothek' (DirectMedia/Zeno.org), DTABf-encoded (TEI P5 subformat), CC BY-SA 4.0, with genre folders including drama; presentation page https://www.deutschestextarchiv.de/dibilit/. The 24 collected early German drama/Schwank texts (ayrer: Sidea, Theseus; gengenbach; opitz) match its drama files.

derived.sort_title: dibiphil — corpus of philosophical texts from zeno's digital library
derived.notes_display: Companion corpus of the Deutsches Textarchiv (BBAW), curated from the philosophical writings of Directmedia's Digitale Bibliothek on Zeno.org and encoded in DTABf/TEI; licence CC BY-SA 4.0. The whole corpus covers the 15th to 20th centuries; this entry covers its early modern texts, e.g. Böhme's 'Aurora oder Morgenröte im Aufgang' (1612) and Paracelsus treatises. The corpus can be searched at https://ddc.dwds.de/dstar/dibiphil/.

derived.sort_title: das kloster-tagebuch des einsiedler paters joseph dietrich, 1670-1704 – kommentierte online-edition
derived.notes_display: The diary has 18 volumes and about 12,000 pages; a diplomatic transcription with footnotes, Latin translations, weather observations and registers is published volume by volume. Four volumes are online so far: Band 6 (1687-1688), Band 13 (1688-1690), Band 15 (1693-1694) and Band 17 (1697-1698); all are within the period. The others are transcribed but not yet published. Band 17 and a new full-text search were added on 9 October 2026. The counts cover the four published volumes of 18, each counted as one text.

derived.sort_title: digilib armenian
derived.notes_display: Digital Library of Armenian Literature (DIGILIB) of the American University of Armenia, a web library of Armenian-language texts arranged by theme (historiography, philosophy, theology, law, sciences, travel, epistles and others) and by author. It has been operating since 1999 and describes its aim as collecting, digitizing, preserving and presenting material from Armenian national repositories. The texts are shown as HTML pages in the reader; the 17th-century printed works in the catalogue are among them. The About, site and staff subpages could not be retrieved in detail on 2026-10-13.

derived.sort_title: digital donne project
derived.notes_display: The site presents the electronic texts of the Donne Variorum Edition of the Poetry of John Donne (version 2.0, prepared 2025) as web pages, with plain-text transcriptions of the source texts at drc.usask.ca/archive/transcriptions/. The TEI file at the data link is an unlinked working draft of the poems based on the 1633 text, not the edited texts of version 2.0; the XML of those texts is not publicly retrievable.

derived.sort_title: digital renaissance editions
derived.notes_display: Scholarly editions of early English plays and interludes, each with a diplomatic (old-spelling) transcription of the early printed or manuscript witness next to a modern-spelling text. Three peer-reviewed editions are complete (The Honest Whore, Parts 1 and 2, and An Humorous Day's Mirth); the Annex adds about 18 further proofread, unreviewed old-spelling play texts (for example Cambyses, Arden of Faversham, Fair Em, Mankind-era interludes). Everything is readable online without login. The content pages record 'Last Modified' dates of 2014-2015 and the Annex text folders on the server date from 2021-07-14, with nothing newer found, so it is marked archived. Copyright policy: free for educational, non-profit use. The same site is also listed under its http:// address. The counts cover the old-spelling documents whose text is served on the live site (18 of the 19 found), and those whose title gives no year are not counted in the period.

derived.sort_title: digital scholarly edition of angelo poliziano's marginal notes to the epistle of sappho to phaon
derived.notes_display: EVT 2-based digital scholarly edition encoding multiple edition levels of Poliziano's manuscript annotations on the Epistle of Sappho to Phaon, with Wikidata items and CTS URNs; the dataset is also deposited on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17315766). It is a single-work edition, but carries a full scholarly apparatus (diplomatic and critical layers, apparatus of marks), so it is included despite the single-author caveat. The edition (238 marginal notes) is counted as one text. It is peer-reviewed (Journal of Open Humanities Data, 2025).

derived.sort_title: deutsche inschriften online (dio)
derived.notes_display: Edition of the printed series Die Deutschen Inschriften (Latin and German inscriptions up to 1650, some volumes later; whole database 31,197 articles dated 401-2022, of which 80 undated). Full transcriptions are published as EpiDoc only for DI 7 Braunschweig, DI 77 Greifswald and DI 102 Stralsund (978 articles). Other EpiDoc volumes are announced. The portal www.inschriften.net sits behind an Anubis bot check (returns a challenge page to curl), so its content was checked via the Epigraf dumps page, not the portal. Includes Austrian volumes of the Munich/Mainz series; the separate Viennese series (see oeaw-inschriften-wiener-reihe) is not part of it. The counts cover only the three volumes with published transcriptions (978 of 31,197 articles), and many dates are approximate.

derived.sort_title: die internuntiatur des johann rudolf schmid zum schwarzenhorn (1649): reisebericht, instruktionen, korrespondenz, berichte
derived.notes_display: Edition of the diary (Reisebericht) of Johann Georg Metzger, who accompanied the imperial internuncio Schmid zum Schwarzenhorn to Constantinople from December 1648 to September 1649, together with the instruction and secondary instruction, 26 letters to Emperor Ferdinand III, a final report and a secret report, with registers and commentary. The TEI for each object is served at /o:dipko.<id>/TEI_SOURCE (travel diary: o:dipko.rb). The site states a project term of 2017-2021 and shows nothing newer, so it is listed as archived.

derived.sort_title: disco: diachronic spanish sonnet corpus
derived.notes_display: DISCO is the Diachronic Spanish Sonnet Corpus of ~4,500 Spanish sonnets 15th–20th c. in XML-TEI with metrical annotation and VIAF-linked metadata; the Golden Age subcorpus (15th–17th c.) deliberately includes minor/non-canonical authors, exactly matching the harvest reference 'DISCO Golden Age minor-author sonnets' (150 texts). Distributed under CC-BY 4.0 via GitHub and Zenodo (zenodo.org/records/7604914). The former project site editionsdisco.com no longer resolves (checked Oct 2026), but the project site is mirrored at prf1.org/disco/about.html.

derived.sort_title: die chronyk van hollandt, zeelandt ende vriesland (divisiekroniek) of cornelius aurelius, 1517
derived.notes_display: Reader with page images and a transcription of the 1517 Leiden edition (Jan Seversz; copy in the Koninklijke Bibliotheek, The Hague), a history of Holland, Zeeland and Friesland from earliest times to 1517. Description page modified February 2026. Its words could not be counted: the site refuses automated requests.

derived.sort_title: waruchiri (huarochiri manuscript), runasimi.de edition
derived.notes_display: Quechua text of the Huarochirí Manuscript (c. 1600) in the Runasimi.de reworking, with revised spelling, based on Gerald Taylor's 1976 edition 'Ritos y Tradiciones de Huarochirí'. The same manuscript in Taylor's 1987 edition is catalogued separately as huarochiri-quechua-full.

derived.sort_title: documenta catholica omnia
derived.notes_display: Multilingual online collection of writings of popes, councils, Church Fathers, doctors and other Catholic authors from the apostolic age to the present, arranged by topic, author and period (the catalogue uses the section for 1500-1599 and 1600-1699). It is run by the Cooperatorum Veritatis Societas, a non-profit association of lay Catholics. Each work is offered as a single downloadable *.doc or *.pdf file, drawn from public-domain printed versions, checked against the originals and re-typeset by the site; Latin, Greek and vernacular texts are kept in their original language. The site is still being extended.

derived.sort_title: dost olderscots
le catechisme kikongo de 1624 (doutrina christaa): critical reissue (f. bontinck & n. ndembe nsasi)
derived.notes_display: Critical reissue of the Kikongo text of Mateus Cardoso's Doutrina Christãa (Lisbon, 1624), the first printed book in a Bantu language, by François Bontinck and Ndembe Nsasi, published by the Royal Academy for Overseas Sciences.

derived.sort_title: dracor
derived.notes_display: The Neo-Latin plays (NeoLatDraCor, 21 of the texts) are not on the production platform dracor.org; they are served at staging.dracor.org and in the GitHub repository dracor-org/neolatdracor (https://github.com/dracor-org/neolatdracor).

derived.sort_title: digitale ratoromanische chrestomathie (biblioteca digitala)
derived.notes_display: DFG project (2009–2011) at the Universität zu Köln that digitized and deep-indexed Caspar Decurtins' 'Rätoromanische Chrestomathie' (~7,500 pages of Romansh texts), published as the 'Biblioteca Digitala' full-text corpus; data preservation is now with the Data Center for the Humanities (dch.phil-fak.uni-koeln.de). The harvest covers Decurtins vol. V (Engadine 16th-c. authors Travers, Bifrun, Chiampell, Planta, Papa). Caveat: the crestomazia server deliberately answers HTTP 418 (anti-crawler 'teapot') to non-browser clients so verify interactively in a browser. Text units are OCR'd chapters, not TEI.

derived.sort_title: henrik smith: lægebøger (1577), scholarly online edition (tekstnet.dk / dsl)
derived.notes_display: The collection is DSL/tekstnet.dk's scientific online edition of Henrik Smid's six medical books (the posthumous 1577 edition), edited by Simon Skovgaard Boeck with Anne Mette Hansen and Ebba Hjorth; text transcribed from digital photographs in cooperation with the Universität Trier. The three harvested texts correspond word-for-word to the origin ids 'smith-h_1-laegebog-top-til-taa (1577)' etc., verified live at tekstnet.dk/books/smith-h_1-laegebog-top-til-taa/. tekstnet.dk is DSL's portal for Old Danish text editions.

derived.sort_title: reformationstidens danske salme- og messeboeger digitaliseret (salmer.dsl.dk)
derived.notes_display: DSL project 'Musik og sprog i reformationstidens danske salmesang' (Carlsberg-funded) digitally published nine Danish hymnals and mass books of the Reformation era, 1529–1573; the four texts (christian-3-bibel 1550, claus-mortensen-messe-1529, dietz-salmebog-1529/1536, jespersen_1573) match the source slugs exactly. Texts are served as TEI/XML from DSL's eXist-db, with companion portals melodier.dsl.dk and ordnet.dk/ren; project page at dsl.dk/projekter/musik-og-sprog-i-reformationstidens-danske-salmesang.

derived.sort_title: deutsches textarchiv (dta)
derived.notes_display: Texts of the Deutsches Textarchiv, plus the Luther Bible (1545, last hand; 76 texts), which is not a DTA text: it comes from an OSIS edition (2012) published at lutherbibel.net, a site that now returns HTTP 410 (gone).

derived.sort_title: early americas digital archive (eada)
derived.notes_display: Collection of electronic texts originally written in or about the Americas from 1492 to about 1820, stored as TEI and shown as HTML pages; about 134 text pages are preserved in the Wayback Machine. The part dating from 1450-1700 is the texts of the colonial period up to 1700 (for example the Plymouth Plantation history of William Bradford, written c. 1630-1650); later items such as Barlow's poems and Banneker's letter are eighteenth-century. The exact in-period share was not established. The live site is gone (eada.lib.umd.edu returns 400 Bad Request, checked 2026-10-13; last Wayback captures of the site are 2013-2015); the url is the Wayback copy. The TEI files are not downloadable from the archive. The counts cover the in-period texts among the 114 text pages captured by the Wayback Machine, in their original language; 27 modern English translations of Spanish and Dutch texts are not counted.

derived.sort_title: early nahuatl library (wired humanities projects)
derived.notes_display: Online library of colonial Nahuatl manuscripts with transcriptions and analytic translations; this entry counts a selection of 16 documents.

derived.sort_title: clarin:el resources of early modern greek (16th-17th century)
derived.notes_display: CLARIN:EL resource 'Resources of early modern Greek (16th-17th century)', a set of editions of notarial deeds (Alexakis, Olokalos) and literary and deed editions (Kapianos, Visvizis, Montselese's Evgena, 1646), distributed as MS Word .doc files.

derived.sort_title: english broadside ballad archive (ebba)
derived.notes_display: English Broadside Ballad Archive, a collection of English broadside ballads of the 16th to 18th centuries gathered from libraries such as the British Library, the National Library of Scotland, the Pepys collection at Magdalene College, the Beinecke, Houghton and Huntington libraries and others. Each ballad is offered as a sheet facsimile, a facsimile transcription (preserving the original layout), a plain text transcription and, where available, a recording of the tune, with detailed catalogue headings. A TEI-XML file with the transcription and metadata can be downloaded from the transcription view of each ballad. The project began in 2003 under director Patricia Fumerton at the University of California, Santa Barbara (associate director Carl Stahmer), and has received repeated National Endowment for the Humanities grants (NEH 1 to NEH 8, the latest for 2020-22). It is still described as a continuing project.

derived.sort_title: secrets of craft and nature in renaissance france (bnf ms fr 640)
derived.notes_display: Secrets of Craft and Nature in Renaissance France, the digital critical edition and English translation of BnF Ms. Fr. 640, a late 16th-century French artisanal manuscript held at the Bibliothèque nationale de France. The edition offers three versions of the text for each folio (transcription, normalised transcription and English translation) with commentary, glossary and manuscript images from Gallica. It was published in 2020 (DOI 10.7916/78yt-2v41) by the Making and Knowing Project at the Center for Science and Society, Columbia University, directed by Pamela H. Smith; the editors named in the edition's citation are Pamela H. Smith, Naomi Rosenkranz, Tianna Helena Uchacz, Tillmann Taape, Clément Godbarge, Sophie Pitman, Jenny Boulboullé, Joel Klein, Donna Bilak, Marc Smith and Terry Catapano. The edition's XML sources and derived files are on GitHub, with a Zenodo release.

derived.sort_title: eebo text creation partnership
derived.notes_display: Keyed and corrected TEI XML transcriptions of Early English Books Online (EEBO) texts. Produces scholarly digital editions of early printed books. EEBO-TCP Phase I and II texts have been free of restrictions since 1 August 2020 (CC0).

derived.sort_title: effectus amoris: network critical edition of a 16th-century hungarian verse romance
derived.notes_display: Hungarian verse romance (széphistória) surviving only as damaged printed leaves from a Debrecen print of 1587-1588. Three free text versions: a letter-faithful critical transcription, a pronunciation-oriented text and a modern-language text, plus photographs. The site is a hand-made 1998-99 HTML publication; the server reports a last modification in 2006 and no later change was found.

derived.sort_title: egpa — escritorio galego-portugues antigo
derived.notes_display: Open collaborative platform of transcribed Galician-Portuguese archival documents (EGPAdoc) and literary texts (EGPAlit) from the Middle Ages to the 19th century, with paleographic and critical presentation; freely readable without login; per-document TEI at corpora.uah.es/egpa/xmlfiles/<id>.xml (checked EGPAdoc-0061); the public file list at index.php?action=files also includes test files (prueba_*). Most material is 12th-15th century; only a handful of documents dated 1478-1566 fall within 1450-1700. The counts cover the 5 documents dated within 1450-1700, and 20 documents without a date in the header are not counted.

derived.sort_title: crenum - edition numerique de la chronique francaise de guillaume cretin
derived.notes_display: CreNum is the ELAN (Grenoble) digital XML-TEI edition of Guillaume Crétin's Chronique française (five books, 1515 edition), edited by Antoine Brix and Ellen Delvallée with the ELAN team. The edition is published at crenum.elan-numerique.fr; the TEI sources are in the project's GitLab repository (gricad-gitlab.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/elan/crenum), which shows a bot-check page to browsers.

derived.sort_title: fnvr - fictions narratives en vers de la renaissance (1490-1600)
derived.notes_display: FNVR is a Litt&Arts (Grenoble) project building XML-TEI editions of French verse narratives composed or translated 1490-1600, some first modern editions, led by Pascale Mounier; the TEI dataset is openly published on Recherche Data Gouv (DOI 10.57745/SSC5XT). The collected texts (amantDesconforte, chevallier, palamon, rondeaux) match the repository layout on the Grenoble GitLab, whose project page is live.

derived.sort_title: poly-grenaille - edition numerique des oeuvres morales de francois de grenaille
derived.notes_display: POLY-GRENAILLE is the digital critical edition of the moral works of François de Grenaille, published on the ELAN platform (UMR Litt&Arts, Grenoble) with TEI encoding and critical annotation. The edition is in progress: so far one work is edited in TEI, La Mode (Paris 1642); the site menu already lists about ten further works (Le bon esprit, L'honnête fille, L'honnête mariage, L'honnête veuve...).

derived.sort_title: la correspondance du chancelier antoine du bourg (1535-1538), ecole des chartes (elec)
derived.notes_display: Letters of Francis I and others to Antoine Du Bourg, chancellor of France, with a short inquiry on the Great Bible of 1536-1537. Each text is readable online without login and the complete TEI XML source is served at the data link. The edition has 95 letters plus the Great Bible inquiry, all dated 1536-1538. The TEI history ends in March 2012 and the server files date from July 2012; no later change found, so the edition is marked archived.

derived.sort_title: les edits de pacification et l'edit de nantes (1562-1598), ecole des chartes (elec)
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of the main edicts and treaties that ended the French Wars of Religion, from the Edict of January 1562 to the Edict of Nantes of 1598, set out article by article from the registers of the Parlement of Paris and the two sealed originals of the Edict of Nantes. Readable online without login; the TEI XML is offered on the downloads page. The 15 texts are edicts, treaties and conference articles. The TEI history ends in 2009 and the server file dates from June 2012, so the edition is marked archived.

derived.sort_title: emblem project utrecht
derived.notes_display: Dutch love emblem books of the seventeenth century (about 27 books, c. 1601 to 1724, secular and religious, by Heinsius, Vaenius, Hooft, Cats, Hugo, Luyken and others). Each book has full transcriptions, page facsimiles, indexes and concordances, an editorial introduction and Iconclass-based search and comparison tools, stored in an XML (TEI) database. The Emblem Project Utrecht was a joint effort of Utrecht University (Faculty of Arts, OGC, University Library), the Koninklijke Bibliotheek, DBNL and the Emblem Digitization Project; NWO funded it from November 2003 to November 2006 (project coordination E. Stronks). Texts are viewed as HTML on the site; no bulk download is offered, and the site continues to be online.

derived.sort_title: emlap
derived.notes_display: EMLAP (Early Modern Latin Alchemical Prints) is a text-based corpus of 100 Latin alchemical and Paracelsian volumes printed between 1500 and 1650. The texts were transcribed with Transkribus (first with the Noscemus GM6 model, then a project-trained model) and edited by hand, then tokenised, lemmatised and POS-tagged and exported as TEI P5 XML and plain text. The corpus was created in the TOME project (PI Petr Pavlas, Institute of Philosophy, Czech Academy of Sciences; Digital-Philological group led by Georgiana Hedesan), funded by the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (September 2023 to August 2025). It can be searched on the website and is released on Zenodo (record from February 2026); the lemmatised XML files are also served from the University of West Bohemia.

derived.sort_title: emmo: early modern manuscripts online
derived.notes_display: EMMO is the Folger Shakespeare Library's IMLS-funded project giving web access to TEI P5 transcriptions, images and metadata of 16th- and 17th-century English manuscripts, with diplomatic/semi-diplomatic/regularized text flavors and a downloadable XML corpus; the site documents exactly '100 transcribed documents'. Crowdsourced transcription ran on Dromio (transcribe.folger.edu); the IMLS grant concluded, leaving the site a preserved static resource.

derived.sort_title: emothe - teatro europeo de los siglos xvi y xvii: patrimonio y bases de datos
derived.notes_display: EMOTHE at the Universitat de València studies and edits the canon of early modern European theatre (Italian, English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, 16th–17th c.); its digital library has ~350 TEI-XML editions (originales y traducciones) with ids like EMOTHE0357, EMOTHE0382. TEI files (TEI-All validated) are openly distributed via GitLab (gitlab.com/emothe/emothe-research-project) and the Zenodo community zenodo.org/communities/emothe; workflow is FileMaker + oXygen, not TEITOK.

derived.sort_title: early modern recipes online collective (emroc)
derived.notes_display: Early modern recipe books is a FromThePage collection of digitised manuscript recipe books from the 16th to 18th centuries (45 works at the time of checking), a collaboration between the Folger Shakespeare Library (Washington, DC) and the Wellcome Collection (London), with volumes from other repositories such as the College of Physicians of Philadelphia. It was funded by a grant to the Folger from the University of Sheffield as part of the AHRC-funded US-UK Food Digital Scholarship Network, and aims to give repositories a free platform for crowdsourced transcription. The transcriptions are made page by page by volunteers and reviewed, and the works are exposed through IIIF manifests; completion varies from volume to volume and work is ongoing.

derived.sort_title: epicat: cartes familiars de catalunya (segles xvi-xix)
derived.notes_display: Catalogue and transcriptions of family correspondence in Catalan archives, 1500-1850; about 3,800 letters, mostly of the 18th and 19th centuries. Only 40 letters dated 1526-1699 (all showing a transcription on the page) fall in the period; the earliest is from 1526. Of these, 39 are in Catalan and 1 in Spanish. No bulk download. The site files were updated on 21 September 2026.

derived.sort_title: epidat – datenbank zur judischen grabsteinepigraphik
derived.notes_display: Jewish gravestone inscriptions (322 digital editions, 54,243 monuments on the site; monuments after 1956 withheld). EpiDoc TEI per monument (?id=<code>-teip5) and bulk in the public GitLab repository (xml/tei, tsv, json, ttl). The vast majority of the corpus is 18th-20th century. The in-period inscriptions are concentrated in Frankfurt (ffb 864), Hamburg-Altona (hha 270) and Worms (wrm 251). The older site interface is no longer developed; a beta interface exists. Repository last activity 2026-08-13. Inscriptions without a parseable year are not counted, and the transcriptions mix Hebrew with a German or Latin-script rendering, so word counts are approximate.

derived.sort_title: bibliotheques virtuelles humanistes — epistemon
derived.notes_display: Epistemon is the text database of the Bibliothèques Virtuelles Humanistes (BVH) programme at the Centre d'Études Supérieures de la Renaissance, Université de Tours (head: Rémi Jimenes). It offers Renaissance texts (literature and author corpora, literary manuscripts and 16th-century archival documents) transcribed in a 'patrimonial' manner that respects layout, spelling and punctuation, encoded in XML-TEI following the project's TEI-Renaissance guidelines. The first texts went online in 1998 at the University of Poitiers and moved to Tours in 2001; TEI encoding has been used since 2007. Texts are read and searched through XTF, PhiloLogic and TXM, with facsimiles shown alongside where available. Fidelity levels of older transcriptions are heterogeneous, and the base is still being extended and revised. It includes the Montaigne author corpus of the ANR MONLOE project (montaigne.univ-tours.fr): the genetic edition of the Exemplaire de Bordeaux of the 1588 Essais (also deposited on HAL, halshs-01239978), the 1580 edition of the Essais (books I and II), Montaigne's 1581 translation of Sebond's Théologie naturelle, La Boétie's Servitude volontaire (Bordeaux Ms 2199), letters and family archives; MONLOE's editions of Montaigne's marginalia and inscriptions are PDFs on the BVH server and are not counted. The counts combine two harvests that share no text: 70 texts from the BVH site and 46 printed texts from a legacy TEI copy in Lou Burnard's tei-fr repository on GitHub (last updated 2015).

derived.sort_title: erdy-kodex (sermones compilati research group, elte)
derived.notes_display: The Érdy codex, a Hungarian-language sermon and legend manuscript copied in 1526-1527, set out in a table with photographs of the manuscript pages, a letter-by-letter (diplomatic) transcription and related studies, plus a link to the 19th-century printed edition. At the time of checking, 108 pages are transcribed (pages 001-055 and 103-157); the rest of the critical edition is marked 'in preparation'. The server reports a last modification in 2014 for the page and nothing newer was found, so the resource is listed as archived. The Sermones site is still maintained for other projects such as the exempla database. The counts cover the 108 transcribed pages only, and the codex is counted as one text.

derived.sort_title: estilometria siglooro
derived.notes_display: Open GitHub corpus of Spanish Golden Age literature as plain-text (.txt) files for stylometry, in the Siglo_de_Oro folder: about 345 comedias, 66 novelas and 22 entremeses, plus a file of ballads by one author. The texts were harvested from public-domain sites: TC/12 (Red del Patrimonio Teatral Clásico Español), Teatro de los Siglos de Oro, the AHCT comedias.org text list, José Manuel Fradejas Rueda's NovelaBarroca repository (Universidad de Valladolid) and the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes. The repository also holds a separate set of novels from 1880-1940, outside the period. The README is dated September 2020 and the last commit in the repository is from January 2025; the contact is the company Publiconsulting.

derived.sort_title: etheridge project: an encomium on henry viii and elizabeth i by george etheridge (bl royal ms 16 c x)
derived.notes_display: Electronic edition of a Greek encomium in Etheridge's own hand, prepared for Elizabeth I's Oxford visit of 1566, with transcription, edited text with apparatus, English translation and manuscript images. Readable without login. Built with HTML and JavaScript only, no TEI. The server's file listing shows the most recent edits on 2023-03-20 and the edition page is dated 20 March 2023; no later change found, so it is marked archived.

derived.sort_title: digital edition of the ethica complementoria
derived.notes_display: Annika Rockenberger's GitHub project holds the TEI P5 transcriptions and analysis code for her digital scholarly edition of the 17th-c. German etiquette prints of the Ethica Complementoria tradition, part of the Greflinger digital edition project (https://greflinger.hypotheses.org/). The texts counted here are A3 (1648), C3 (1665), Complementierbüchlein (B6, 1660), Cochleatio Novissima (1656) and Klag und Trost (1652). The Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel published the accompanying bibliographical study (2017); the edition of the 1643 print is published at the Deutsches Textarchiv (https://www.deutschestextarchiv.de/nn_ethica_1643). The project has moved to the companion repository https://github.com/greflinger-dse/EthicaComplementoria; data on GitHub under CC-BY.

derived.sort_title: evans early american imprints (evans-tcp)
derived.notes_display: Roughly 5,000 transcribed English-language texts (books, pamphlets, broadsides and periodicals printed in America) selected from Readex's Evans Early American Imprints, which covers American imprints from 1639 to 1800. The transcriptions were produced by the Text Creation Partnership (TCP) with Readex (NewsBank) and the American Antiquarian Society; they are encoded as SGML/XML and were released into the public domain under a CC0 dedication, with copies distributed through the University of Michigan Library and the Oxford Text Archive. Access to the Readex page images was withdrawn in 2022; the text files remain available.

derived.sort_title: fabulas mitologicas del siglo de oro (ed. antonio rojas castro, github)
derived.notes_display: Antonio Rojas Castro's 2016 TEI-XML corpus of 26 Spanish Golden Age mythological fables (~150k words, CC BY 4.0), included here with witnesses Barahona de Soto's Acteón and Vértumno, Bermúdez's Narciso, Bocángel's Leandro, Carrillo's Acis; the repo is the canonical public source, with a companion publication in Studia Aurea (2017) and stylometry workshops built on this corpus.

derived.sort_title: tale of the fall of constantinople - parallel interlinear edition (obdurodon.org)
derived.notes_display: arranz.obdurodon.org hosts the interlinear collation digital edition of the East Slavic 'Povest' o vzjatii Car'grada' (Tale of the capture of Constantinople), developed by Isabel Arranz del Riego from her 2013 UCM dissertation and maintained by David J. Birnbaum with XML/RelaxNG files and the three Hilandar Monastery witnesses 281 (1561), 280 (1585) and 282 (1826) - the first two are exactly the harvested witnesses ('witness HM281 (1561)', 'witness HM280 (1585)'). Released under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

derived.sort_title: famsi bolles yucatecmaya
derived.notes_display: Texts, documents, rituals, recipes, songs and other material in Colonial Yucatec Maya (including sections from the Books of Chilam Balam and the Ritual of the Bacabs, with H-Men chants) typed by David Bolles for his Combined Dictionary-Concordance of the Yucatecan Mayan Language. The report was prepared in 1997 for the Foundation for the Advancement of Mesoamerican Studies (FAMSI) and published online as HTML pages and PDF files, with some items available as MP3. The texts are plain transcriptions copied as closely as possible from the sources, some reworked with footnotes; the last update noted on the index page is November 2004. FAMSI is now stewarded by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

derived.sort_title: edition der familienkorrespondenz ferdinands i. (family correspondence of ferdinand i)
derived.notes_display: Digital version of the first volume (1912, edited by Wilhelm Bauer) of the family correspondence of Ferdinand I, letters A1-A261 of 1514-1526; the later printed volumes (to 1536) and the letter lists for 1537-1564 are announced, not yet online. Each letter page gives the transcription with German and English summaries, notes and indexes, and a link to the TEI file (data/dtabf_id/band_001/A###.xml). The index lists 262 letter records; 201 carry transcribed text and 61 are asterisked entries with a summary or cross-reference only. The TEI headers state CC BY 3.0; the TEI files were last modified 1 October 2024.

derived.sort_title: filologiasarda sardinian
derived.notes_display: Digital reproduction (PDF) of Gerolamo Araolla's 'Rimas diversas spirituales' (original collection 1597), the spiritual verse of a Sardinian priest of Sassari, edited by Maurizio Virdis (Cuec, series Scrittori sardi, 2006, 510 pp.). It is published on the portal of the Centro di Studi Filologici Sardi (Cagliari), which offers the series as PDF files beside the print edition. The record is one entry in an ongoing series of editions of Sardinian authors.

derived.sort_title: transcript of the florentine codex (nahuatl)
derived.notes_display: Plain-text transcription of the Nahuatl text of Bernardino de Sahagun's Florentine Codex (General History of the Things of New Spain, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Florence), edited and deposited on Zenodo by Valery A. Berthoud F. The deposit has twelve text files, one per book, plus a readme; some special characters, such as the tilde, are missing. Version 1.0 was published on 16 October 2022 and the record was last modified in June 2025.

derived.sort_title: folger shakespeare (formerly folger digital texts)
derived.notes_display: All of Shakespeare's plays, the Sonnets and the narrative poems, read free online and downloadable as XML (TEI), TEI Simple with linguistic annotation (the 37 plays without the Two Noble Kinsmen and the poems), HTML, PDF, Word and plain text. These are the modern-spelling texts of the New Folger Editions (edited by Barbara Mowat and Paul Werstine), not diplomatic transcriptions of the early printings. The old address shakespeare.folger.edu now redirects to the Folger website. All the works date from the 1590s to 1613. The texts were last revised in 2021.

derived.sort_title: jacques de fonteny, livre d'enigmes: manuscript of an early 17th-century para-emblematic sonnet sequence (hab wolfenbuttel)
derived.notes_display: Manuscript (HAB Cod. Guelf. 117.5 Extrav.) of sonnet riddles, each with an engraving; the edition gives an original-spelling transcription with variants, a regularised version, introduction, commentary and facsimile. Readable and downloadable without login: the TEI files tei-transcript-fr-or.xml (original spelling) and tei-transcript-fr.xml are served from the HAB server. The edition is dated 2012 and the TEI file was last modified on 2012-08-21, so it is marked archived.

derived.sort_title: fornsvenska textbanken (fsvtb): nysvenska annexet
derived.notes_display: Nysvenska annexet of Fornsvenska textbanken (Lund University): 26 machine-readable Swedish texts from 1526 onwards, such as Olaus Petri's chronicle, Peder Swart's chronicle, Gustav Vasa's Bible (1541), Anna Vasa's letters and Agneta Horn's memoir, most from the project 'Bidrag till en nysvensk textbank pa data'. Mats Thelander and Carin Ostman gave permission to publish them. The texts are keyed or scanned from printed editions and proofread unevenly, so the site advises against quoting them and recommends them for word, phrase and statistical searches. The page was last updated on 2 September 2026.

derived.sort_title: korpus 16: korpus besedil slovenskih protestantskih piscev 16. stoletja
derived.notes_display: Corpus of the texts of 16th-century Slovenian Protestant writers (Trubar, Dalmatin, Krelj, Juricic and others): transcriptions of 45 printed books on 12,945 pages, from catechisms, psalters and postils to Dalmatin's Bible of 1584. The texts were double-keyed by CyberData India, checked against the sources and converted to TEI XML. Edited by Kozma Ahacic for the Institut za slovenski jezik Frana Ramovsa ZRC SAZU and published by Zalozba ZRC in 2019 as version 1.0 in the Fran collection, with funding from the Slovenian ministries and ARRS projects. The corpus is searchable and readable page by page online, and the colophon announces deposit in CLARIN.SI.

derived.sort_title: freem (french early modern corpus)
derived.notes_display: FreEM (Early Modern French corpora) is a project led by Simon Gabay (University of Geneva) with Inria Paris colleagues, building corpora and NLP models for French of the 16th-18th centuries. The text corpus is FreEMmax, a large collection of historical French texts assembled to train language models (it underlies D'AlemBERT, presented at LREC 2022); the open-access version, FreEMmax_OA, was published on GitHub and Zenodo in April 2022 (v1.0.0, later 1.0.2). It contains source documents in mixed formats plus minimal TEI/XML transcriptions and cleaned plain text built by a script, with teiHeaders carrying metadata. A non-open version exists that cannot be distributed.

derived.sort_title: briefe der fruchtbringenden gesellschaft und beilagen: die zeit furst ludwigs von anhalt-kothen 1617-1650, band 1: 1617-1626 (hab wolfenbuttel)
derived.notes_display: Electronic TEI P5 edition of the first volume of the letters and enclosures of the Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft (Fruitbearing Society), a German literary and linguistic society, from the printed edition of 1992. Readable and downloadable without login: the METS file lists each letter's TEI file (briefe/*.xml). The 91 letter files are dated 1617-1626. The online edition is dated 2014 and the files were last modified between 2015 and 2018, so it is marked archived. Later volumes (1627-1650) are not part of this record.

derived.sort_title: fruhneuzeitliche furstinnenkorrespondenzen (fuerstinnenkorrespondenz corpus, laudatio)
derived.notes_display: DFG project on the letter corpora of early modern princely women of the central German area (~5,500 letters in 24 correspondences; the published corpus v1.1 has ~250k tokens of 16th-c. princesses' letters), published in the LAUDATIO repository with TEI plus morphological/POS annotation, queryable in ANNIS. Related Anhalt/Thuringia letter materials sit in ThULB Jena 'Digitale Fürstinnenkorrespondenzen' collections; a BBAW reuse experiment by Stefan Dumont confirms the free licence of the TEI data.

derived.sort_title: galileo galilei, notes on motion (ms. gal. 72): electronic representation of the manuscript
derived.notes_display: Galileo's working papers on motion and mechanics (folios 33-196 of Ms. Gal. 72): short texts, drafts for the Discorsi, calculations and tables. Each folio side has a transcription of the final text, plus levels showing the genetic apparatus, with indices. Readable without login after clicking a notice that accepts the conditions (images may not be published without the library's permission). The pages are marked Version 2.2 of 10 May 1999 and no later change was found. The folio sides are undated and are counted as falling within 1450-1700 because the papers document work from about 1590 to 1637.

derived.sort_title: galileo opere favaro
derived.notes_display: Italian Wikisource project transcribing Antonio Favaro's Edizione Nazionale of Galileo's works (Le opere di Galileo Galilei, 20 volumes, Florence, Barbera, 1890-1909). It is incomplete: the index page is tagged at 25% proofreading, only volume I is linked to its scanned source and volumes X-XX have no pages yet. Texts are wiki transcriptions proofread by volunteers against the scans and are available through Wikisource and its Wikimedia dumps. The page was last edited in May 2026.

derived.sort_title: jahrrechnungen der stadt basel 1535–1610 (basel records) — digital edition
derived.notes_display: Jahrrechnungen der Stadt Basel 1535-1610: a digital edition of the annual city accounts of Basel, 76 objects (one per year from 1535/36 to 1609/10; 1584/85 is missing), from the Staatsarchiv Basel-Stadt (series Finanz H). Edited by Susanna Burghartz with Sonia Calvi, Lukas Meili, Jonas Sagelsdorff and Georg Vogeler; part of DEPCHA (Digital Edition Publishing Cooperative for Historical Accounts), hosted on GAMS at the University of Graz (ZIM-ACDH) with the Mellon-funded DEPCHA partners. Each year is published as an HTML edition with TEI-XML and RDF, and bulk downloads of all TEI and RDF files are offered; objects are dated 30 March 2023.

derived.sort_title: ganjoor (گنجور) — persian poetry library
derived.notes_display: Ganjoor is a Persian poetry website and database of classical Persian poets and their poems; the Renascor record covers the part of the content dated 1466-1700. It was started by an individual hobbyist and moved to ganjoor.net in 2007/8; it is not tied to any institution or commercial body. Poems are typed by volunteers mostly from free sources, with sources listed on the Sources page. The data is exported periodically as a database and, as of 2026-10-13, as a public git-tracked JSON repository (about 240 poets and 135,000 poems) on GitHub.

derived.sort_title: nottingham corpus of early modern german midwifery and women's medicine, ca. 1500–1700 (gemi, ota 2562)
derived.notes_display: Whitt's GeMi corpus (Oxford Text Archive 2562, published 2016) holds 12 German midwifery and women's-medicine texts ca. 1500–1700 (Rösslin's Rosengarten, the anonymous Frauenbüchlein ca. 1500, Rüff's Trostbüchlein, HoffWeheMutter, HebammenBuch...) as paired plain-text and TEI XML files plus a manual. Transcriptions derive mostly from the Würzburg 'Digitale Volltexte' Gynäkologie collection; CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The record is now held on the Oxford Text Archive's repository server (llds.ling-phil.ox.ac.uk); the older ota.ox.ac.uk/desc/2562 address no longer works, and the repository shows a bot-check page before the record in a browser.

derived.sort_title: germanc - historical corpus of german 1650-1800 (ota 2544)
derived.notes_display: GerManC is a manually annotated, genre-balanced corpus of Early Modern German (1650-1800), built at the University of Manchester and distributed through the Oxford Text Archive (record ota:2544) under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The catalogue entry covers the texts of 1654-1700 (drama, humanities, legal, narrative, newspapers, scientific and sermon texts). The former project site no longer responds, and the Oxford Text Archive pages sit behind an anti-bot check, so they may need a browser.

derived.sort_title: glasgow university emblem website (alciato and french emblems projects)
derived.notes_display: Glasgow University Emblem Website: digitised emblem books from the Stirling Maxwell Collection of Glasgow University Library, with transcribed texts, translations and images. It brings together the French Emblems project, the Italian emblem project, and the Alciato project (about 17 editions of the Emblematum liber, 1531-1621), plus an edition of Mignault's treatise on the emblem with parallel English text by Denis Drysdall. It is run by the University of Glasgow (Special Collections and the Stirling Maxwell Centre; contacts Laurence Grove, Luis Gomes, Alison Adams) with partners including Emblematica Online, the Universidade da Coruna and the Herzog August Bibliothek. The site is still online as HTML pages.

derived.sort_title: gondomar: corpus dixital de textos galegos da idade moderna
derived.notes_display: The online corpus holds 84 texts up to 1791; this entry counts only the 31 texts dated 1594-1697.

derived.sort_title: soledades. edicion digital (luis de gongora, 1613) — ed. antonio rojas castro
derived.notes_display: TEI encodings and datasets supporting the digital edition of Góngora's Soledades (1613) in the arojascastro/soledades GitHub repository: an annotated edition (soledades_anotada.xml), a critical edition (soledades_critica.xml) and simple transcriptions. The Renascor Corpus harvest labelled this set 'GitHubTEI'.

derived.sort_title: obras de gongora (obra poetica, ed. antonio carreira) — labex obvil gongora project
derived.notes_display: The OBVIL GONGORA project digitised Antonio Carreira's edition of Góngora's poetic works and the polémica gongorina in TEI P5 (2013-2016, CC BY-NC-ND). The TEI files are published in the gongoradigital GitHub repository gongoraobra, which holds the poetry, the Epistolario and three comedias. The catalogue statistics cover only two of these texts, the Epistolario (1610) and the Comedia venatoria (1605). The original OBVIL portal is no longer reachable.

derived.sort_title: grand tour digital — tei dataset of early modern travel testimonies (grand tour tei)
derived.notes_display: TEI-XML files underlying the digital edition of a corpus of early modern travel testimonies (Reiseselbstzeugnisse). Full text was created with Transkribus HTR plus NER, i.e. project-released corrected machine text, published as an open dataset (CC BY-SA 4.0) on 30 September 2026. The corpus spans the 16th–18th centuries, so only part falls within the catalogue window; the edition website is http://selbstzeugnisse.hab.de/edition_grand_tour, and the Zenodo deposit (with the git.hab.de repository it points to) is the stable access point for the TEI files. The counts cover the four travel journals in the deposit, of which three are dated within 1450-1700 (the fourth is dated 1701-1702).

derived.sort_title: correspondence of hugo grotius (huygens institute, elaborate)
derived.notes_display: Digital version of the printed Briefwisseling van Hugo de Groot (letters written and received by Grotius from 1597 to 1645), with an introduction, name and quotation indices and the editors' Dutch notes. Every letter is readable online without login and can be browsed by year, sender or recipient. The site states 'basic digital version, October 2009'; its newest style file is dated 2023-07-04 and nothing newer was found, so it is marked archived.

derived.sort_title: storia d'italia (francesco guicciardini): analytical digital edition of the opening passage
derived.notes_display: Semi-diplomatic transcriptions, beside facsimiles, of the successive drafts of the opening passage (exordium) of Guicciardini's History of Italy in eight manuscripts (family archive and Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Florence). Only the opening is edited so far; the project hopes to extend it. The site was last changed in 2021 (server dates 2019-2021) and no extension has appeared since. The 14 transcribed sections carry no dates, so their place within 1450-1700 rests on the dating of the drafts to 1537-1540.

derived.sort_title: gwaith guto'r glyn (guto'r glyn.net)
derived.notes_display: Gutorglyn is the digital edition of the poems of Guto'r Glyn (c. 1435-c. 1493), edited at the Centre for Advanced Welsh and Celtic Studies (University of Wales) by a team led by Ann Parry Owen, with editors Iestyn Daniel, Alaw Mai Edwards, Dafydd Johnston, Barry Lewis and Eurig Salisbury, encoding editor Jenny Day and web officer Alexander L. Roberts (Swansea University). It was funded over five years by the AHRC and the University of Wales, in partnership with the National Library of Wales and the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales, which supplied manuscript images. The site presents each poem with its editor named, lists of patrons, names, places and manuscripts, and audio performances; a GitHub repository holds the site code and its XML text files. Copyright year of the site: 2013.

derived.sort_title: h15corpus (historia15, universidad de sevilla)
derived.notes_display: Corpus of letters 'escritas en España ... en el tramo 1450 a 1600' (project description), 'en construcción'; the status page says 394 editions (the TEITOK statistics page lists 410 documents on 2026-10-12). Dated documents run from c. 1500 to 1598, with one dated 1417; 73 documents of the Bolea collection carry no date. Collections include Bolea, Granvela and Vizcaya. Raw TEI XML is served per document. The counts cover the 402 files of the directory, leaving out 12 test files, and documents without a date are not counted in the period.

derived.sort_title: philipp hainhofer: das große stammbuch (annotated digital edition)
derived.notes_display: Annotated edition of the album amicorum of the Augsburg merchant and art agent Philipp Hainhofer: 228 numbered pages of parchment and paper with entries (signatures, mottoes, dedications, coats of arms) dated 1596-1633, with translations, commentary and indexes. Downloads: TEI P5 XML of the full edition, a plain-text file of the transcription, PDF, and registers. The site went online 29 August 2024; the project closed 30 November 2024 and the last small corrections are dated 29 July 2025. The counts cover the 96 pages that carry a transcription, and the others are blank or only picture descriptions.

derived.sort_title: hamletworks (hamletworks.org): the enfolded hamlet and hamlet textual notes
derived.notes_display: Research site for Shakespeare's Hamlet. It offers the 'Enfolded Hamlet' (Bernice Kliman, 1996) as linked texts of the Second Quarto (1604/5) and the First Folio (1623) in exact original spelling, a modern enfolded text, line-by-line commentary and textual notes, and diplomatic versions of the First Quarto (1603) and Sixth Quarto as PDF/DjVu files, plus later editions and promptbooks. The domain redirects to a different host name (server-66-113-234-189.da.direct). The introduction page was last modified in February 2025. Copyright is held by the editors; reading is free. The counts cover the Q2 and F1 transcriptions only, since the Q1 and Q6 versions exist only as PDF or DjVu images.

derived.sort_title: hartlib papers (samuel hartlib, c. 1600-1662)
derived.notes_display: Correspondence, diaries and papers of the 'intelligencer' Samuel Hartlib (Sheffield University Library MS 61), with full-text transcriptions and facsimiles of over 25,000 folios; the open online edition dates from 2013. The site opens with a short automatic browser check. The transcriptions are downloadable as hartlib-txt.zip (5,740 .txt files: 5,234 main documents, 442 additional items, 64 pamphlets); the files are plain text carrying SGML/HTML-like layout and editorial tags (<DOC>, <HEADER>, <BLOCK>, <I>, <EDITOR>, <ADD>, <DEL>), not well-formed XML. Dated documents run from the 1630s to the 1660s (a handful earlier or later); about 1,600 files carry no date but belong to the same papers. The data service also offers a cleaned and lemmatised version (TXT and XML) made by the Alan Turing Institute, and the page images (1.8 GB). Undated files are not counted in the period.

derived.sort_title: hearth tax digital
derived.notes_display: Transcribed hearth tax returns and assessments from The National Archives and local record offices (Bristol, Cheshire, Essex, Kent, Lancashire, Norfolk, Norwich, Sussex, Warwickshire, Yorkshire and others), encoded in TEI with Latin text translated into English. The records list individuals by name, with hearth numbers, titles and occupations; the site counts 394,123 database entries. The 61 transcribed assessments are each downloadable as TEI from their record pages. Assessment years found in the titles run from 1662 to 1674. New records are still being added (last TEI revision date found: 22 July 2026). The counts cover the 61 assessments available as TEI, not the individual database entries.

derived.sort_title: henslowe-alleyn digitisation project
derived.notes_display: Digitised manuscripts of the Henslowe-Alleyn papers at Dulwich College (Philip Henslowe's diary and account book 1592-1609, the Rose and Fortune playhouse contracts, letters, deeds, Edward Alleyn's papers 1612-1626), with essays and a set of transcriptions. All the documents date from 1450-1700 (about 1587-1626). The transcriptions are PDF documents. Although the catalogue says the diary and account book is transcribed, Henslowe's diary (MSS 7) is given only as images; the transcribed items are seven documents and Alleyn's diary (MSS 9, 116 page transcripts). The counts cover the seven documents; Alleyn's diary, mostly sums of money, falls under the corpus filter for text with too few letters. The old address henslowe-alleyn.org.uk/index.html returns HTTP 500 but the root address works. Site footer reads 2026, maintained by King's Digital Lab. robots.txt asks for a 10-second crawl delay.

derived.sort_title: hexenverhoerprotokolle (sigs corpus, laudatio repository)
derived.notes_display: The SiGS corpus published in LAUDATIO holds Early New High German witch-trial interrogation protocols of 1570-1665 from the Macha et al. (2005) edition 'Deutsche Kanzleisprache in Hexenverhörprotokollen der Frühen Neuzeit'. The release (v1.0, 2023-06-01, about 98,700 tokens) has three parts: the Kernkorpus of 18 texts evenly spread over place and time, an extended corpus and a remainder; it is published as PAULA XML and relANNIS for ANNIS. Project page with corpus map: uni-muenster.de/SIGS-Projekt/corpus/index.html.

derived.sort_title: histcorp — historical corpora and tools (fornsvenska / fornsvenska textbanken)
derived.notes_display: HistCorp is an open platform for historical corpora and tools, distributed via the Swedish CLARIN node. Its Swedish section draws on Fornsvenska textbanken (machine-readable Old and Early Modern Swedish texts 1350-1758), which HistCorp supplies as plain text (txt and one-token-per-line tok files); the original Fornsvenska textbanken material is published as annotated XML by Språkbanken Text (https://doi.org/10.23695/pyqj-0s75). The source site (project2.sol.lu.se/fornsvenska) no longer resolves; the texts are available through the HistCorp Swedish download (Zenodo). The 5.6 M words exceed Fornsvenska's 44 texts and 1.4 M tokens, so the entry includes other HistCorp Swedish corpora; the texts counted here come from this download bundle. Freely available; the licence is CC BY. Related searchable corpora are offered by Språkbanken Text's Korp ('all_hist' mode).

derived.sort_title: histoire des albigeois (2nd half of the 15th century): critical edition (a. tondi, phd thesis)
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of the anonymous Occitan prose chronicle Histoire des Albigeois (Paris BnF witness, ms P), with a linguistic study, published as a doctoral thesis (PDF) in HAL; also listed on theses.fr (2019PSLEP014).

derived.sort_title: hooke folio online
derived.notes_display: Transcription, beside images, of the Hooke Folio, a manuscript volume of the Royal Society holding extracts from the Journal Books (April 1661 to June 1677) and the rough minutes made while Robert Hooke was secretary (1677-1691), plus supplementary papers and contemporary indexes. The text is on 573 transcribed pages (folios). Transcriptions were released in September 2007, with corrections and new images in April 2008, and no later project change is recorded. Free for personal use; the Royal Society images and the project's materials are copyright. The counts cover the pages that carry transcribed text, and 101 of the 679 pages requested had none.

derived.sort_title: hortus sanitatis : livre iv, les poissons (de piscibus) — edition en ligne
derived.notes_display: Online companion to the printed critical edition: the Latin Tractatus de piscibus (Book IV of the Hortus sanitatis, editio princeps by Meydenbach, Mainz 1491) with apparatus, a modern French translation, notes, an index and facsimiles of copies from Épernay and Valognes. The server shows the chapter pages last modified on 3 June 2022 and the home page on 10 January 2022, so it is listed as archived.

derived.sort_title: ritos y tradiciones de huarochiri (taylor 1987) — biblioteca digital curt nimuendaju
derived.notes_display: The collection is the single-text digitisation of Gerald Taylor's 1987 IEP/IFEA edition of the Huarochiri manuscript (Quechua, ca. 1608), held on the Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendaju at etnolinguistica.org (PDF verified live: https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/biblio%3Ataylor-1987-ritos/TaylorG_1987_RitosYTradicionesDeHuarochiri.pdf). The Renascor Corpus has only the reconstituted quechua text as plain text-derived 'keyed' material. Publicly downloadable; not a TEI project.

derived.sort_title: icepahc — icelandic parsed historical corpus
derived.notes_display: IcePaHC is the Iceland Parsed Historical Corpus treebank (Old/Norse-to-modern Icelandic span, texts 1350-1750+ for pre-1700), distributed on GitHub as .psd/.tagged/.txt files. The 21 Renascor Corpus files (bandamenn, ectorssaga, judit, vilhjalmur etc.) match the corpus .txt files exactly. Free public release; the linguist.is wiki site returned HTTP 511 from two networks, so the verified live canonical entry point is the GitHub repo. The Renascor Corpus collected from the raw txt layer (word-level parses dropped).

derived.sort_title: imp — digital library and corpus of historical slovene
derived.notes_display: IMP is the IMPACT-project digital library/corpus of historical Slovene (658 texts, 1584-1919), published as hand-corrected TEI P5 transcriptions with facsimile links and lemma/MTE morphology. CLARIN.SI handle 11356/1031 is exactly the Renascor Corpus source: it contains filenames such as 'ZRC_00001-1584-ana.xml' (Jurij Dalmatin's 1584 Bible) and 'ZRC_00002-1695-ana.xml' (Janez Svetokrski), matching the origin verbatim. License CC BY-SA 4.0 (CLARIN.SI); the site nl.ijs.si/imp is still online though the project completed in 2014.

derived.sort_title: impactes originalimprint
derived.notes_display: IMPACT-es is a diachronic corpus of historical Spanish with over one hundred books (about 8 million words) from the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes and ground-truth pages from the Spanish national libraries, with a complementary lexicon of more than 10,000 lemmas linked to variant forms; about 7% of the words carry lemma, part of speech and modern equivalent. It was produced by the Universidad de Alicante and the Fundacion Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes within the IMPACT project, described by Sanchez-Martinez, Martinez-Sempere, Ivars-Ribes and Carrasco in Language Resources and Evaluation. The ground-truth files (works by Cervantes, Lope, Calderon, Garcilaso, Quevedo and others, in 16 folders) are on GitHub (impactcentre/groundtruth-spa) and the corpus is offered as zipped XML with DTDs; no later changes were found.

derived.sort_title: inscriptiones alborum amicorum (iaa)
derived.notes_display: Database of entries (inscriptions, mottoes, dedications, signatures, owners' notes) in 16th-18th century alba amicorum with a Hungarian connection: entries by Hungarians or owners from Hungary, entries made in Hungary, and entries mentioning Hungary. Each record separates the date, place, motto, dedication, signature and quoted or composed inscription text, with scans where permitted. Record numbers run to about 17,090, and the database covers the 16th to the 18th century. Status active: copyright line 2003-2026 and the database is described as continuously growing. The counts cover the entries dated 1450-1700 that have transcribed text, and 327 entries with only metadata or notes are left out.

derived.sort_title: internet shakespeare editions (university of victoria)
