derived.notes_display: Open-access site with diplomatic old-spelling transcriptions of all 37 plays and the poems (quarto and folio versions) and, for 22 plays and most poems, modern-spelling editions prepared for the web, with facsimiles, performance and 'Life and Times' sections. The home page was last modified on 8 December 2022 and other pages date from 2015-2018 ('Accessed on 2019-01-11'); the publisher's follow-up work is on the Linked Early Modern Drama Online platform (lemdo.uvic.ca), which is a separate resource. This is the same resource as the old address http://internetshakespeare.uvic.ca/ (candidate 346). The counts cover the 67 old-spelling quarto and folio witnesses listed on the Texts index, not the modern-spelling editions.

derived.sort_title: acts and ordinances of the interregnum
derived.notes_display: The full text of the legislation passed into law during the Interregnum (1642-1660), over 900 acts and ordinances, from the edition by C. H. Firth and R. S. Rait (London, 1911, three volumes). British History Online presents the three volumes together, with tables of acts for each year and the editors' introduction. The text was digitised by double rekeying and is free to read on the site. British History Online is a not-for-profit digital library run by the Institute of Historical Research, University of London.

derived.sort_title: izbornyk ukrainian
derived.notes_display: Izbornyk (litopys.org.ua), 'History of Ukraine, 9th-18th centuries: primary sources and interpretations', an electronic library of early Ukrainian writing. It gathers chronicles, historical documents, lives of saints, grammars, lexicons, memoir prose and translated and poetic works, plus scholarly literature,. The project was started and is run by a single editor who signs as Maksym (Kyiv), with the main site opened on 1 October 2003 and a mirror at izbornyk.org.ua opened in 2008. The site is still online and carries visit statistics for 2016.

derived.sort_title: familiensache? die korrespondenz der kaiserin eleonora magdalena (1655–1720)

period.raw: 1677-1720 (letters sent by and to the empress)
period.note: letters sent by and to the empress

derived.notes_display: Digital edition of the letters of Empress Eleonora Magdalena of Pfalz-Neuburg (wife of Leopold I) with transcriptions, facsimiles, indexes, a calendar and PDF export; the TEI file of each letter is served at the letter's address with .xml instead of .html, and the working files are in the project's GitHub repository. Of the 1,605 letters listed in the edition's CMIF file of 24 September 2026, 472 date from 1701 to 1716. Language: German in nearly all letters (a few in other languages).

derived.sort_title: kritische gesamtausgabe der schriften und briefe andreas bodensteins von karlstadt
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of the writings and letters of the Wittenberg reformer Andreas Karlstadt, with a TEI transcript of each text (from printed works and manuscripts), commentary, German translations and facsimile links. The published part covers 1507 to 1518, 74 transcribed items. The TEI files are served one by one (for example texts/001/001_transcript.xml) with no bulk download, so no data link is given. The edition's files were last changed in 2017 and its METS record in April 2022. The HAB's terms allow private, scholarly use and forbid commercial use or republication.

derived.sort_title: das kirchenbuch zu groben (1578-1769)
derived.notes_display: Transcription, spread by spread (two pages per web page, with facsimile), of the church register begun in 1578: baptisms, marriages, burials, plus some inserted documents such as a letter of Melanchthon. The site covers 1578-1769; the part dated 1578-1700 is 248 page spreads (pages 1 to c. 505). The site footer reads © 2009 EKBO and its news feed was last updated on 18 March 2014, so it is listed as archived.

derived.sort_title: athanasius kircher an herzog august den jungeren: lateinische briefe der jahre 1650-1666 (editiones electronicae guelferbytanae 1)
derived.notes_display: Transcription of the nineteen Latin letters Athanasius Kircher sent to Duke August the Younger of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel (Herzog August Bibliothek, BA II 351-365 and others), with line numbers, a transcription with apparatus, a German translation, commentary and source images. Published in 2003; the revision log shows the last changes in December 2012 and 2018 (link corrections), so the status is archived. HAB terms allow private scholarly use and bar commercial reuse. The counts cover the 21 letters found on the transcription page.

derived.sort_title: kirishitan japanese
derived.notes_display: Transcriptions of Jesuit mission press books printed in Japanese in romanised or Japanese script, from the 'Text Data Sets for Research on the History of Japanese' of the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics (NINJAL). They include the Amakusa edition of Feiqe no monogatari (1592) and Esopo no fabulas (1593) after the British Library copy (Or.59.aa.1), the 1596 Contemptus Mundi after the Herzog August Bibliothek copy, and the 1603 Nippojisho dictionary as entry-word data. Each text is offered as downloadable plain text (txt), in original romanisation and, for some, a Japanese-script transliteration; the transcriptions were published from 2019 (Contemptus Mundi 2023, revised 2025; Nippojisho entry words 2025-10). The Contemptus Mundi transcription was made with Transkribus by Sven Osterkamp, Sophie Neutzler and So Miyagawa; the site is maintained and still updated (news of July 2026).

derived.sort_title: die urkunden und akten des klosters und des oberamts konigsfelden – 1308-1662
derived.notes_display: Charters and records of the Königsfelden convent and the later Bernese Hofmeisterei: about 1,000 single documents and three copy books, transcribed and tagged for persons, places and organisations, with a standardised and a diplomatic view. The Zenodo data dump (version of 9 April 2024, 1,557 TEI document files) lists 459 documents dated within or overlapping 1450-1700, in Early New High German (428) and Latin (18 marked; the rest unmarked). Moved to the Sources Online server (TEI Publisher) in early 2024.

derived.sort_title: korba — elektroniczny korpus tekstow polskich z xvii i xviii w.
derived.notes_display: KorBa (korba.edu.pl) is the largest corpus of historical Polish (1601-1800, ~27M segments), TEI P5 encoded with transcription/transliteration layers and rich metadata; maintained by the Institute of Polish Language, Polish Academy of Sciences (IJP PAN) with IPI PAN, PI Włodzimierz Gruszczyński, National Humanities Programme (2013-2023). The manually annotated subcorpus is downloadable under CC BY-SA (the legacy hostname korba.clarin-pl.eu no longer resolves). The Renascor Corpus working snapshot contains three collections of this project (KorBa_Polish, KorBa_Polish_full17c and KorbaText, the plain-text layer whose titles match KorBa's published text list), merged here as one edition.

derived.sort_title: kronieken dataset (chronicling novelty)
derived.notes_display: The Kronieken corpus of Dutch and Flemish chronicles of 1500-1850, written by lay people, made in the NWO project 'Chronicling Novelty: New knowledge in the Netherlands, 1500-1850' (2018-2024). The project team was led by Judith Pollmann (Leiden University) and Erika Kuijpers (Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam), with Theo Dekker, Alie Lassche, Carolina Lenarduzzi and Roser Morante, helped by students and volunteers. The transcriptions were made in Transkribus and are deposited on GitHub and Zenodo (August 2024, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13332815) as annotated XML files in three variants (without tags, with tags for dates, places, persons, margin text and so on, and with source tags), with metadata tables; scans and transcriptions can also be searched at kronieken.transkribus.eu.

derived.sort_title: nicaise ladam, chronique abregee: digital critical edition (b. salvati, phd thesis)
derived.notes_display: Digital critical edition of the Chronique abrégée and the collected works (1488-1546) of Nicaise Ladam, published as a doctoral thesis in HAL; also listed on theses.fr (2024UPSLN003).

derived.sort_title: lampeter corpus of early modern english tracts (ota ota:3193)
derived.notes_display: 120 English tracts and pamphlets 1640-1740 (about 1.19M words), TEI, CC BY-SA 3.0. The Oxford Text Archive record ota:3193 is now served by the Oxford Linguistics Data Store; the older ota.ox.ac.uk and ota.bodleian.ox.ac.uk addresses no longer reach the record.

derived.sort_title: lazarraga eskuizkribua: edizioa eta azterketa / the lazarraga manuscript: edition and study
derived.notes_display: Edition of a Basque-Spanish manuscript of poems and prose by Joan Perez Lazarraga (c. 1547-1605), found in 2004. Transcriptions (diplomatic Basque or Spanish text), modernised spelling and Spanish translations are given for each piece, with commentary, grammar and glossary. Text A (the 'Artzain-liburua' pastoral and 29 poems) is shown as web pages; text B (34 pieces) and text C are offered as PDF transcriptions. The first palaeographic study dates the hand to 1564-1567, and a poem refers to events of 1564; the manuscript is generally dated before 1602. Pages were last modified on 19 May 2017 (version 1.2 of the edition). The counts cover 64 of the 65 pieces, since the PDF of text C is no longer available on the site.

derived.sort_title: briefportal leibniz: ausgewahlte briefe
derived.notes_display: Selected letters from the Akademie edition of Leibniz's correspondence (series III, volumes 5-8): 188 letters in the database, mostly the exchange with Johann Bernoulli, 1692-1701, with variant readings and graphics. Of the 188 letters, 148 are dated 1692-1700, 28 date from 1701 and 12 are undated. The metadata can be downloaded as TEI (adw_goettingen_leibniz_briefportal.xml, CC BY 4.0), but that file holds no letter text; the letters themselves are read in the portal.

derived.sort_title: leibniz: samtliche schriften und briefe, reihe viii (naturwissenschaftliche, medizinische und technische schriften)
derived.notes_display: Series VIII of the historical-critical edition of Leibniz: his scientific, medical and technical writings. Volume 1 (1668-1676) and volume 2 (1668-1676) are wholly in the period; volume 3 (mechanics 1, 1671-1705) mostly; volume 4 (1676-1715) later, and is online only as PDF. Free PDFs (same pagination as the print) are on the site and the BBAW repository; LaTeX and TEI data for volumes 1-3 are on GitHub (CC BY-NC 4.0). The TEI files are 3.8, 6.2 and 10.1 MB for volumes 1, 2 and 3. Volume 4 was added in 2024-2025. The counts cover volumes 1 to 3 (TEI) and leave out volume 4, which is online only as PDF, and pieces dated after 1700.

derived.sort_title: lexicons of early modern english (leme)
derived.notes_display: Lexicons of Early Modern English (LEME), a historical database of monolingual, bilingual and polyglot dictionaries, lexical encyclopedias, hard-word glossaries, spelling lists and other lexically valuable treatises in print or manuscript from about 1475 to 1755 (the catalogue covers 1477-1699). Edited by Ian Lancashire at the University of Toronto, it was first co-published by University of Toronto Press and University of Toronto Libraries (2018 edition) and is now maintained by Lancashire with Isabelle Zhu and a team of programmers. The texts are read on the site as entry-structured pages and are also deposited as TEI-based XML in the University of Toronto's TSpace repository; the site was last revised in 2024 and the collection is still being added to.

derived.sort_title: letradas — corpus de textos escritos por mujeres en espana (1400-1900)
derived.notes_display: Manuscript letters and other documents written by women (queens, nobles, nuns, 19th-century writers such as Gertrudis Gómez de Avellaneda), with paleographic, transcribed and critical presentations, metadata on the women involved and map/search tools; TEITOK platform; per-document TEI at corpora.uah.es/letradas/xmlfiles/<id>.xml, no bulk download page. The whole corpus has 270 documents, and 21 of them carry no date. 'Corpus histórico en desarrollo'.

derived.sort_title: letters of william herle project (edition 2)
derived.notes_display: Hypertext edition of the letters of Elizabethan intelligencer and diplomat William Herle, with a transcript of each (web page and PDF), a catalogue entry, indexes by date, sender, recipient, place and first line, a word search, and sample images. 302 letters, dated 1559 to 1588, so the whole resource lies in the period. Edition 2 was released in March 2006 and the content shows no change since; the server's file dates (2025) reflect migration only. Free for personal use; commercial use needs permission (all rights reserved).

derived.sort_title: lettres de calvin: digital critical edition of the french correspondence of john calvin
derived.notes_display: Bilingual critical edition of the letters John Calvin wrote in French between 1538 and 1554, still growing: the site currently publishes 27 of the 120 letters of the planned corpus. Each letter has facsimiles of the manuscript or printed sources, the text of Jules Bonnet's 1854 edition in sixteenth-century French, a modernised and annotated French version, and a Spanish translation; a selection of autograph manuscripts also has diplomatic transcriptions. The TEI XML files of the French letters are in the GitHub repository (the Spanish versions are in a separate folder). The project is the work of one researcher. The counts cover the 27 letters published so far, from the Bonnet base text.

derived.sort_title: liberliber
derived.notes_display: The digital library of the Italian association Liber Liber, run since 1993 (formally constituted on 28 November 1994) through its Progetto Manuzio. It offers free electronic texts of Italian and other literature, including Renaissance and Baroque authors in Italian, Latin and Venetian, as HTML pages and downloadable ePub files, made by volunteers and distributed at no cost. The library is still active, with new texts announced in October 2026. Liber Liber is supported by donations, the sponsor E-text and partnerships.

derived.sort_title: justus lipsius, de bibliothecis syntagma (1602): digital edition
derived.notes_display: Transcription of Lipsius' short treatise on libraries from the 1602 Antwerp printing, shown beside facsimiles of the 1602 printing and later editions (1607-1741), with an introduction, a modern German translation and commentary. Frames-based site; the TEI files are served openly. Marked archived because the edition's files date from 2018 (start page last modified 2018-02-12) and nothing newer was found.

derived.sort_title: litteraturbanken (the swedish literature bank) — swedish texts
london lives 1690-1800
derived.notes_display: Searchable transcriptions of over 240,000 manuscript and printed pages from eight London archives (criminal justice, poor relief, parish, hospital and guild records), with linked datasets, covering 1690 to 1800. The part dating from 1450-1700 is limited to the first decade, 1690-1700; the rest is eighteenth-century. The in-period share was not established. Free, no login. The site is now a JavaScript application (assets rebuilt 2026-05-08). The project's XML transcriptions (in its own Plebeian Lives XML schema, not TEI) are downloadable from figshare under CC BY-NC 4.0; the licensing guide permits non-commercial and linguistic analysis but not the training of generative AI. The counts cover the pages dated 1690-1700 in that download (8,778 pages from 144 files).

derived.sort_title: lope de vega, la dama boba: edicion critica y archivo digital
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of one play, La dama boba (autograph dated 1613, first printed 1617), with a variant apparatus and an archive that shows facsimile and transcription of the three witnesses (autograph, a contemporary copy, the 1617 printed Parte XI). The downloadable TEI/XML (edicion_critica.xml) holds the critical text with the apparatus. Published 2015 (ISBN 9788898010257, doi 10.6092/UNIBO/LADAMABOBA); the server reports files changed on 10 January 2025.

derived.sort_title: lorenzo lotto, libro di spese diverse: transcription and commentary (f. de carolis, phd thesis)
derived.notes_display: Critical transcription of Lorenzo Lotto's account book (1538-1556, Loreto) with analysis and commentary, in a doctoral thesis (PDF) on AMS Dottorato, the University of Bologna's thesis repository; a revised edition appeared with EUT Edizioni Università di Trieste.

derived.sort_title: netzwerke der nonnen. edition und erschließung der briefsammlung aus kloster lune (ca. 1460-1555)
derived.notes_display: Edition (work in progress, 2016-) of the letters in manuscript Hs. 15 of Kloster Lüne, Lower Saxony, written to and by the nuns, in Low German and Latin, with facsimiles, registers and an introduction. The METS file at data_url lists the 413 TEI transcription files (texts/BriefNNN-D/L/LD_tei-transcript.xml). The project dates the collection c. 1460-1555; the titles of 3 letters mention years before 1450 (1423, 1432, 1438), which are probably years referred to in the text, and 212 letters have no date. Files on the server changed in October 2025. All 413 letters are counted within 1450-1700 on the strength of the project's dating of the collection.

derived.sort_title: ein sermon von ablass und gnade: a digital edition (taylor editions, oxford)
derived.notes_display: Transcription of Luther's Sermon von dem Ablass und Gnade (Leipzig print of 1518), with a facsimile, an English translation, linguistic notes and an introduction, and a note on the variant Basel print. Part of the Taylor Editions 'Reformation' pamphlet collection. The edition is dated 2018 (TEI change date 2018-02-14); the Taylor Editions site is online.

derived.sort_title: london provisioner's chronicle, 1550-1563, by henry machyn: manuscript, transcription, and modernization
derived.notes_display: Edition of the diary of the London merchant tailor Henry Machyn (British Library Cotton Vitellius F.v), 1550 to 1563, with manuscript images, a diplomatic transcript and a modern English rendering, browsable by year. The edition dates from 2006 and no update is evident. The counts treat the diary as one text, read from Internet Archive copies of the fulltext pages because the live site blocks automated access.

derived.sort_title: historische methode und arbeitstechnik der magdeburger zenturien: edition of selected documents
derived.notes_display: Edition of the letters, plans and reports through which Matthias Flacius and his collaborators organised the Magdeburg Centuries, the first Protestant church history. The introduction counts 154 documents from 1552 to 1568, with commentary and summaries. Each document is a separate TEI file linked from the mets.xml listing at data_url. The edition was published in 2012 and its files have not changed since (start page last modified 2012-11-21), hence archived. The counts cover 153 of the 156 listed files, since 3 files could not be downloaded.

derived.sort_title: malory project: winchester manuscript and caxton's morte darthur (1485)
derived.notes_display: Electronic edition and commentary of Malory's Morte Darthur: facsimiles of the Winchester Manuscript (British Library Add. MS 59678) and the John Rylands copy of Caxton's 1485 edition. Transcriptions (encoded in TEI P5 but not offered for download) are currently online only for parts: the Roman War episode and Caxton's Book V (sig. h7v-k3r), a few other leaves, and the Winchester and Caxton texts shown side by side. Images may not be reproduced. Marked archived: funded 2005-2010, site assets last changed in 2012 (Last-Modified 2012-05-04), the news page only says 'More information coming soon', and a web-archive capture from 2018-07-20 shows the same text loader. The counts cover the two transcribed witnesses only (the Winchester Roman War episode and the transcribed parts of Caxton), not the whole Morte Darthur.

derived.sort_title: maltese cantilena
derived.notes_display: The poem Il-Kantilena by Pietru Caxaro (15th century), the oldest known literary text in Maltese, as transcribed on Wikisource (original-orthography column, 135 words; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il-Kantilena). The Wikisource page cites no source edition.

derived.sort_title: progetto mambrino digital library — sferamundi di grecia
derived.notes_display: Mambrino Digital Library is the digital library of Spanish-inspired Italian chivalric romances (named after Mambrino Roseo da Fabriano). Each the Renascor Corpus text is a separate Zenodo dataset of a digital scholarly edition of 16th-century Sferamundi di Grecia books: 10.5281/zenodo.14235252 (Sferamundi 1), 11398260 (2), 11400259 (3), 11400335 (4), 11400513 (5), 11400584 (6) — each containing TEI XML transcription and commentary files. License CC BY-SA 4.0 (checked for record 14235252; per-record). All Zenodo records verified live. The collection also includes Il secondo libro di Palmerino d'Oliva (Zenodo 20445621).

derived.sort_title: map of early modern london
derived.notes_display: A digital scholarly edition of early modern London, combining a gazetteer, an anthology of TEI-encoded texts, and a map. Includes links between places, people, and texts. The site is a static release (version 7.0, May 2022); the mayoral shows strand continues separately in LEMDO. The counts cover the primary-source documents, not the gazetteer, personography or encyclopedia entries, and a few very small primary texts may be missed.

derived.sort_title: marinelives: transcribed high court of admiralty depositions and related records
derived.notes_display: Wiki with page-by-page transcriptions, beside images, of Admiralty Court deposition books (HCA 13) and other records at The National Archives, Kew, such as customs port books (E 190) and Chancery cases (C 5). The wiki lists 102 volume pages, but many are empty or only partly transcribed (for example HCA 13/46 and 13/129 are empty, HCA 13/70, 1654-1656, has 1,506 pages, mostly transcribed 2013-2015). The front page, last edited 2024-04-10, presents the SOLM-2024 database of 24,000 deponents. Reading is free without login (some deeper pages answer slowly or ask for a browser check). Licence: the wiki footer says CC BY 3.0 unless otherwise noted. The counts cover the 8,427 transcribed folio pages in 56 volumes, and volumes without start and end dates are not counted in the period.

derived.sort_title: francisci maurolyci opera mathematica: electronic edition of the mathematical works of francesco maurolico
derived.notes_display: Critical edition, with variant readings from each manuscript or print witness, of the scientific works of Maurolico (1494-1575): Euclid, spherics, arithmetic, Archimedes, conics, music, optics, cosmography, mechanics, letters and methodological writings. The introduction says the full corpus is about 5,000 pages of manuscripts and prints and that works are added as they are ready; pages are frames-based HTML with PDF versions. Source-image sites need a login. The original Pisa address in the catalogue (www.dm.unipi.it/pages/maurolic, 2008 Wayback copy) now redirects to this one. Archived: pages last modified between April and July 2006. The counts cover 58 works or sections, which are undated and counted as falling within 1450-1700 because Maurolico lived from 1494 to 1575.

derived.sort_title: mazarinades
derived.notes_display: Mazarinades (pamphlets of the Fronde, 1648-1653) published by the ANTONOMAZ project at Sorbonne Université. The counts come from the Zenodo release of December 2022 (3,064 files); the project site and its GitHub repository now hold more (3,132 texts).

derived.sort_title: magyar elektronikus konyvtar (mek)
derived.notes_display: Hungarian Electronic Library (MEK), the digital library of the National Széchényi Library. Most of the texts come from MEK; three poems (Gyöngyösi's Murányi Vénus and Phoenix, Esterházy's Egy csudálatos ének) were taken from the Syrena site of the Department of Old Hungarian Literature, ELTE (magyar-irodalom.elte.hu/syrena).

derived.sort_title: memis – epigraphic corpus of medieval and early modern inscriptions in slovenia
derived.notes_display: TEI XML edition (version 1.0, published 2020-12-06, on CLARIN.SI) of 51 Latin inscriptions from the Slovenian coastal towns dated 1222 to the mid-17th century, with expanded transcriptions and Slovenian translations. Static repository deposit, no later version found. Some inscriptions carry only an approximate date (for example 'second half of the 15th century'), and four are undated.

derived.sort_title: mercure galant (obvil/iremus — edition complete 1672-1721)
derived.notes_display: The OBVIL/IReMus Mercure galant programme publishes the whole run 1672-1710 in TEI XML (GitHub repo OBVIL/mercure-galant, 'MG-1672-01' to 'MG-1721-05'). The catalogue statistics cover 26 issues of 1672-1700 (4.2M words). Licence: CC BY-NC-ND. The former reading site (obvil.sorbonne-universite.fr/corpus/mercure-galant/) is offline (HTTP 404); the GitHub Pages edition is the live access point.

derived.sort_title: mercurius-baumbank (version 1.1) — laudatio repository
derived.notes_display: The Mercurius-Baumbank (version 1.1), edited by Ulrike Demske (University of Potsdam), is a syntactically annotated treebank of early German newspaper (Relation) texts of the 17th century, deposited in the LAUDATIO repository (HU Berlin). The texts are distributed as TIGER-XML, NEGRA and relANNIS; the TEI files in LAUDATIO carry metadata only.

derived.sort_title: john milton reading room
derived.notes_display: Complete poetry (Paradise Lost, Paradise Regain'd, Samson Agonistes, the 1645 and 1673 volumes, sonnets and the Latin and Italian poems) and about 20 prose works from Of Reformation (1641) to Prolusions (1674), in the original spelling of the seventeenth-century printings, with introductions and hyperlinked annotations. Editing is stated to be still in progress for some prose works. Treated as active because the site is maintained and still carries a copyright line up to 2026; no dated changelog was found.

derived.sort_title: mini lazarillo: edicion minima del lazarillo de tormes
derived.notes_display: Student digital edition of the 1554 Medina del Campo printing of the Vida de Lazarillo de Tormes, in a plain reading edition and an annotated edition, with images of the original volume. The text follows that printing but modernises spelling and accents (see the editorial criteria page), so it is a modernised edition, not a diplomatic transcription. A TEI master file is in the GitHub repository. The counts cover the TEI master text (prologue and seven tratados), keeping the original readings where the file encodes them. The repository was last updated on 4 May 2020.

derived.sort_title: mitteldeutsche selbstzeugnisse der zeit des dreißigjahrigen krieges (mdsz)
derived.notes_display: Electronic edition of four autobiographical texts of the Thirty Years' War, with transcriptions of the originals, digital facsimiles, commentary and indexes: the chronicle of Volkmar Happe (1587-1647/59), the notes of Michael Heubel (1605-1684), Hans Krafft (1589-1665) and Caspar Heinrich Marx (1600-1635). The original address (mdsz.thulb.uni-jena.de) now serves an unrelated Shlink page; the Internet Archive holds copies of the site as it was in 2022. The portal 'Thirty Years War Online' (hosted by the ThULB since 2024) still links to the old address. The counts cover 735 of about 2,600 manuscript pages recovered from Internet Archive copies, so they are a lower bound.

derived.sort_title: muysc cubun — lengua muisca (manuscrito 158 bnc; gramatica de lugo; coleccion mutis ms 2922 bprm)
derived.notes_display: muysca.cubun.org is a MediaWiki-based research site (since 2008/2009) on the Muisca (Chibcha) language: dictionary, and transcriptions of colonial manuscripts including Manuscrito 158 (Biblioteca Nacional de Colombia) and Lugo's 1619 gramatica, exactly matching the origins ('keyed transcription'). The site loaded successfully via WebFetch (curl from this network is blocked by the host's TLS/firewall; HTTPS handshake hangs, so treat liveness as verified-by-fetch). Companion site coleccionmutis.cubun.org holds Manuscrito 2922 BPRM cited in a third origin. Non-TEI (wiki 'keyed transcriptions').

derived.sort_title: das nachlassinventar erzherzog ferdinands ii. (1529-1595) von 1596
derived.notes_display: Inventory manuscript (KHM shelfmark KK_6652) of the possessions of Archduke Ferdinand II of Tyrol (1529-1595), drawn up in 1596 at Innsbruck and Ambras, digitised with a full-text transcription in the repository viewer. The viewer sits behind a bot check, so the pages are best opened in a browser; the "plaintext" API endpoint returns the whole transcription as HTML fragments (the viewer's TEI export is only a wrapper around the same HTML, not a TEI encoding of the text). Status active: the repository and its DOI (registered under the recent 10.60477 prefix) are live in 2026.

derived.sort_title: narragonien digital: digitale textausgaben von europaischen 'narrenschiffen' des 15. jahrhunderts
derived.notes_display: Twelve editions or adaptations of Sebastian Brant's Narrenschiff printed before 1500: the three Basel editions (1494, 1495, 1499), the Nuremberg (1494) and Strasbourg (1494/5) German versions, three Latin editions by Jakob Locher (Basel 1497, 1498), the French Rivière version (Paris 1497) and its 1499 reprint, the Low German Lübeck version (1497) and the Dutch Paris print (1500). Each has a digital facsimile, transcription and, for eight, a normalised reading text, plus a synoptic view and registers. The home redirect is www.narragonien-digital.de/exist/. The news page shows entries up to June 2025.

derived.sort_title: newton project
derived.notes_display: Online edition of the writings of Isaac Newton (1642-1727), printed and unprinted, covering his alchemical, mathematical, Mint, optical, religious and scientific papers, notebooks and correspondence. Most documents are transcribed from manuscript sources in a diplomatic rendition that records Newton's amendments, alongside a normalised, more readable version, with TEI-P5 and MathML XML viewable for each text, plus catalogue records and, for some items, translations from Latin and links to images of the originals. The project was formed in 1998 under the general editorship of Rob Iliffe and Scott Mandelbrote; it is based at the Faculty of History, University of Oxford (hosted there since autumn 2016), and was funded 2008-2014 by two AHRC grants and two JISC awards plus private donors. It is a non-profit and the site is still maintained (copyright line 2026).

derived.sort_title: noscemus — nova scientia: early modern scientific literature and latin
derived.notes_display: The Digital Sourcebook of NOSCEMUS (Nova Scientia: Early Modern Scientific Literature and Latin), an ERC Advanced Grant project (no. 741374) led by Martin Korenjak at the University of Innsbruck, running 10/2017 to 09/2022 (prolonged to 04/2023). The dataset holds plain text of the Latin scientific works catalogued in the Noscemus Wiki, produced from digital copies of the printed books by automatic text recognition in Transkribus, with models trained for early modern Latin prints; the transcriptions were not manually corrected. The texts are linked to the database through their Transkribus IDs and the source of each digital copy is recorded. It was deposited in Zenodo on 17 March 2025 (Stefan Zathammer) as a single zip file.

derived.sort_title: obvil — corpus d'editions anciennes francaises (teinte)
derived.notes_display: Born-digital TEI corpora of early-modern French texts from LabEx OBVIL (Sorbonne Université), encoded with the Teinte toolchain (lauze_apologie-danse_1623, Faceties 1557, La Bruyère 1694, etc.); CC BY-NC-ND. The lab's data platform ObTIC lists the freely available OBVIL corpora; the corpus files are on the OBVIL GitHub organisation. The former reading site obvil.sorbonne-universite.fr is no longer reachable.

derived.sort_title: obvil — corpus la haine du theatre (querelle du theatre)
derived.notes_display: 'La Haine du theatre / querelle du theatre' is an OBVIL corpus of the 17th-century French anti-theatre controversy (1541-1698 texts), TEI encoded (repo OBVIL/haine-theatre, GitHub Pages edition verified live); the 14 the Renascor Corpus texts match its file namespace exactly. License: CC BY-NC-ND. The main OBVIL site was unreachable at check time; the GitHub Pages edition is the verified entry point.

derived.sort_title: 1000 ans de litterature d'oc (universite ouverte des humanites): renaissance excerpts
derived.notes_display: Short excerpts of Occitan Renaissance authors (Garros, Bellaud de la Bellaudièra, Larade, Ader, Godolin) from the online anthology 1000 ans de littérature d'oc. Occitan Wikisource texts harvested alongside it have their own entry.

derived.sort_title: occitan wikisource: renaissance texts (godolin, gailhard, esquerrier, garros)
derived.notes_display: Transcriptions on Occitan Wikisource of Arnaud Esquerrier's chronicle of the counts of Foix, Pèire Godolin's Ramelet Moundi, Augièr Gailhard's Lou Banquet and Pèir de Garròs's Poesias gasconas.

derived.sort_title: ode — oralia diacronica del espanol (includes corderegra)
derived.notes_display: Corpus of unpublished archival documents (inventories, trial testimonies, surgeon reports) of the Real Chancillería de Granada and other Spanish archives, published by the ODE project (Oralia Diacrónica del Español, Universidad de Granada). The original CORDEREGRA site (corderegra.es) no longer resolves, and ODE is its working host; the ODE site is available only over http.

derived.sort_title: proceedings of the old bailey online
derived.notes_display: Online edition of the Proceedings of the Old Bailey, the trial accounts of London's central criminal court, 1674-1913 (the catalogue covers the 1674-1700 part), with the Ordinary of Newgate's Accounts (1676-1772). It was created by the Universities of Hertfordshire and Sheffield and the Open University; the project directors were Tim Hitchcock, Robert Shoemaker and Clive Emsley, with Sharon Howard as project manager, and the funders were the Big Lottery Fund and the AHRC. The texts were double-rekeyed (to 1834) and marked up in XML for names, crimes, verdicts and punishments; the site is run by the Digital Humanities Institute, Sheffield, which also provides the data download (dhi.ac.uk/data/oldbailey). The site is active.

derived.sort_title: old hungarian corpus (regi magyar nyelvemlekek)
derived.notes_display: Old Hungarian Corpus of codices and early printed books (11th-16th c., original orthography betűhű and phonemic levels), maintained by the Hungarian Generative Diachronic Syntax project at the Research Institute for Linguistics. The Renascor Corpus working snapshot contains two collections of this resource (HungarianCorpus and MGTSZ_AporCodex, the Apor Codex file), merged here as one edition.

derived.sort_title: open source shakespeare (globe edition of the complete works)
derived.notes_display: The complete works in the 1864 Globe edition (W. G. Clark and W. A. Wright), with a concordance, advanced search, character search and statistics. The text is the modernised spelling of a nineteenth-century edition, not a transcription of the early printings, as with the Folger Shakespeare entry. The site's statistics page gives 43 works and 884,421 words (plays, sonnets and poems), all written between about 1590 and 1613; the counts below are ours, from the downloaded database, with speaker names included. The database can be downloaded as SQL, Access and delimited text files. The site shows © 2003-2026 and a server update on 21 May 2026.

derived.sort_title: openedges (open editions of early modern dutch and german bibles)
derived.notes_display: The counts cover the Dutch and German Bibles of the public subset (12 within 1450-1700), not the English and Swedish Bibles in the archive.

derived.sort_title: openiti
derived.notes_display: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative: a corpus of Arabic (and other Islamicate-language) texts, published openly on GitHub in the mARkdown format, organised by author death date, with releases archived on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4075046) and tools such as a Python library. It is a multi-institutional effort led by researchers at the Aga Khan University (Institute for the Study of Muslim Civilisations, London), the Roshan Institute for Persian Studies (University of Maryland) and Universität Hamburg. The catalogue entry covers authors of 1451-1700. The organisation is active, with repository updates in 2026.

derived.sort_title: osta — old spanish textual archive
derived.notes_display: OSTA is the lemmatized/morphologically tagged ~35M-word corpus of 400+ semi-paleographic transcriptions of Old Spanish (including Asturleonese/Navarro-Aragonese) texts, begun 2015 by HSMS; the transcriptions and metadata are on GitHub (hispanicseminary/OSTA) and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18931376 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), which is exactly the Renascor Corpus source (Cortes' Cartas de relación, Libro de albeiteria, Libro del abad don Juan etc.). Main search interface v2.0 verified live. The Renascor Corpus keeps the semi-paleographic text layer (not the lemmatized one). The GitHub repository now holds 670 transcriptions, against 644 in this Zenodo version.

derived.sort_title: otomi mission
derived.notes_display: Transcriptions and Spanish translations of Otomi-language mission texts: the García and Martín manuscripts (Otomi and Spanish, held in the Archivo General de la Nación, Mexico) and the Codices of Jilotepec and Huichapan, with a table of Otomi phonemes as an aid. The paleographies are by David Charles Wright Carr, published by Éditions SUP-INFOR (Marc Thouvenot); the García and Martín files date from 2000, the codices and phoneme table from 2002. Each text has an excerpt viewer, an information page and a downloadable ZIP. Each download entry is marked with a copyright sign; no further licence terms are given.

derived.sort_title: paesi novamente retrovati - newe unbekanthe landte: digital edition of early reports of discovery
derived.notes_display: Diplomatic and normalised transcription of Paesi novamente retrovati (Vicenza, 1507), the first printed collection of voyage accounts, and of its German translation Newe unbekanthe landte (Nuremberg, 1508), with facsimiles, editorial notes, indexes of persons and places and a modern translation. Both transcriptions are TEI files (data_url shows the Italian one; the German one is tei-transcript-nul.xml in the same folder). Archived: files date from 2017-2018 (start page last modified 2017-12-11).

derived.sort_title: passiusalmar icelandic
derived.notes_display: Web edition of the Passíusálmar (Passion Hymns) of Hallgrímur Pétursson (1614-1674) with the poet's works, biography, bibliography and images and excerpts of the autograph manuscript (JS 337 4to), plus audio of radio readings and hymn singing. The text is given in modern spelling, from an edition of the National and University Library of Iceland. It was made by the Icelandic broadcaster RÚV with the Árni Magnússon Institute for Icelandic Studies and the National and University Library; the first version appeared on 9 February 1998 and the site was last updated in April 2014. Editing and web design were by Anna S. Melsteð and Jón Karl Helgason (1998).

derived.sort_title: correspondance complete et autres ecrits de guy patin
derived.notes_display: Annotated critical edition of the letters of the Paris physician Guy Patin to colleagues in France, Switzerland, Germany and the Low Countries, with indexes of people, places and terms, a full-text search and printing options. The site shows '4e édition (mai 2022) revue et augmentée' as its latest update and no later change was found, hence archived. Letters are open without login.

derived.sort_title: pceec2
les pensees de blaise pascal: edition electronique
derived.notes_display: Electronic edition of Pascal's Pensées, online since June 2011. It gives the modernised text with notes together with the diplomatic and scholarly transcriptions of the Recueil des originaux (BnF Ms 9202), the manuscript Copies of 1662-1666, the Port-Royal editions of 1670 and 1678 and later manuscripts, with a glossary and studies of the paper and handwriting. Texts are read on the site; no download was found. The legal-notice page is dated 'Juin 2011-Octobre 2026'. The counts cover the fragments with an extractable transcription, and 87 pages without one are left out.

derived.sort_title: diary of samuel pepys (phil gyford edition)
derived.notes_display: The diary text published by Phil Gyford's pepysdiary.com is taken from Project Gutenberg. The word and text counts were measured on the Project Gutenberg e-text (one text, including the 19th-century editors' introductions and notes), not on the website itself.

derived.sort_title: perseus digital library: renaissance materials (english)
derived.notes_display: The Renaissance (early modern English) collection of the Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University. Its public GitHub repository (PerseusDL/canonical-engLit, last pushed June 2026) holds the collection's texts in folders by author or work, among them Shakespeare, Marlowe, Sidney, Bacon, Hakluyt, Holinshed, James I and Lanyer, alongside reference works such as Schmidt's Shakespeare Lexicon. The Perseus site presents the texts for online reading and searching. Individual editors and encoding details were not established.

derived.sort_title: philipp hainhofer: reiseberichte & sammlungsbeschreibungen 1594–1636 (annotated digital edition)
derived.notes_display: Annotated digital edition presenting the travel accounts and collection descriptions of the Augsburg merchant and cultural broker Philipp Hainhofer (1578–1647) for the first time in full, with manuscript facsimiles, full text, critical apparatus and text/image commentaries. TEI/XML transcriptions and registers are archived on arthistoricum.net@heiDATA. Edition website went online in 2020 (first DFG phase, Munich journeys 1603–1636); further phases are scheduled until 2029, so the project is ongoing. The counts cover the 16 journey and collection-description files published so far. The edition is DFG-funded.

derived.sort_title: philological museum: library of humanistic texts (dana f. sutton, ed.)
derived.notes_display: Free hypertext editions of Neo-Latin works, mostly British, with introductions, notes and English translations: poetry, drama (including Jesuit plays), history, letters, treatises and speeches by authors such as Buchanan, Camden, Alabaster, Cowley and Bacon. The library page lists about 265 works. Of these, about 219 carry a date between 1459 and 1700 in their title, 9 are dated after 1700 (for example Addison, Bentley, Anstey), and 37 give no date (mostly 16th-17th-century authors). The University of Birmingham states a commitment to keep the site free online. The library page was last modified on 5 August 2025. The counts cover 187 of the 258 linked works, those whose Latin text could be identified, and works without a year in their title are not counted in the period.

derived.sort_title: early latin poetry of sylvester johannis phrygius (p. sjokvist, phd thesis)
derived.notes_display: Edition with introduction, translation and commentary of three major portions of the early Latin poetry of the Swedish theologian Sylvester Johannis Phrygius (1572-1628), published as a doctoral thesis with full text (PDF) in DiVA.

derived.sort_title: poeti d'italia in lingua latina (mqdq)
derived.notes_display: Digital library of Latin verse written in Italy from Dante's time to the mid-16th century, with metrical scansion, a search tool, co-occurrence search and indexes of authors, metres and works. The text of each poem is freely readable and is taken from a named modern critical edition (for example L. Capra 1973 for Leonardo Teronda). The chronological index lists 346 authors in three periods: 'Da Dante a Petrarca' (1250-1374, 76 authors), 'Umanisti del Quattrocento' (1374-1494, 172) and 'Prima metà del Cinquecento' (1494-1550, 98). The site states 'Ultimo aggiornamento: 2026.06.03'. Because the texts reproduce modern critical editions of poems that survive in manuscripts and prints, they are not diplomatic transcriptions. Dates of individual works are approximate (author life spans), so the share within 1450-1700 is approximate.

derived.sort_title: polemos — codificacion xml de la polemica gongorina (labex obvil)
derived.notes_display: Polemos is the XML-TEI encoding of the 17th-century polémica gongorina (Jáuregui, Espinosa, Díez de Revenga texts, 1613-1630s), edited for the Labex OBVIL by the Polémica Gongorina project (Mercedes Blanco et al.) and published on GitHub in the gongoradigital organisation (polemos, polemos-naked). The 31 texts in the catalogue (carta-amigo_1613, anti-jauregui, apologetico_1662, censura-lope...) belong to this edition. The reading edition and its download menu are now at https://obtic.huma-num.fr/obvil-web/corpus/gongora/ (the former obvil.sorbonne-universite.fr address no longer works). Licence: CC BY-NC-ND.

derived.sort_title: poly-olbion project (michael drayton, poly-olbion)
derived.notes_display: Full, unmodernised electronic copy of Drayton's 15,000-line topographical poem in the two parts published in 1612 and 1622 (songs 1-18 and 19-30), plus modernised extracts and a word list; John Selden's Illustrations are not included. All the text dates from 1450-1700. The site announces a forthcoming scholarly edition. Status: latest blog post is January 2019 but the site feed was rebuilt on 2024-04-11, so it is kept as active. No licence stated for the text; the CC BY-NC 3.0 mention on the home page concerns images. robots.txt blocks only /wp-admin/. The counts cover the thirty songs; the modernised extracts are not counted.

derived.sort_title: digital tei-xml edition of camillo porzio's "la congiura de' baroni del regno di napoli contra re ferdinando primo"
derived.notes_display: A Zenodo-published TEI-XML dataset of the critical digital edition of Porzio's La congiura de' Baroni (first published Naples 1565), encoded and curated by Cristiano Amendola; matches the Renascor Corpus origin (single text). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18047915 verified live; license CC BY 4.0. The Renascor Corpus holds the TEI-derived text (~49k words).

derived.sort_title: p.s. post scriptum (arquivo digital de escrita quotidiana)
derived.notes_display: Digital archive of private letters from early modern Portugal and Spain (the catalogue covers the 16th and 17th centuries), built in the P.S. Post Scriptum project at CLUL, Lisbon, with an ERC Advanced Grant (7FP, GA 295562); the project ran 2012-2017 and the researchers include Rita Marquilhas. It is both a scholarly edition and an annotated corpus: transcriptions expand abbreviations and standardise word boundaries and i/j/u/v, and a standardised (modernised) layer carries part-of-speech tags and syntactic parsing. The corpus is searchable in TEITOK and downloadable as ZIP files by language and century (original text, standardised text, POS, parsed). Letters mostly survive in Inquisition and court files.

derived.sort_title: ppchy yiddish
derived.notes_display: Penn Parsed Corpus of Historical Yiddish: a syntactically parsed corpus of about 200,000 words of Yiddish, begun as examples collected for research on the syntax of subordinate clauses. Most of the text comes from two 20th-century works; the repository also holds reference material (Olsvanger's 1947 glossary, transliterated chapters of Zaretski's 1929 grammar). It is maintained by Beatrice Santorini (University of Pennsylvania) and published on GitHub as version 1.0 (2021) for use with CorpusSearch; it is not a diplomatic edition of early modern documents.

derived.sort_title: progetto pico / pico project: oratio de hominis dignitate (brown university and university of bologna)
derived.notes_display: Hypertext edition of Pico's Oratio (the 'Discourse on the Dignity of Man'), with a transcription of the Latin text of the first printed edition (Bologna, 1496) divided into paragraphs 1-47, an annotated text with commentary by seven scholars, and introductions in Latin, Italian and English. The incunable copies (Exemplar Brunense, Exemplar Bononiense, editio princeps) and the Apologia (1487) are shown as page images only. The original address (brown.edu/Departments/Italian_Studies/pico/) now returns a 404 error, so the link goes to the Internet Archive copy of 13 September 2025.

derived.sort_title: project gutenberg

period.label: c. 1451–1699
period.estimate_note: Includes broad author-lifespan estimates for texts without a recorded year.

derived.notes_display: Project Gutenberg, a volunteer-produced library of free eBooks in HTML, plain text and e-reader formats, run by the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation. The catalogue entry covers its transcribed early modern texts (1450-1700) in many languages, harvested from the site. Most eBooks are out of copyright in the United States; each file carries a licence notice and the 'Project Gutenberg' trademark is subject to separate rules. The robot-access policy page governs bulk harvesting.

derived.sort_title: protokoll des religionskolloquiums in vilnius am 14. juni 1585
derived.notes_display: Transcription of the minutes of the religious colloquy held in Vilnius on 14 June 1585, from a manuscript in the HAB, with a German translation, introduction, manuscript description and digital facsimile. The TEI file was last modified on 7 May 2006 and there is no sign of later changes.

derived.sort_title: qhod — quellen zur habsburgisch-osmanischen diplomatie (digital scholarly edition of habsburg-ottoman diplomatic sources 1500-1918) — edition-data release 2.0
derived.notes_display: QhoD is the born-digital critical edition of Habsburg-Ottoman diplomatic sources (diplomatic correspondence, instructions, minutes...), TEI encoded, CC BY 4.0, published via qhod.net with TEI/image data released on GitHub (QHOD/qhod-edition-data) and Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.14449603, release 2.0 by Stephan Kurz) — exactly the Renascor Corpus source. The Renascor Corpus's 219 texts (1570-1600 era) come from that Zenodo/GitHub TEI edition-data bundle (Habsburg-Ottoman diplomatic texts in Latin etc.).

derived.sort_title: queen's men editions (qme)
derived.notes_display: Online editions of plays associated with the Queen's Men: The Famous Victories of Henry V, Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay, King Leir, Selimus and The True Tragedy of Richard III, each in a modern-spelling and an old-spelling text from the early quarto, with introductions, collations, performance materials and videos. The Old Wives' Tale is announced in the menu but its edition page returns an error. The TEI source of each text is downloadable under /qme/xml/source/ (for example emdFV_Q1.xml); the index file is given as data address. The old address qme.internetshakespeare.uvic.ca redirects here. The counts cover the five old-spelling texts only, not the modern-spelling versions or The Old Wives' Tale.

derived.sort_title: records of the parliaments of scotland to 1707
derived.notes_display: Proceedings of the Scottish parliament from the first surviving act of 1235 to the Union of 1707, with the original text (Latin, French, Scots) and a parallel English translation, links to the manuscript images and an editorial apparatus. The part dating from 1450-1700 is the fifteenth-, sixteenth- and seventeenth-century parliaments, conventions and committee records (roughly the second half of the 1235-1707 run); earlier and 1700-1707 records are outside the period. Free, no login. The site is an old frameset: the in-page 'Service currently unavailable' text is commented out and the footer reads '2007-2026 University of St Andrews'. No data download found. The October 2026 harvest fetched the original-language text of the 11,104 records dated 1450-1700 listed in the reign indexes, at a rate agreed with the RPS team; languages are assigned per record, and short English editorial headings could not all be separated from the text.

derived.sort_title: reed english
derived.notes_display: REED Online: the TEI-XML collections of Records of Early English Drama, documents about drama, secular music and other entertainment in England before 1642, published by county or playhouse (Berkshire, Cambridgeshire, Hampshire, Staffordshire, Suffolk, Yorkshire North Riding, and the Bear Garden, Newington Butts, Rose and Swan playhouses). It is an international research collaboration associated with the University of Toronto (reed.utoronto.ca), with support credited to bodies including the British Academy, NEH and SSHRC; the site is powered by Kiln and EATS and is copyrighted 2016-25, with the Swan Playhouse collection (ed. Sally-Beth MacLean) added in June 2026. The TEI source files are also on GitHub (REEDProject/Collections).

derived.sort_title: referenzkorpus fruhneuhochdeutsch (ref; reference corpus of early new high german)
derived.notes_display: Reference Corpus of Early New High German (1350-1650): diplomatically transcribed texts, annotated at three sites (morphology at Bochum and Halle, syntax at Potsdam). The Zenodo release (version 1.0.2, December 2021; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5793616) is by Klaus-Peter Wegera, Hans-Joachim Solms, Ulrike Demske and Stefanie Dipper and comprises two archives, the annotated corpus and a reading-text version. No later release was seen.

derived.sort_title: regensburger wappen- und portratbucher (band 06, vormundamt: edited text)
derived.notes_display: Twelve Regensburg office books of the 16th to early 19th century are shown as page images in the DFG-Viewer; only Band 06 (Wappen- und Porträtbuch des Vormundamtes, StAR I Aa 6) also has an edited text. It contains a preface (1649), the founding decree of 1537 and a list of directors, assessors and clerks from 1537 to 1787, with 64 portraits dated 1649 to c. 1751. The project dates from 2012 (TEI file dated 2012-03-29, site copyright 2012) and has no later update, so it is listed as archived. The counts cover Band 06 only, the one volume with an edited text, and the part of it dated 1700 or earlier.

derived.sort_title: regi magyar exemplumadatbazis / database of old hungarian exempla (rmex)
derived.notes_display: Searchable database of the exempla (short moral stories) found in the old Hungarian-language codices, including the Domonkos, Margit-legenda, Érdy, Cornides, Székelyudvarhelyi, Érsekújvári and Teleki codices. Each record gives the exemplum text (a modernised reading taken from the printed Nyelvemléktár editions), a summary, keywords, the source codex and folio, and Latin sources and parallels. Version 1.0 appeared in 2014 and version 2.0 has been in progress since 2021; records were uploaded as recently as 2024. The counts cover the 'exemplum text' field of the record pages 0001 to 0386 and their lettered variants (for example 0016a); the codices named on the site are Hungarian-language manuscripts of the early 16th century (for example the Debreceni codex of 1519, the Érdy codex of 1526-1527 and the Érsekújvári codex of 1529-1531). The text is edited and modernised, not a diplomatic transcription. Searches use a web form; no bulk download was found.

derived.sort_title: rejestr kontrybucji diecezji poznanskiej z 1561 r. (digital edition)
derived.notes_display: TEI edition of the register of the double contribution imposed on the clergy of the Poznań diocese in 1561, from two copies kept in the Archiwum Główne Akt Dawnych, Warsaw (ASK 91 and a fragment in ASK 3), with page images. The whole TEI file is served at the data link. Status active: the project site is maintained (events listed for 2026) and the app runs a recent TEI Publisher release; no date of last change to the edition itself is given.

derived.sort_title: relationen vom russischen hof: berichte europaischer diplomaten, 1690-1730
derived.notes_display: Transcriptions of reports and letters from the Russian court sent to the imperial court in Vienna and to Berlin. Of 660 transcribed documents, 34 date from 1690-95 (per the introduction); the rest are from 1726-1728 and fall outside the period. 37 transcribed documents are dated or filed 1690-1696. The whole edition lists 1,242 items, of which 660 have transcripts. The document index was last modified on 5 July 2018 and the introduction is dated 2016; the project (funded 2012-2015) is a pilot that was not continued. Texts are served as HTML with RDFa; no download of the texts was found.

derived.sort_title: religiose friedenswahrung und friedensstiftung in europa (1500-1800): digitale quellenedition fruhneuzeitlicher religionsfrieden
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of religious peace treaties, edicts and diets, with diplomatic and modernised transcriptions side by side, links to facsimiles at the HAB and notes. The edition covers 1485-1788; 39 source texts (Quellentexte) are dated 1485-1689. The TEI files are served per document at /g/pa000001-00NN (the example data_url is the Speyer Reichsabschied of 1526). Languages include German, French, Latin, Czech, Italian, English, Polish and Dutch. The edition was published in 2020; the site was last modified on 31 July 2022. The counts cover the original-language source texts only, not the German translations or the texts of 1712-1788.

derived.sort_title: renascence editions (university of oregon / luminarium mirror)
derived.notes_display: Online repository of works printed in English between 1477 and 1799, sorted by author (222 titles in all). The part dating from 1450-1700 is the large majority: sixteenth- and seventeenth-century poetry, drama, prose, proclamations and pamphlets (for example Bacon, Spenser, Dekker, Elizabeth I's proclamations, 1640s-50s pamphlets). Later items (Defoe, Fielding, Gay, Goldsmith, Gray, American colonial documents of 1775-76) fall outside the period. Texts are keyed from the original or later facsimile editions in original spelling; each is a plain HTML page, with PDF copies at the University of Oregon Scholars Bank. No bulk download. The counts cover the in-period HTML texts of the index, one record per page or part. Status: the site states '222 titles; updated November 21, 2009', and nothing newer was found (page checked 2026-10-13); the host's robots.txt allows crawling except /cgi-bin.

derived.sort_title: referenzkorpus mittelniederdeutsch/niederrheinisch, 1200-1650 (ren)
derived.notes_display: The ReN collection is NOT a ReFrame sub-project but the Referenzkorpus Mittelniederdeutsch/Niederrheinisch (ReN, 1200-1650), the DFG reference corpus of Middle Low German/Low Rhenish texts built at the Universities of Hamburg and Münster. The texts come from the CorA-ReN-XML TEI dump the project distributes; corpus metadata is CC-BY via the RefCorG/REDE framework.

derived.sort_title: renumar — de minute en minute 2.0 (ressources numeriques pour l'edition des archives de la renaissance)
derived.notes_display: Database of Renaissance archival acts at the CESR, Tours: 95% notarial minutes (Tours, Amboise, Touraine, Paris, Bourges, Chartres, Châteaudun), with municipal accounts and deliberations and urban correspondence, 1450-1650. Of the 20,800 documents published on 1 April 2025, about 85% are given as analyses (summaries) and about 15% as transcriptions; the search engine indexes the two separately. Only the transcriptions are texts for this catalogue, and their number is not published, so texts and words are omitted. The data are encoded in XML-TEI with TELMA (IRHT) and shown as HTML through XTF (MSH Val de Loire); no TEI download was found on the site, Nakala, Zenodo or HAL, and the 2023 BVH report lists a FAIR release as work in progress. The base continues 'De minute en minute', created by the CESR in 2007 on the BVH site and moved in full to this platform in 2018; Pierre Aquilon contributed the Tours and Paris notarial records. The site returned server errors (HTTP 502 and 500) on 2026-10-27; a progress report of November 2025 (HAL halshs-05404234) shows continuing work. Sources: D. Rivaud, presentation at the École des chartes, 9 April 2025 (https://www.chartes.psl.eu/sites/default/files/public/media/document/2025-05/rivaud.pdf); S. Breuil, HAL halshs-03597555 (2018); rfgenealogie.com, 25 October 2022.

derived.sort_title: representative poetry online (university of toronto)
derived.notes_display: Anthology of English-language poems (version 3.0 states about 4,700 poems by 723 poets from Caedmon to the 20th century). The part dating from 1450-1700 is the Renaissance and seventeenth-century sections (poets such as Skelton, Wyatt, Surrey, Sidney, Spenser, Shakespeare, Donne, Jonson, Herbert, Milton, Marvell). Spelling is mixed: the editors' introduction says the texts of the printed editions were generally normalised, while texts added only online are transcribed from original editions mainly without altered spelling, and Spenser is not modernised. The site is therefore not marked as modernised-only. Free to read; the copyright page says most poems are public domain and the collection as a whole is copyright. No bulk download. robots.txt blocks only admin and search paths. Site shows current daily content (checked 2026-10-13). The counts cover the poems of the poets who lived within 1450-1700; anonymous poems and poets who died after 1701 are not counted.

derived.sort_title: rhythmic corpus of 100 spanish golden age plays
derived.notes_display: Zenodo dataset DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17537343 (all-versions DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17537048 family): 100 securely attributed comedias by nine Golden Age playwrights (Cervantes, Lope, Tirso, Calderon, etc.), each in original and rhythmic-scansion versions, produced with Fernando Sanz-Lázaro's libEscansión and revised by hand. It accompanies Álvaro Cuéllar's article 'From Atoms to Waves: Rhythmic Stylometry for Authorship Studies of Early Modern Spanish Theatre' (Janus 14, 2025). Licence CC BY 4.0. The record is the exact source string cited by the harvest ('Cuéllar Rhythmic Corpus 100 SGA Plays').

derived.sort_title: rialc - repertorio informatizzato dell'antica letteratura catalana
derived.notes_display: RIALC (built 1999-2003 at Naples Federico II, in collaboration with the Universities of Barcelona, UAB and Girona) is the standard digital library of medieval Catalan poetry: ~216 authors and ~1,600 13th-15th c. poems transcribed from critical editions (HTML, not TEI). The texts include Joan de Masdovelles (~1460, 9 poems) and Joan Berenguer de Masdovelles (~1460, 168 poems); they are author pages of this repertory. No explicit licence; site is live but the project is no longer actively extended.

derived.sort_title: richard brome online
derived.notes_display: Edition of the fifteen surviving plays of Richard Brome and The Late Lancashire Witches (with Heywood), with the original quarto or octavo text and an annotated modern-spelling text side by side, essays, a glossary, stage histories and recorded workshop performances. Published 2010 (AHRC-funded); no later update seen. Copyright is held by Royal Holloway. The counts cover the original-spelling text, not the modernised version.

derived.sort_title: rimay janos ifjukori versgyujtemenye (network critical edition, gepeskonyv)
derived.notes_display: Network critical edition (demo 1999, full version 2001-2004) of the early poems of the Hungarian poet János Rimay, edited by Tünde Tóth. The site gives the critical text of the poems (30 poem pages), a repertory of first lines, and the sources: the Fanchali Jób codex (1596-1608), the Balassa codex (after 1656) and further 16th-17th-century manuscripts and prints, which can be compared with the edition. The pages show a last-modified date of 2006 and no later activity, so the resource is listed as archived. The text opens in nested frames. The counts cover the 30 critical-text pages only, not the source transcriptions of each witness.

derived.sort_title: conde — faire vivre six siecles de coutumiers normands (corpus numerique des editions de la coutume de normandie)
derived.notes_display: The ConDE project (RIN = Réseau d'Intérêt Normand funding scheme; the TEI corpus itself is released on GitHub at github.com/RIN-ConDE/editions, which is why the Renascor Corpus collection carries the 'RIN-ConDE' name) transcribes and TEI-encodes successive editions of the Coutume de Normandie and its commentaries (Le Rouillé 1539, Terrien 1578, Bérault 1614, Basnage 1678...). The project site is hosted by the MRSH / Pôle Document Numérique in Caen with a blog at conde.hypotheses.org; corpus cited as 'corpus ConDE, Caen, CRISCO EA4255'.

derived.sort_title: kikongo sermon attributed to manuel roboredo, c. 1649 (ed. j. thornton)
derived.notes_display: Kikongo sermon of about 1649 attributed to Manuel Roboredo (Francisco de São Salvador), from a manuscript in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Rome, edited on John Thornton's African Texts pages.

derived.sort_title: ropsalt romanian
derived.notes_display: Verse-aligned XML corpus of the sixteenth-century Romanian Psalters, produced by the roPSALT project (4 January 2021 to 31 December 2023), 'Re-evaluating the Sixteenth Century Romanian Psalters', hosted by the Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi and funded by UEFISCDI (PN-III-P4-ID-PCE-2020-2939). Each psalm (1 to 151) is one XML file that sets the Romanian witnesses (the Hurmuzaki, Scheian, Voronet and Ciobanu manuscripts and Coresi's printed psalters) beside the Church Slavonic and Latin (Vulgate and other) variants, with Cyrillic passages marked by language. The project is led by Ana-Maria Ginsac; Alex Moruz, a team member, uploaded the files to GitHub in December 2023, with a stylesheet and an XSD schema for viewing them in a browser. The repository has had no change since that upload.

derived.sort_title: rostocker matrikelportal: database edition of the matriculation of students at the university of rostock
derived.notes_display: Searchable entries of the Rostock matriculation books, each with the date, name, origin, status and the editor's notes, with page images of the Hofmeister edition and of the original book. The database for 1419-1831 holds about 51,000 entries and is based on Adolf Hofmeister's printed edition (1899-1922). Records are short, structured entries rather than running text, and the portal also covers 1831 to today (names after 1945 are masked). The portal answers on http only. The counts treat each matriculation entry as a text, but the entries are short name entries (forename, surname, origin), not running text.

derived.sort_title: rostocker urgichten des 16. jahrhunderts in fallen von zauberei und hexerei. digitale methoden und lehrkonzepte auf der testbank
derived.notes_display: Confessions from magic, sorcery and witchcraft trials before the lower court of the city of Rostock, from the Stadtarchiv Rostock. Each of the 50 items (a person's confession, dated 1543-1596; 20 of them from 1584 and 7 from 1586) is published with the scan (PDF), a TEI-XML transcription and an RTF version; a separate file gives the transcription rules (based on the DTA basic format). Deposited in 2019; no later additions were found. The counts cover all 50 TEI transcriptions, downloaded once in a browser because the file downloads are protected against automated access.

derived.sort_title: royal society corpus 6.0 open - philosophical transactions (1665-1700)
derived.notes_display: The Royal Society Corpus 6.0 Open, built at Saarland University from the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London (texts from JSTOR and the Royal Society); the full corpus covers 1665-1920 and this entry covers the texts up to 1700. Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

derived.sort_title: rubens-online: quellen und dokumente zu leben, werk und literarischen bezugen des malers peter paul rubens (1577-1640)
derived.notes_display: Edition of documents on Rubens: 307 archival records and letters (1564-1682: notarial and city-court acts, payments, Rubens's will), 30 contemporary biographies, poems and mentions up to 1700, and 8 longer printed works (Peacham 1627; de Piles 1677, 1681 and 1699; Asterius 1615; Baudius, Epistolae 1636; Philip Rubens 1608). The TEI files are listed in mets.xml (served one by one; the data_url is the index of the files). Files date from 2011; the index was last changed in April 2016. The counts leave out the works dated after 1700 (Houbraken 1718, Dubos 1719, de Piles 1708 and 1766, Orlandi 1733) and the six volumes of the Codex diplomaticus Rubenianus, a nineteenth-century edition of Rubens's letters.

derived.sort_title: rup — rare or unique poems from manuscripts, 1500-1660 (rup)
derived.notes_display: RUP is an early-stage collaborative project (project blog at rup.hypotheses.org) publishing TEI encodings of rare or unique early modern English manuscript poems (<= 3 manuscript copies, never printed), begun during Jessica Edmondes' fellowship at the Folger Shakespeare Library; the source is the project's experimental TEI repo, whose file naming follows Folger LUNA image ids of the form 'rup_000001_va103_1_002v'. No custom ODD and no stated licence.

derived.sort_title: middle russian (old east slavic) treebank sample from the russian national corpus (ud_old_east_slavic-rnc)
derived.notes_display: Thirteen Middle Russian texts (documents, letters, chronicle passages and charms, c. 1300-1700) from the UD_Old_East_Slavic-RNC treebank, a sample of the Middle Russian Corpus of the Russian National Corpus. The RNC site itself offers no download of its Middle Russian corpus.

derived.sort_title: sobornoe ulozhenie 1649 goda (russian wikisource transcription)
derived.notes_display: The single text is a transcription on Russian Wikisource of the 1649 Sobornoe ulozhenie (Muscovite law code, Introduction and 25 chapters). It follows the Polnoe sobranie zakonov Rossiiskoi imperii, Sobranie pervoe, vol. I (St Petersburg, 1830), proofread page by page on Russian Wikisource; the text is public domain (RusGov licence template). No scholarly project stands behind it; it is a community wiki transcription rather than a TEI project.

derived.sort_title: school of salamanca: digital collection of sources (tei)
derived.notes_display: TEI XML files of full-text editions of 16th- and early 17th-century legal, theological and economic works by authors of the School of Salamanca and of reference works they used, from the project 'The School of Salamanca: a digital collection of sources and a dictionary of its juridical-political language'. The GitHub repository holds 18 works (Azpilcueta, Banez, Mercado, Soto, Vitoria, Las Casas, Solorzano Pereira, Sepulveda and others, in Latin and Spanish), generally from the first printed edition; the digitised editions are dated 2018 to 2021. The project is a cooperation of the Academy of Sciences and Literature | Mainz, the Max Planck Institute for Legal History and Legal Theory and Goethe University Frankfurt, with the team based in Frankfurt. Files are released under CC BY 4.0 and are forwarded automatically to Zenodo; the full texts are also searchable and downloadable (PDF and other formats) on salamanca.school. The repository was last updated in October 2024.

derived.sort_title: joachim von sandrart: teutsche academie der bau-, bild- und mahlerey-kunste, nurnberg 1675/1679/1680 (sandrart.net)
derived.notes_display: Online edition of Sandrart's art-historical encyclopaedia and the Iconologia Deorum (published 1675, 1679 and 1680): complete transcription, page images, indexes of persons, places, artworks and bibliography, and commentary. The TEI P5 file can be downloaded in three variants. The project ran 2008-2012; the TEI archive is dated July 2013 and no later change was found. The three printed parts are counted as three texts.

derived.sort_title: madeleine et georges de scudery: artamene ou le grand cyrus
derived.notes_display: Complete text of the novel in diplomatic reproduction (edition of Paris, Courbé, 1656), divided into sequences and episodes with summaries, pop-up notes on characters and places, and the engravings of the 1654 edition. Each of the ten parts can be downloaded as a PDF (https://artamene.othone.org/pdfs/cyrus1.pdf to cyrus10.pdf); the site also gives a full-text search through the ARTFL PhiloLogic server and offers TEI files (TEI P4, one per part plus a complete cyrus.xml) in the Othone project's GitHub repository (github.com/cschuwey/othone, folder artamene). The PDFs were last modified on 6 March 2024.

derived.sort_title: sefaria
derived.notes_display: Official bulk exports provide JSON and TXT downloads; the developer documentation describes the REST API.

derived.sort_title: selbstzeugnisse der fruhen neuzeit in der herzog august bibliothek: diarium herzog augusts des jungeren and tagebucher ludwig rudolphs und christine luises
derived.notes_display: Portal of the HAB with a register of manuscript self-testimonies in the library, the edition of the diary (Ephemerides sive Diarium) of Duke August the Younger of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel for 1594-1635 (1,656 dated entries), the edition of four diaries of Duke Ludwig Rudolph and Duchess Christine Luise (1698-1724) and, since 2022, the 'Grand Tour digital' project (separate entry in the catalogue). TEI P5 files are available for download (the diary as one XML file, the 1698-1724 diaries as sz2.zip, both in the HAB GitLab). The data are under CC BY-SA 4.0 unless stated otherwise. The counts cover the 1594-1635 diary of August the Younger and Christine Luise's diary of 1698/99, since the diaries of Ludwig Rudolph (1701 to 1724) fall after the period.

derived.sort_title: senie latvian
derived.notes_display: The Corpus of Early Written Latvian (SENIE) gives access to texts and facsimiles of written Latvian of the 16th to 18th centuries (102 sources in the 2025 release, including catechisms, postils, Gospels and Epistles, psalters, hymnals, dictionaries and Bible books). It is run by the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory of the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Latvia (AiLab IMCS UL), with the Latvian Language Institute of the Faculty of Humanities, University of Latvia; the site opened in 2003 and was converted to Unicode in 2017. The site (updated 2026-10-08) is a library of full source texts and facsimiles, and the corpus is also searchable in the National Corpora Collection (korpuss.lv). The CLARIN.LV repository item (issued 2025-11-27) offers TEI XML (hyphenated and unhyphenated) and plain-text DSL downloads, with state research programmes and the Language Technology Initiative named as funders.

derived.sort_title: sermo - corpus de sermons protestants 1550-1750
derived.notes_display: SERMO is an SNSF project (2015-2018) at Neuchâtel that produced a corpus of 62 French Protestant sermons (about 600,000 tokens, mostly printed in Geneva, 1555-1750). The complete TEI texts are on the project site (served over http only); the Zenodo deposit (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14620210, CC BY 4.0) is only a partial copy. The annotation (lemmas, parts of speech) is available only through the project's CQPweb interface, which needs a login.

derived.sort_title: johannes serranus' dictionarium latinogermanicum (nuremberg, 1538)
derived.notes_display: Transcription of the 428-page Latin-German dictionary printed by Johann Petreius in Nuremberg in 1538 (copy: HAB, P 1084.8° Helmst.), in 23 TEI files (front matter, letters A-Z, back matter) linked to the facsimile. Published in 2015; no later change was found. The dictionary is counted as one text.

derived.sort_title: complete works of william shakespeare (mit)
derived.notes_display: Online since 1993. HTML pages for the 37 plays, the Sonnets, Venus and Adonis, The Rape of Lucrece, A Lover's Complaint and A Funeral Elegy. All of it dates from 1450-1700. The text comes from the Moby Shakespeare, a modernised-spelling text, not a transcription of the early prints. HTML public domain according to the site. Status: the home page says 'Current copy taken from GitHub and hosted by MIT IS&T in a static location' (5/10/23) and the repository's last push is 2023-09-19; nothing newer was found. The counts cover the GitHub repository's plays, sonnets and poems, including The Passionate Pilgrim and The Phoenix and the Turtle from its plain-text poetry file.

derived.sort_title: saggi musicali italiani (smi)
derived.notes_display: Saggi musicali italiani (SMI) is an archive of Italian-language texts on music theory and aesthetics, modelled on the Thesaurus Musicarum Latinarum, with transcriptions and page graphics for treatises from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century. The sixteenth- and early seventeenth-century part includes Pietro Aaron, Zarlino, Bocchi, Bottrigari (printed and manuscript), Artusi, Bonini, Doni and Cerreto. Texts are transcribed in plain ASCII, following the source's spelling except for expanded abbreviations, spaced apostrophes and normalised accents. The project was started in 1998 at Indiana University by Andreas Giger (director until 2018) at the Center for the History of Music Theory and Literature (CHMTL), Jacobs School of Music; Giuliano Di Bacco has directed it since 2019, when redevelopment into a wider archive of vernacular music-theory texts began. The search utility was shut down after a cyberattack in 2015 and restored in 2017; in 2026 the original address redirects to a CHMTL page saying the digital thesauri are unavailable after a university-wide outage and are being moved to a new server.

derived.sort_title: corpus de sonetos del siglo de oro (adso)
derived.notes_display: The well-known metrical corpus of 5,078 Spanish Golden Age sonnets (matching the catalogue count) in TEI XML with metrical pattern annotation, edited by Borja Navarro-Colorado (Univ. Alicante) from texts of the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes; part of the ADSO project. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0 for the annotations (BVMC terms for the texts); a searchable interface exists at BVMC.Labs (data.cervantesvirtual.com/goldenage). The 'Sonetos del Siglo de Oro' label in the harvest refers to this corpus (texts stem from Ramón García González-type BVMC anthologies).

derived.sort_title: die sozinianischen briefwechsel: zwischen theologie, fruhmoderner naturwissenschaft und politischer korrespondenz
derived.notes_display: Letters of and to Socinian (anti-Trinitarian) scholars, including Fausto and Lelio Sozzini, Martin Ruar, Stanislaw Lubieniecki and Samuel Crell; the site holds 2,205 dated letters from 1545 to 1744 and 2,159 of them are dated 1700 or earlier. Each letter has one or more text versions (printed edition, copy, final copy, draft or autograph manuscript). The letters are published as TEI P5 XML files (one teiCorpus per letter with its attachments and witnesses, with standOff registers) in the project's GitLab data repository; the website itself serves the text through a public GraphQL service with standoff markup, and our counts were harvested from that service. The site was last deployed on 15 January 2026. The counts are per text version, so a letter with several versions is counted more than once, and letters without a transcription or a date are not included.

derived.sort_title: korpus polszczyzny xvi wieku (słownik polszczyzny xvi wieku)
derived.notes_display: Corpus of sixteenth-century Polish texts built for the Slownik polszczyzny XVI wieku (Dictionary of 16th-century Polish): about 198 texts of the dictionary's source canon (works such as Rej, Kochanowski, Bielski, Gornicki and Orzechowski, plus letters and documents), shown as transliterated text that keeps almost all features of the original.
