The corpus was prepared in 2012-2017 under National Programme for the Development of the Humanities project no. 0138/FNiTP/H11/80/2011, in TEI P5, as the first stage of a planned fuller corpus; part of the texts were tagged on a trial basis. It is published by the Pracownia Slownika Polszczyzny XVI wieku (Torun) of the Institute of Literary Research of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IBL PAN). Texts are read page by page on the site as HTML with numbered lines; no download of the TEI files was found, and the site was still maintained in 2026.

derived.sort_title: ssrq online — sammlung schweizerischer rechtsquellen / collection des sources du droit suisse
derived.notes_display: SSRQ is Switzerland's critical edition series of medieval/early modern legal sources, published in XML/TEI online since 2019 (Omeka S) and now also on the new 'editio' platform; the harvested origins are Zurich volumes of the Neue Folge (e.g. 'SSRQ ZH_NF_I_2_1 (1452-1637, 222 docs)', 'SSRQ ZH_NF_II_11 (1458-1696, 124 docs)'). The old domain ssrq-sdsr.ch has been renamed to ssrq-sds-fds.ch (the .sdsr URLs no longer resolve); TEI data is published on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10878757) and by the GitHub org SSRQ-SDS-FDS.

derived.sort_title: briefverkehr der stadt st. gallen 1400-1650: digitale missivenedition
derived.notes_display: Full text and images of incoming letters (Missiven) to the imperial city of St. Gall, published in stages. The site lists 760 dated letters (1417-1651, 228,746 words); 218 are before 1450. The TEI of each letter is served at /api/document/<id> (for example stasg_missiv_00300). The letter list is at the data link. Status active: the site presents a 'Missive des Monats' every first Friday of the month.

derived.sort_title: stationers' register online
derived.notes_display: Database of the copy-entries (permissions to print) recorded in the Stationers' Company Register, 1554-1640, from Arber's transcript corrected against the Register's images, with original spelling, cancelled text, marginalia and Arber's notes, and indexes of stationers and titles. The full TEI XML is delivered by the site's /api/allEntries service (10,453 entries). The sibling series by Eyre and Rivington (1640-1708) is described by the project but was not found in the data. The site works as of October 2026; the web application dates from about 2018 and no dated update was found, so the status 'active' is a cautious reading. Most entries (9,792) carry no date of their own, so their year is carried forward from the preceding entry and is approximate.

derived.sort_title: statutes of the realm
derived.notes_display: Three volumes (5 to 7, covering 1625 to 1701) of the Statutes of the Realm, the authoritative collection of Acts of the Parliament of England, in British History Online. The volumes are the printed edition by John Raithby (1819-1820), from Charles I and Charles II to the Bill of Rights, the Triennial Act, the Civil List Act and the Act of Settlement under William III, with each act as a page and the tables and prefaces. British History Online is a not-for-profit digital library at the Institute of Historical Research, University of London (editor John Levin), run with the History of Parliament Trust. The text was digitised by double rekeying and is offered as HTML pages; no bulk download was found. The site footer shows version 6.0 (2024).

derived.sort_title: lo statuto di paganico: statuti della comunita (secolo xv)
derived.notes_display: Edition of a single statute book, the only known copy, with an introduction, historical and codicological chapters, an index of rubrics and the full text of the rubrics (page 'Edizione'). The original site (www.gol.grosseto.it) no longer answers; the link points to the Internet Archive capture of 17 February 2005, which loads fully. Statutes were approved by Siena in 1487, 1489 and 1490. The counts cover the full statute text of the archived copy, not the introduction or the historical and codicological chapters.

derived.sort_title: suriano correspondence
svea-pommern: maps and texts of the swedish land survey of pomerania north of the peene (1692-1709)
derived.notes_display: Edition of the Swedish land survey (Landesaufnahme) of Pomerania north of the river Peene, the first cadastre of its kind in Germany: descriptions of villages and estates in older Swedish, with a transcription (HTML only) and a German translation (HTML and TEI P5 XML) for each of 255 places; the TEI files cover the German translations only, not the Swedish transcriptions that we count, a web map and indexes. The main survey is dated 1692-1698 (our check: 1694, 1696 and 1697 are the usual dates); a revision of 1704-1709 is transcribed in the same pages, so part of each text falls after 1700. Most pages give both the original fair copy and the draft. The project is described as finished and the site was last edited on 3 March 2025. The Greifswald and Rostock copyright notice allows research, teaching and private use. The counts cover the transcription pages, and because the revision of 1704-1709 sits in the same pages, part of the words fall after 1700.

derived.sort_title: doctrina christiana (manila, 1593): tagalog prayers
derived.notes_display: Tagalog prayers (12 texts) from the 1593 Manila Doctrina Christiana, in Project Gutenberg eBook #16119, a facsimile edition by Edwin Wolf, produced by Jeroen Hellingman, Tamiko I. Camacho and Distributed Proofreaders. The eBook is in English, Spanish and Tagalog; only the Tagalog texts are counted.

derived.sort_title: digitale edition und kommentierung der tagebucher des fursten christian ii. von anhalt-bernburg (1599-1656)
derived.notes_display: Annotated edition of the diaries Prince Christian II wrote between 1621 and 1656 (about 17,000 manuscript pages, all done), with facsimiles, translations of foreign passages, comments, indexes and a project website (www.tagebuch-christian-ii-anhalt.de). One TEI XML file per month is served on the HAB server. The 338 monthly files hold 10,086 diary entries. Each monthly file is counted as one text.

derived.sort_title: repositorio de teatro breve del siglo de oro (tbso)
derived.notes_display: Personal research repository of short Golden Age plays (entremeses) by David Merino Recalde, as plain text and XML-TEI, based on printed editions such as Cotarelo y Mori (1911). The collection is not closed and only some texts have TEI. Released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

derived.sort_title: testaments of culhuacan (s. l. cline & m. leon-portilla)
derived.notes_display: Nahuatl testaments from Culhuacan with English translation, from the 1984 edition, made available as a PDF by the UCSB Department of History.

derived.sort_title: textgrid repository
derived.notes_display: A digital repository for the humanities offering TEI-encoded texts, images, and structured data. Includes many scholarly editions of German literature. Free registration for some features; texts are openly licensed. The counts cover works from the Digitale Bibliothek and a few other projects, dated by the author's active span, so dates are approximate and works straddling 1450 or 1700 are left out.

derived.sort_title: latin library
derived.notes_display: Online collection of Latin texts from antiquity to the modern period, kept by a single webmaster (contact latinlibrary@mac.com) as plain HTML pages, with no translations, morphological help or apparatus. The Neo-Latin section lists about 60 authors and works (for example Erasmus, Melanchthon, Buchanan, Kepler, Galileo, Newton, Milton, Spinoza, Pontano, Sannazaro and Vida), only part of it dated 1450-1700. Texts were scanned from public-domain editions, taken from other websites or submitted by contributors; a Credits page names the edition and submitter where known, and many are from unidentified editions. The site says the texts are not meant for research or as substitutes for critical editions and may contain scanner errors. The Neo-Latin index page was last changed in January 2022 and the home page in August 2025.

derived.sort_title: theatre classique
derived.notes_display: The two texts in the catalogue statistics were taken from the dramacode/tcp5 GitHub conversion of the Théâtre classique XML sources (https://github.com/dramacode/tcp5, TEI P5); one of them (Dorimond, Le Festin de Pierre) is credited in its header to Molière 21 / Université Paris-Sorbonne (Marc Douguet, 2016) rather than to the site.

derived.sort_title: ticha zapotec
derived.notes_display: Ticha is a digital text explorer for Colonial Valley Zapotec, with images of the original documents, transcriptions, English and modern Spanish translations, morphological interlinear glossing and commentary, on a corpus of manuscripts (mainly 17th- and 18th-century testaments and legal documents from Oaxaca archives) and printed works such as Cordova's Arte (1578), Feria's Doctrina and Levanto's Arte and Cathecismo. At the time of checking, 31 of 204 listed manuscripts had transcriptions. The project was led by Brook Danielle Lillehaugen (Haverford College) with George Aaron Broadwell (University of Florida), Michel R. Oudijk (UNAM), Laurie Allen, May Plumb and Mike Zarafonetis, supported by ACLS, NEH, the American Philosophical Society and Haverford College; the first edition dates from 2016. TEI versions of the texts are in the project's GitHub repository (HCDigitalScholarship/ticha-xml-tei); the news page has no entry after September 2021.

derived.sort_title: johannes tinctoris: complete theoretical works (early music theory)
derived.notes_display: New critical edition of the Latin treatises of Johannes Tinctoris (c. 1435-1511) with full English translations and commentary, based on three principal manuscripts (Valencia 835, Bologna 2573, Brussels II 4147). Eleven treatises are online as edited text (with variant readings and music examples); Expositio manus, De natura et proprietate tonorum and the Diffinitorium musice are still listed as placeholders. The site describes itself as in its initial stages of development. Everything is dated 1470s-1480s. The home page says it was last updated on 17 December 2020 and the treatise pages date from 2015; the whole site was re-uploaded to its server in July 2026 (all files carry the same date), so it is listed as active but the content has not changed since 2020. The counts cover the 11 treatises online, which are not dated individually (the site dates all to the 1470s-1480s).

derived.sort_title: titus (thesaurus indogermanischer text- und sprachmaterialien)
derived.notes_display: TITUS is the Frankfurt Thesaurus of Indo-European Text and Language Materials; the selection here covers Albanian, Georgian, Lithuanian and Old Prussian texts of 1545–1700. Most are published as HTML pages; only the Old Lithuanian texts of the SLIEKKAS sub-project (linked as the data page) are available as XML, with Toolbox and ELAN files.

derived.sort_title: thesaurus musicarum italicarum (tmiweb) and saggi musicali italiani
derived.notes_display: Texts of the Thesaurus Musicarum Italicarum (TmiWeb, Utrecht University), an electronic corpus of Italian music treatises from the Renaissance and early Baroque, together with the Saggi Musicali Italiani (SMI) texts. The original SMI site at Indiana University is no longer available; those texts were retrieved from the Internet Archive. A TEI P5 deposit exists at DANS (doi:10.17026/dans-zum-ywbw) but its files are restricted.

derived.sort_title: tmk
derived.notes_display: Corpus of private letters and witness testimonies from trial records in Old and Middle Hungarian (before 1772), in roughly equal parts. The texts are normalised, morphologically annotated and given sociolinguistic metadata, and are searched through an online query interface with lexical maps. They are taken from printed source editions (e.g. Schram's Magyarországi boszorkányperek, the Kolozsvár witch trials, the Nádasdy, Zrínyi and Batthyány letters), listed on the site's source page. Made by Attila Novák, Katalin Gugán, Mónika Varga and Adrienne Dömötör (Research Institute for Linguistics, Budapest) with OTKA K 81189 and NKFI-OTKA K 116217 funding; it belongs to the Hungarian National Corpus Portal. The latest size statement on the site dates from September 2020, when the material was said to be still growing.

derived.sort_title: thesaurus musicarum latinarum revivificatus (tmlr) - adaptation of the tml
derived.notes_display: Thesaurus Musicarum Latinarum Revivificatus (TMLr) is a static-site rebuild of the Thesaurus Musicarum Latinarum, the collection of Latin music-theory treatises from late antiquity to the seventeenth century begun in 1990 under Thomas Mathiesen at the Center for the History of Music Theory and Literature, Indiana University. The adaptation is by Caleb Mutch; its GitHub repository was created in January 2026 and last updated in February 2026. Texts are HTML pages that can be browsed by century, incipit, source and title and searched, with concordances to Grove and other lists. Only public-domain material is reproduced: copyrighted items of the original TML are left out and linked externally where possible.

derived.sort_title: renard — renaissance aristophanes digital (translatoscope / elan)
derived.notes_display: RenArD is the Renaissance branch of the Translatoscope project (ELAN, Litt&Arts Grenoble), offering the first XML-TEI editions of the Latin humanist translations of Aristophanes — Ploutos and Les Nuees (Clouds) translated by Alessandro da Otranto (1470), Johannes Cuno, Beatus Rhenanus, Lorenzo Giacomini etc. — presented alongside the manuscript facsimile via EVT. The harvested origins ('Translatoscope: Les Nuees / Alessandro da Otranto (1470)', 'Translatoscope: Ploutos / Beatus Rhenanus (1520)') map directly onto these translations; TEI data is deposited on Nakala.

derived.sort_title: tychobrahe portuguese
corpus de documentos coloniales (cdc) de merida, venezuela — documentos para la historia linguistica de merida (siglos xvi-xvii)
derived.notes_display: 37 public and private documents (testaments, powers of attorney, sales, dowries, petitions) transcribed literally (Proyecto Histórico del Español de América / ALFAL norms), published in 2002 (ISBN 980-11-0652-2), each as a separate PDF with text layer. All documents date from 1564-1657. Probably related to the CDHM documents of the same group in the CHARTA corpus. The page shows no update since 2002.

derived.sort_title: documentos privados antiguos (1600-1900), universidad de navarra
derived.notes_display: Despite the page title (1600-1900), the oldest document is dated 1550. Documents are 105 PDFs (notarial documents and letters), each with metadata, TRANSCRIPCIÓN PALEOGRÁFICA, PRESENTACIÓN CRÍTICA and facsimile; text layer present (pdftotext). The collection has 105 documents dated 1550-1900. Mostly Spanish, some Basque. PDFs only, no machine-readable XML.

derived.sort_title: urfehdebucher der stadt basel – digitale edition (urfehdebuch x, 1563-1569)
derived.notes_display: Digital edition (beta) of one volume of the oaths of truce (Urfehden) sworn before the Basel council: Staatsarchiv Basel-Stadt, Ratsbücher O 10, Urfehdebuch X, January 1563 to December 1569. The site does not cover the other Urfehdebücher. The volume has 626 entries, all within the period. The record page shows 'zuletzt verändert am 31.1.2017' (last changed 31 January 2017) and the project belongs to a 2016 teaching exercise, so it is listed as archived. Page images are hosted externally by the Staatsarchiv Basel-Stadt.

derived.sort_title: vakk estonian
derived.notes_display: Corpus of Old Written Estonian (VAKK) of the University of Tartu, with texts from the 15th to the 19th century. It holds all known surviving Estonian texts of the 15th and 16th centuries (manuscripts and prints, name lists excepted), most surviving 17th-century prints and known manuscript sermons, and a selection of 18th- and 19th-century prints; it also hosts 19th-century parish court protocols. Older texts are lemmatised and morphologically tagged, partly by hand and partly with Külli Prillop's Vakker software, and the corpus is searched and filtered online, with CSV or Excel export of results. The work began in 1995 in the Old Written Language research group of the Chair of Estonian (led by Valve-Liivi Kingisepp) and is funded by Estonian national programmes; the corpus has a DOI and is listed in META-SHARE.

derived.sort_title: music theory of harald vallerius: three dissertations from 17th-century sweden (p. sjokvist)
derived.notes_display: Edition with translation and commentary of three Latin dissertations on music theory presided over by Harald Vallerius at Uppsala (1674, 1686, 1698), published open access by Uppsala University Press (PDF; also on OAPEN).

derived.sort_title: de ystroom: joannes antonides van der goes, ystroom (1671), online edition
derived.notes_display: Annotated edition of the Dutch epic poem Ystroom, on the Amsterdam first edition of 1671, with a diplomatic transcription, a modern Dutch translation, three earlier editors' notes and facsimiles. Readable without login. The reading interface (Elaborate) is fed by JSON files, listed in config.json (177 entries). The edition's publication date in its data is 2015-10-28 and the newest site file is dated 2023-09-12, so it is marked archived. The poem is counted as one text.

derived.sort_title: vasto: benedetto varchi, storia fiorentina (genetic and annotated digital edition)
derived.notes_display: Digital genetic and annotated edition (EVT2) of Varchi's unfinished Storia fiorentina, left incomplete at his death in 1565 and printed only in 1721 in a censored form. The site offers diplomatic and critical views with facsimile. Only the Proemio is published so far: the TEI file pilot_proemio.xml in the project's GitHub repository holds it; the whole work is not online. Status archived: the repository's last commit is 13 June 2021 and the site has had no update since. The licence is the Creative Commons BY-NC-ND 3.0 link shown on the home page.

derived.sort_title: venetian inscriptions in cyprus (la lettera e il leone)
derived.notes_display: Open access platform of Latin Renaissance inscriptions from Venetian-ruled Cyprus (1474-1571) with interpreted and diplomatic transcriptions, English and Italian translations, apparatus and photos; no login needed (the LogIn link is for editors). 27 inscriptions in total on 17 sites: 24 are dated within or overlapping 1450-1700 (15 with numeric years, 9 with approximate dates such as 'end of the 15th century'), 1 is Janus I's epitaph of 1432, 2 are illegible fragments with 'Uncertain' dates. No bulk download or TEI export found. Pages modified as late as September 2024. Related: the Titulus/ERC GRAPH-EAST corpus covers Cyprus (575 texts) but is not yet published online. Verbal dates such as 'end of the 15th century' are converted to approximate years, so the share within 1450-1700 is approximate.

derived.sort_title: verse miscellanies online
derived.notes_display: Critical edition of seven printed verse miscellanies: Tottel's Miscellany (1557), A Handful of Pleasant Delights (1566), The Paradise of Dainty Devices (1576 and later), The Gorgeous Gallery of Gallant Inventions (1578), The Phoenix Nest (1593), England's Helicon (1600, 1614) and The Poetical Rhapsody. Everything dates from 1450-1700 (all the texts are sixteenth- or early seventeenth-century prints); the annotations and indexes are modern. Texts come from the EEBO-TCP transcriptions (original spelling), with added notes. The Bodleian withdrew the live site (holding page: 'no longer available ... technologies ... reached end-of-life'); the url points to the Wayback Machine copy of 2025-07-30, which the Bodleian itself names as the archived static version. No data download found. The counts cover the leaf pages captured by the Wayback Machine (1,099 of 1,108).

derived.sort_title: vespasiano da bisticci, lettere. a digital edition (knowledge site)
derived.notes_display: Digital edition (Knowledge Site 3.0, 2020) of the letters of Vespasiano da Bisticci (Florentine book dealer, 1444-1497), a semantic/RDF-based faceted edition with philological apparatus (nota filologica, authorities, tavola sinottica), built at /DH.arc Bologna. The harvested origin 'Vespasiano da Bisticci, Letters (15th c.)' with source '(DHARC, digital edition)' refers to this site; the edition is stable but no longer actively developed. Site code CC BY 4.0 on GitHub (dharc-org/vespasiano-da-bisticci-letters-de).

derived.sort_title: phep giang tam ngay (cathechismus) — alexandre de rhodes, rome 1651
derived.notes_display: The Vietnamese Wikisource page 'Phép giảng tám ngày' (Latin title page 'Cathechismvs ... in octo dies divisus') is a page-by-page transcription of Alexandre de Rhodes's catechism, printed in Rome in 1651 by the Congregation de Propaganda Fide; it is the first printed prose work in chữ Quốc ngữ script, and public domain. Most of the 330 pages are still marked as not yet proofread (only 3 are proofread); the text was bot-imported in 2018 and partly edited in 2022, and is usable transcribed text rather than raw OCR.

derived.sort_title: vks oldliteraryfinnish
derived.notes_display: Corpus of Old Literary Finnish (Vanhan kirjasuomen korpus, VKS) of Kotus, the Institute for the Languages of Finland, distributed through the Language Bank of Finland (Kielipankki) and its Korp search interface. It holds written Finnish texts from 1543 to 1810, among them Bible translations and religious texts (all of Mikael Agricola's Finnish works), legal texts, poems and texts on agriculture, nature and health. It was compiled for lexicographic use and is browsable and searchable on the web; the resource is listed as publicly available. The Kielipankki page was last modified on 2025-11-26.

derived.sort_title: vokabular webovy
derived.notes_display: Vokabulář webový is the web portal of the Department of Language Development of the Institute of the Czech Language (Czech Academy of Sciences), online since November 2006, which gathers text, image and audio sources for historical Czech. It includes the Old Czech and Middle Czech text banks (with a KonText corpus search), critical editions, grammars, digitised dictionaries and secondary literature. Its operation is supported by the Ministry of Education project LINDAT/CLARIAH-CZ (LM2023062) and earlier national grants. The site shows a data version dated 2026-06-19. A TEI version of one of its editions, Lék jádro brněnské (Knihy lékařské, 1502-1503), is published on GitHub (CzechLanguageInstitute/tei2019).

derived.sort_title: wandering jew's chronicle
derived.notes_display: Quasi-diplomatic transcriptions with images of 15 copies of an English broadside ballad printed between 1634 and 1830, compared in a Versioning Machine interface, with bibliography and a textual history. The four copies printed before 1700 are A.2.a (Francis Grove, Charles I version), and C.1.a, C.2.a, C.3.a (Charles II versions, Coles/Vere/Wright and others). The other 11 copies are from the 18th and 19th centuries. Status archived: the site and the GitHub repository were last changed in December 2016. The counts cover those four copies, and the dates of the copies are approximate placeholders from the resource description.

derived.sort_title: wathay ferenc osszes muve (complete works of ferenc wathay)
derived.notes_display: Network critical edition of the songbook ('Enekes könyv') of Ferenc Wathay, written while he was held in the Black Tower at Constantinople: title page, preface and 28 songs in a letter-faithful transcription, with facsimile pages and an afterword. Status archived: pages date from 1999-2000 and the site's files show no change after September 2023.

derived.sort_title: die autobiographischen aufzeichnungen hermann weinsbergs – digitale gesamtausgabe
derived.notes_display: Transcription of the three books of the Cologne citizen Hermann Weinsberg (1518-1597): Liber Iuventutis, Liber Senectutis and Liber Decrepitudinis, in Cologne German with Latin passages, each served as a series of long HTML pages (8, 11 and 10 files) with marginal notes. Everything dates from 1518-1597, so all of it is in period. The pages use an old frameset layout; the site says some functions (editorial notes) no longer work and that a relaunch is being prepared. The home page shows 'Letzte Änderung: 09.04.2024'. A DFG project since 2002. The counts cover the three books without the author's marginal notes.

derived.sort_title: historical corpus of the welsh language, 1500-1850 (hcwl; corpws hanesyddol yr iaith gymraeg)
derived.notes_display: Historical Corpus of the Welsh Language 1500-1850: about 420,000 words of Welsh in TEI XML (30 texts, including the 1588 Welsh Bible), built at the University of Cambridge (Department of Linguistics, David Willis) from c. 2004. celticstudies.net is the corpus's official site (published from the GitHub repository dwew2/hcwl); a parsed derivative (PARSHCWL) is included in the repository. A LINDAT/CLARIAH-CZ record (LRT-883) exists but is metadata-only and points to the old Cambridge address. Site copyright 2004, University of Cambridge.

derived.sort_title: wikisource
derived.notes_display: Texts harvested from the language subdomains of Wikisource (de, es, it, ca, cs, el, sv, pl, hr, hu, pt, among others), the multilingual library of openly licensed digitised source texts; the entry points to the portal wikisource.org, whose per-language subdomains host each text. Several Renascor Corpus collections scope Renaissance-era texts and early Bibles specifically (e.g. Luther NT 1522, Gustav Vasa Bible 1541, Diodati 1607).

derived.sort_title: win — wiedererzahlen im norden. digitale analyse weltlicher erzahlungen in niederdeutschen inkunabeln (win-korpus v1.0)
derived.notes_display: The WiN project (Goettingen GCDH, funded by Niedersächsisches Vorab) built a parallel corpus of Early New High German short narratives and their Middle Low German versions from late 15th c. incunabula (Dracole, Griseldis, Juden, Graf, Kaufleute...), published as WiN-Korpus v1.0 (2022) in the LAUDATIO repository (HU Berlin), TEI-annotated, with the transcription handbook on DARIAH-DE; the project page is uni-goettingen.de/de/wiedererzählen+im+norden./607371.html.

derived.sort_title: winthrop papers digital edition (papers of the winthrop family)
derived.notes_display: Digitised volumes of the Winthrop Papers documentary edition (letters, diaries, memoranda, legal documents and John Winthrop's journal), with the editors' markup of uncertain readings, deletions and gaps. The documents are dated 1544-1644 (plus 1682), and the browse list also holds a few items dated outside the period (1265, 1274, 1927). Only volumes 1-4 are online. No licence is stated beyond the MHS copyright line (2026). Status active: the site carries a 2026 copyright notice.

derived.sort_title: postil time machine (postime) — digital edition of the old lithuanian postilles incl. the wolfenbuettel postille of 1573
derived.notes_display: PosTiMe (DFG, Frankfurt/Cologne, 2021+) produces the language-historically annotated TEI edition and reference corpus of the Old Lithuanian Lutheran postilles; its core object is the Wolfenbüttel Postille of 1573 (Cod. Guelf. 11.2 Aug. 2, Herzog August Bibliothek), the first Lithuanian collection of sermons. The Renascor Corpus text ('Wolfenbüttel Postil (1573), Old Lithuanian', source 'WP1573-TEI (postime, TITUS-derived)') is the WP1573-TEI layer derived from the earlier TITUS transcription associated with the Gelumbeckaite/HAB 1573 Postille edition project; the HAB project page describes the underlying critical edition.

derived.sort_title: wolne lektury
derived.notes_display: Wolne Lektury is a Polish online library of free e-books and audiobooks run by the Fundacja Wolne Lektury, aimed especially at schoolchildren and offering many set school readings. Works that are in the public domain or released under free licences are annotated (footnotes, literary motifs, links to Wikimedia) and offered in HTML, TXT, PDF, EPUB, MOBI and FB2; a public API and an OAI-PMH interface are provided. The library describes holdings of several thousand works (7332 on its about page) and over a thousand audiobooks, among them older Polish texts relevant to the 1450-1700 range. The site is active and publishes news in October 2026.

derived.sort_title: kunstlike werltsproke und eyn schon rimbokelin (wsrb): digital edition of 16th-century middle low german proverb collections
derived.notes_display: Transcriptions and facsimiles of the eight known editions of the 'Künstlike Werltspröke' (seven editions) and the 'Schön rimbökelin', printed in Lübeck and later Hamburg between about 1540 and 1601, and a critical edition of 849 sayings with search and filters. The DOI belongs to the data publication in the RosDok repository (all TEI files plus the software); the TEI of each transcription is also served at /wsrb/xml_raw/. A book edition appeared at the same time. The counts cover the eight transcriptions, not the critical edition of the sayings.

derived.sort_title: zlatyfond slovak
derived.notes_display: Zlatý fond denníka SME is a digitised collection of classics of Slovak literature, run by the publisher Petit Press (daily SME) in cooperation with the Institute of Slovak Literature of the Slovak Academy of Sciences. Founded by Tomáš Ulej and launched around December 2006, it relies on volunteer digitisers and gives priority to recent, linguistically modern editions; the oldest editions are digitised only rarely. The project is led by Viera Studeničová. The live site refused automated requests (firewall), so these facts come from an archived copy of January 2025.

derived.sort_title: zrinyi miklos: adriai tengernek syrenaja (parallel source edition of the syrena codex and the 1651 print)
derived.notes_display: Parallel edition (published 1998 in the Gépeskönyv series of the Old Hungarian Literature Department, ELTE) of Miklós Zrínyi's epic cycle 'Adriai tengernek syrénája': the text of the so-called Syrena manuscript beside the 1651 Vienna print (printed by Kosmerovi Máte), with the idylls, the 15 parts of the Obsidio Szigetiana, and the shorter poems. Both witnesses are old-spelling transcriptions in plain HTML pages. The site's files date from 2006 and show no later change, so it is listed as archived. The text opens in a frameset; the page at this address links to it.

derived.sort_title: huldrych zwingli briefe: digitale texte
derived.notes_display: Each letter is its own page (n=Brief.1 to Brief.790, 804 pages) with the running text of the critical edition Huldreich Zwinglis sämtliche Werke vol. 7-9 (Corpus Reformatorum 94-96, 1911-1925), without the apparatus; letters from 1510 to 1528. Letters 790-1292 (vols. 10-11, 1528-1531) are not online. Searchable by full text, sender, recipient and place. The wiki's change log shows the letters last edited in 2011 and the last change of any page on 1 July 2021, and the site still runs on old PHP, so it is listed as archived. The counts cover all 804 letter pages, fetched once in a browser because the site refuses automated clients.
